jobs.description:
Job Description
Senior Staff Frontend Engineer, Admin Experience
Zendesk is transforming the way businesses build meaningful customer relationships. Our products help organizations deliver exceptional customer and employee experiences at scale, and our Admin Experience is central to how customers configure, manage, and get value from the Zendesk platform.
We are looking for a Senior Staff Frontend Engineer to help bring Zendesk’s Admin Experience vision to life for an AI-first future. This is a high-impact technical leadership role for someone who combines deep frontend expertise with product thinking, system design, and strong cross-functional leadership.
In this role, you will strengthen and operationalize our vision by translating high-level concepts into technically sound, scalable, and actionable frontend strategies. You will work closely with Product, Design, and Engineering to reimagine complex user journeys and deliver intuitive, intelligent, and cohesive experiences for Zendesk admins.
What You’ll Do
Translate the Admin Experience vision into a clear end-to-end strategy focused on the frontend, architecture, roadmap, and execution plan.
Lead major initiatives across teams and product areas while remaining hands-on with writing code.
Partner with Product and Design to deliver intuitive, scalable, and cohesive experiences for Zendesk admins.
Establish reusable frontend patterns, components, and platform capabilities that improve consistency and accelerate delivery.
Identify technical risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs while balancing near-term priorities with long-term maintainability.
Advance performance, accessibility, reliability, testing, observability, and developer experience.
Build and maintain scalable, unified CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Spinnaker) for Admin Experience and Agent Workspace to improve delivery speed and reliability.
Drive developer productivity by optimizing build systems, testing infrastructure (PlayWright), and local development tooling.
Mentor engineers and raise the engineering bar through technical guidance, design reviews, and 1-1 coaching.
What You Bring to the Role
15+ years of software engineering experience, with deep expertise in frontend product development.
Proven success delivering complex, enterprise-scale UI initiatives.
Strong proficiency in Javascript or TypeScript, React, modern web standards, GraphQL, API integration, and frontend architecture.
Deep knowledge of frontend best practices, including accessibility, performance, testing, and reliability.
Ability to translate ambiguous product goals into pragmatic execution plans.
Experience leading cross-functional initiatives from discovery through to delivery
Ability to influence without direct authority, align teams, and communicate effectively with senior leaders.
Experience collaborating with globally distributed teams.
Nice to Have
Experience leading major transformations or redesigns of existing user experiences, particularly to make them AI-first.
Experience building enterprise SaaS products, configuration tools, or complex operational experiences.
Familiarity with AI interaction patterns, including agents, recommendations, automation, conversational interfaces, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
Please note that Zendesk can only hire candidates who are physically located and plan to work from Karnataka or Maharashtra. Please refer to the location posted on the requisition for where this role is based.
Hybrid: In this role, our hybrid experience is designed at the team level to give you a rich onsite experience packed with connection, collaboration, learning, and celebration - while also giving you flexibility to work remotely for part of the week. This role must attend our local office for part of the week. The specific in-office schedule is to be determined by the hiring manager.
The intelligent heart of customer experience
Zendesk software was built to bring a sense of calm to the chaotic world of customer service. Today we power billions of conversations with brands you know and love.
Zendesk believes in offering our people a fulfilling and inclusive experience. Our hybrid way of working, enables us to purposefully come together in person, at one of our many Zendesk offices around the world, to connect, collaborate and learn whilst also giving our people the flexibility to work remotely for part of the week.

Enterprise Account Executive - North & East India
Join us at Zendesk, where we're on a mission to power exceptional service for every person on the planet. We're accelerating our ambition by building products rooted in the belief that behind every interaction is an opportunity to make a human connection.
To achieve this, we're in search of a successful Enterprise Account Executive with a proven track record in B2B sales and a passion for driving growth within the SaaS space. Your focus will be on building relationships and introducing innovative solutions to new customers, in addition to growing our existing partnerships by continuing to expand our offerings and deepen Zendesk's impact.
What You'll Be Doing:
Directly drive top-line revenue growth by acquiring new Enterprise customers and developing strategies to penetrate top tier accounts.
Proactively identify and pursue opportunities to cross sell additional products and services to existing customers to optimize account revenue and profitability.
Manage and nurture key customer relationships to ensure maximum satisfaction and retention, fostering long-term strategic partnerships.
Leverage data insights, customer intents, and adoption history to effectively prospect new clients and enhance retention strategies, leading to improved conversion rates in new business pipeline and increased retention and expansion of existing clients.
Create quarterly territory plans, developing strategies and actionable tactics to increase our market share in the Enterprise sector.
Demonstrate a strong understanding of Zendesk products and align them with clients’ business objectives to secure product expansion and customer satisfaction.

Establish and maintain C-level executive sponsorship, leveraging your industry expertise to build relationships with decision-makers and champions.
Collaborate effectively with internal teams and leadership to optimize sales strategies and drive sales execution.
Negotiate and close complex deals, leveraging a consultative approach, utilizing your exceptional communication skills to present compelling business cases and value propositions.
Maintain thorough knowledge of Zendesk solutions, staying current with competitive landscape and industry trends.

BA/BS degree or equivalent experience required.
Experience in cloud/software B2B sales or solution engineering, with a minimum of 10 years of experience and a proven track record of exceeding sales targets.

Expertise in navigating complex sales cycles and renewals, including multi-month, value-centric processes with proof of concept stages.
A history of successfully selling to VP and C-level executives in Enterprise accounts.
Outstanding presentation, negotiation, and deal-closing abilities.
Experience creating and leveraging territory and account plans.
An entrepreneurial spirit, a collaborative mindset, and a drive for personal and professional growth.
Demonstrated industry experience, with the ability to navigate industry trends and dynamics and build relationships with key decision-makers and champions.
Familiarity with key Sales tools such as Salesforce, Outreach, Clari, Seismic and Looker.
Ability to travel to customer locations.

jobs.description:
Meet the Moment with Alteryx
We're living through a once-in-a-generation shift in how work gets done. Data, automation, and AI are quickly becoming the center of every business decision - and Alteryx is leading the transformation.
You'll be working on the challenges that sit at the heart of modern business. No matter your role, the work you do will help organizations move faster, see more clearly, and tackle questions that used to feel impossible.
If you're ready to meet the moment with innovation, curiosity, and excellence, there's a place for you here.
The Senior AI Data Engineer builds and operates trusted data capabilities that support enterprise analytics and AI. This role owns the reliability and continuous improvement of key AI-powered data products, including Data Concierge and AskInsights, while also developing and optimizing data pipelines and models using dbt, SQL, and Alteryx.
Working across Data Engineering, Data Science, Governance, and business-aligned data teams, this role turns emerging AI use cases and traditional data requirements into secure, scalable, and reusable enterprise capabilities.
Core Competencies:
Data Engineering: Design and build maintainable data pipelines, transformations, and data models using modern data-engineering practices.
Production Ownership: Proactively monitor, support, troubleshoot, and continuously improve business-critical data and AI products.
AI Systems Understanding: Understand how enterprise data, semantic context, data models, APIs, and application components come together to enable reliable AI-powered experiences.
Technical Problem-Solving: Diagnose complex data, performance, integration, and production issues and implement durable solutions.
Data Quality & Reliability: Build appropriate testing, monitoring, observability, and governance into data products.
Collaboration: Work effectively across technical and business teams while reinforcing shared engineering standards and ownership.
Key Responsibilities:
Own the ongoing support, maintenance, reliability, and enhancement of Data Concierge, AskInsights, and related AI-powered data products.
Build, test, deploy, and optimize data pipelines and transformations using dbt, SQL, Alteryx, and related technologies.
Design and develop governed, reusable data models and contextual data capabilities that support analytics, automation, and AI use cases.
Monitor data and application health, troubleshoot production issues, perform root-cause analysis, and improve reliability, performance, scalability, and cost efficiency.
Implement automated testing, data-quality controls, observability, documentation, and deployment practices across data products and pipelines.
Build and maintain integrations with enterprise platforms, APIs, data sources, and AI services as required.
Partner with Data Engineering, Data Science, Governance, Customer 0, and embedded Data Ops teams to deliver reusable enterprise data products.
Translate business and AI requirements into scalable technical solutions while maintaining appropriate governance and security standards.
Evaluate emerging AI and data-engineering technologies and capabilities and apply them where they provide practical enterprise value.
Contribute to engineering standards, reusable patterns, documentation, and best practices across the broader data organization.
Qualifications & Experience:
4–6 years of relevant professional experience in Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering, or a closely related technical role.
Strong hands-on experience building and supporting production-grade data pipelines, transformations, and data models.
Strong proficiency in SQL and practical experience working with modern data transformation frameworks such as dbt.
Experience with Alteryx or similar data preparation, analytics, or workflow automation platforms.
Experience designing and maintaining data solutions within cloud-based or modern enterprise data environments.
Good understanding of data modeling, data quality, testing, monitoring, observability, and production support.
Experience integrating data solutions with APIs, enterprise applications, and external services.
Understanding of software engineering practices such as version control, CI/CD, automated testing, and deployment processes.
Exposure to AI/ML, Generative AI, LLM-powered applications, semantic layers, or AI-enabled data products is highly desirable.
Ability to troubleshoot complex data and integration issues and drive them through to resolution.
Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work across engineering, data science, governance, and business teams.

If you meet some of the requirements and you share our values, we encourage you to apply. As part of our ongoing commitment to a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace, we’re invested in building teams with a wide variety of backgrounds, identities, and experiences.

Our Global Content team is looking for a talented technical writer who wants to create valuable content experiences for our audience. Our team writes content for Alteryx Documentation. Our site is available in 8 languages and has over 100,000 monthly users.
You'll fit right in if you are passionate about online technical communication and helping customers to find the answers they need. You will thrive if you believe that all customers should have a helpful, positive, and accessible experience, regardless of the language they choose and the technologies they use to navigate and consume our content.
What You Will Own and Improve
Authoring documentation: Write help articles, release notes, and examples that enable customers to use and configure Alteryx products.
Publishing documentation: We create our content in the Paligo CMS and publish it in AWS. You will own the process for generating the outputs (usually in HTML5), testing, and publishing them. You will also collaborate with the other tech writers to suggest improvements to the outputs and publishing process.
Contribute to our peer review and styles and standards processes: You will ask your fellow writers to review your work, and you will review their work. You will propose topics for styles and standards and participate in our discussions.
AI-assisted workflows: Use AI tools and agent-assisted workflows to improve efficiency, reduce repetitive work, and produce better first drafts. Contribute to the team's growing set of shared AI practices, including documentation agents that integrate with Jira, Confluence, and GitLab, and help refine them over time.
Cross-functional collaboration: Work with engineering, product, UX, localization, and support teams to ensure your content is accurate, timely, and accessible across languages and user contexts.
Requirements
· You have 2 or more years of experience in technical writing for software or SaaS products.
· You write clear, professional American English and can adapt your style for a global audience.
· You can translate complex technical details into clear, accessible documentation.
· You work well with multidisciplinary teams and are comfortable partnering with engineering, product, and UX.
· You plan and track your work using Jira and Confluence. You seek clarity, follow through on commitments, and communicate proactively.
· You have a bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) in a field relevant to this role.
Your Team
We are part of the Product organization. Our group reports to the VP of UX. You will be a member of the Technical Writing team, which reports to the manager of Global Content. Global Content includes two teams: Technical Writing and Content Design.
We have work flexible schedules. India team members collaborate with US-based colleagues across time zones, with team calls scheduled to accommodate distributed working hours.

About Yugabyte
At Yugabyte, we are on a mission to become the default transactional database for enterprises building cloud-native applications. YugabyteDB is our PostgreSQL compatible distributed database for cloud-native apps. Resilient, scalable, and flexible, it runs on any cloud and enables developers to become instantly productive using well-known APIs.We are looking for talented and driven people to join us on our ambitious mission and help us build a lasting and impactful company.The transactional database market is estimated to grow to $150B by 2030. YugabyteDB is cloud-native by design, has on-demand horizontal scalability, and supports geographical distribution of data using built-in replication. This means that we are well-positioned to meet market demand for geo-distributed, high-scale, high-performance workloads.
Yugabyte offers a culture of innovation, ownership, and technical excellence, with opportunities to impact a cutting-edge distributed SQL database used by global enterprises. As a member of the DST team, you’ll help meet growing demand for high-scale, high-performance, globally distributed transactional workloads — instrumental to our product’s success.
Role Overview
As a Staff Engineer on the Distributed Storage & Transactions (DST) team, you will play a critical role in designing, building, and scaling the core distributed storage, replication, and transaction foundations of YugabyteDB.
You will work on some of the most challenging problems in distributed systems — including consistency, durability, fault tolerance, performance, and scalability — while collaborating closely with query layer, platform, and cloud teams. This role is ideal for engineers who thrive in low-level systems work and want to shape the future of a globally distributed database.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the design, development, testing, and delivery of core storage and replication features in YugabyteDB.
Write high-quality C/C++ code with comprehensive automated tests; actively participate in design discussions and code reviews.
Troubleshoot and resolve correctness, stability, and performance issues in complex distributed storage and transactional subsystems.
Improve database scalability and throughput as cluster sizes, data volumes, and transaction rates continue to grow.
Build and streamline database management operations, including:
Horizontal cluster scale-out
Incremental and point-in-time backups
Online schema and index operations
Rolling upgrades and blue-green deployments
Identify and implement performance improvements across the storage engine, transaction processing, and replication layers.
Contribute to the open-source YugabyteDB project, helping evolve its storage architecture and operational reliability.
Mentor and technically influence other engineers in distributed systems design, performance engineering, and systems-level debugging.
Required Qualifications
8+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a strong foundation in systems programming using C/C++.
Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science (or related field), or equivalent practical experience.
Deep understanding of distributed systems fundamentals, including:
Replication and consensus
Transactions and consistency models
Fault tolerance and recovery
Experience working on storage engines, databases, or other infrastructure-level systems.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to operate effectively in a collaborative, distributed team environment
Preferred Skills
Hands-on experience with distributed storage systems, transactional engines, or consensus protocols.
Familiarity with LSM-tree based storage engines, WALs, snapshots, or compaction strategies.
Experience with PostgreSQL internals or other relational database engines is a strong plus.
Prior contributions to open-source systems or database projects.

Git and Gitaly are core to GitLab. If they go sideways in production, they affect everything downstream, including continuous integration, code review, and deployments. This role starts with genuine subject matter expertise in Git technologies and extends to reliable operation across GitLab's deployment models: Self-Managed, GitLab Dedicated, and SaaS.
You'll build and develop a team with deep platform expertise and strong operational judgment. You'll partner across engineering groups to shape how Git and Gitaly operations evolve as the platform grows.
What you’ll do
Build and lead a team with deep platform expertise in Git and Gitaly, hiring and developing engineers who can operate this infrastructure layer with strong operational judgment.
Own production reliability for Git and Gitaly across GitLab's full deployment footprint.
Drive incident management, root cause investigation, and postmortems with the technical depth to distinguish a Git internals problem from a generic infrastructure problem.
Design and operate Git and Gitaly service models that work across Self-Managed, GitLab Dedicated, and SaaS, with a clear view of which elements are common and which must differ between them.
Maintain cloud-agnostic architecture and tooling decisions, avoiding designs that assume a single hyperscaler's primitives.
Partner with the teams that own each deployment model so operational practices stay coherent rather than fragmenting into separate playbooks.
Apply distributed systems fundamentals, including consistency, replication, and failure domains, to Gitaly's storage and replication model.
Own elastic storage and compute strategy for Git repository data, including capacity planning, autoscaling, and consumption-based provisioning for GitLab's largest self-managed and SaaS customers.
What you’ll bring
Familiarity with GitLab's product and deployment models, and how Git and Gitaly support repository operations across self-managed, dedicated, and SaaS environments.
Hands-on subject matter expertise in Git internals, including how the protocol, object model, and storage layer behave under load and at scale, not only familiarity with Git usage.
Strong distributed systems fundamentals, including consistency, replication, failure handling, and horizontal scalability.
Experience running production infrastructure across multiple deployment models, such as self-managed, dedicated or single-tenant, and multi-tenant SaaS, or a credible path from adjacent experience to it.
Experience with elastic storage and compute, and consumption-based system design for variable, unpredictable load.
People management experience, ideally leading site reliability engineering-style or platform operations teams.
Direct experience with Gitaly, libgit2, JGit, or another Git implementation's internals is advantageous.
Experience operating cloud-agnostic infrastructure across multiple hyperscalers or on-premises environments is advantageous.
About the team
The Git & Gitaly Operations team owns the Git infrastructure layer that powers GitLab and works at the intersection of Git internals, distributed systems, storage, and production operations.

An overview of this role
Support Engineering at GitLab believes that healthy teams deliver a healthy customer experience, and that command during a crisis shouldn't fall to whoever happens to be senior and available. GitLab's global Incident & Escalation Management (IM/EM) function coordinates critical incidents, complex multi-team engagements, and executive-level escalations for enterprise customers. As Escalation Manager, you'll own complex, executive, and commercial escalations where customer trust and the relationship are at stake, alongside or independently of a technical issue.
In this functional role, you'll advocate for customers inside GitLab, coordinate teams toward resolution, and lead relationship repair after the event.
What you'll do
Own complex, executive, and commercial escalations end-to-end, as defined in GitLab's IM/EM engagement model.
Advocate for customers internally and coordinate Engineering, Support, Product, Customer Success, and Sales toward resolution, tracking commitments and holding owning teams accountable to agreed dates and deliverables.
Maintain a written, customer-facing resolution plan from engagement through confirmed resolution, updating it at each communication milestone.
Coordinate with Incident Managers during concurrent technical incidents to maintain a single, coherent narrative for the customer.
Own external escalation communications using GitLab's approved templates and cadence, and represent GitLab in high-stakes customer conversations where clarity and ownership influence retention.
Engage Sales, Customer Success, and executive stakeholders as needed, including executive-to-executive communication for Severity 1 and 2 events. Brief GitLab leadership with concise summaries that distinguish what's known, what's unknown, and next steps.
Lead post-escalation reviews and relationship repair plans, contribute corrective actions with named owners and due dates to postmortems, and hand the relationship back to the account's Customer Success Manager at resolution.
Partner with the Head of IM/EM to develop playbooks, communication templates, and process improvements based on patterns from escalations.
What you'll bring
Experience in enterprise technical support, customer success, or incident and escalation management at a business-to-business software-as-a-service or enterprise software company.
A track record of owning complex, multi-stakeholder escalations end-to-end, including executive customer engagements and structured resolution or account plans.
Executive-level written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical detail into plain-language updates for customers and GitLab leadership.
The ability to coordinate Engineering, Support, Product, Customer Success, and Sales under pressure without formal authority over those teams.
Calm, structured decision-making with incomplete information and the ability to provide a steadying presence in high-stress customer situations.
Proficiency with support and coordination tools such as Zendesk, Salesforce, Slack, and PagerDuty, or equivalent platforms.
Availability for on-call coverage supporting executive escalations as part of a globally distributed team.
Nice to have:  Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Foundation or equivalent certification; customer-facing experience with GitLab, development, security, and operations (DevSecOps), continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), or cloud-native products; experience with formal escalation or incident command frameworks; or AI-assisted support tools for triage, sentiment analysis, or resolution drafting.
About the team
The Incident & Escalation Management function sits within Support Engineering in GitLab's Enterprise Technology & AI (ETA) division. We operate a follow-the-sun model anchored in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and Asia-Pacific, providing year-round, 24-hour coverage for enterprise customers. Our Escalation Managers work globally rather than within a single region, partnering with Incident Managers, Communications Leads, and regional Support Engineering leadership. You'll help shape our playbooks, templates, and standards as we scale.

Ownership: You'll take features from requirements through delivery and follow-up; your code will run on a platform used by millions of users.
Learning and Growth : You’ll work alongside your engineering team, who treat code review and design review as a learning loop rather than a gate — one of the fastest ways to grow your engineering judgment.
Innovative Culture: You’ll use AI as a genuine part of daily engineering work, developing the judgment to know when to trust it and when not to.
Autonomy: You’ll thrive in our remote-first, asynchronous organization, where clear written communication and self-direction are the pillars of success.
User-Centric Collaboration: You’ll partner closely with PMs and designers to shape requirements, so you understand why you’re building something, not just what.

Own and Ship Features: Design, implement, test, and ship backend features and improvements with minimal guidance, working in Ruby/Rails, Go, or any other modern languages.
Build for Production: Write maintainable, secure, observable, and performant code. Design and maintain APIs, background jobs, integrations, and bounded service functionality, and work with data models, migrations, indexes, and query behavior.
Test and Review: Add and improve automated coverage — unit, integration, contract, and end-to-end where appropriate — and review others’ code for correctness, maintainability, security, performance, and operational risk.
Operate What You Build: Investigate build, test, deployment, and runtime failures at the feature boundary, identify technical debt and propose practical improvements, and take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
Leverage AI: Use AI productively in daily work, validate what it produces, and understand where its limitations matter.

Backend Fundamentals: Professional experience building and shipping production backend applications, with strong programming, API, database, testing, debugging, and performance fundamentals.
Adaptability: Experience with Ruby/Rails, Go, or any other modern backend language. We value the ability to learn and adapt over mastery of a single language.
Feature Ownership: The ability to take a feature from clarification through delivery and follow-up, working independently while seeking input at the right time.
Practical Judgment: Sound instincts about security, reliability, performance, maintainability, and operational risk, plus an understanding of modular backend boundaries and the consequences of coupling.
Clear Communication: Strong written communication and effective collaboration in a remote, asynchronous environment.
AI Fluency: Practical experience with AI coding tools, including the ability to review and correct what they generate.

Production Go services, APIs, concurrency, profiling, or gRPC.
Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, CI/CD, or cloud deployment.
Rust, particularly for systems, security, performance, or platform work.
PostgreSQL, schema evolution, caching, queues, messaging, or event-driven workflows.
Observability using metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and alerts.

Consolidating tokens and migrating authentication paths out of the Rails monolith
Building passkeys and passwordless authentication
Developing composite identities that combine machine and human authorization for AI
Improving service accounts and secure automation
Enhancing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP), OpenID Connect (OIDC), and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) capabilities for automated user provisioning and single sign-on (SSO)

Shape the roadmap for GATE and GitLab's authentication services with the team.
Design and implement token issuance, validation, and identity services in Go and Ruby across the Rails monolith and GATE, including new authentication mechanisms such as Workload Identity Federation.
Migrate authentication and token management paths from the monolith into GATE while maintaining reliability across all deployment models.
Build authentication mechanisms from the ground up, such as Workload Identity Federation.
Strengthen security for users and organizations through access management tooling and by addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program.
Define and improve standards for style, maintainability, and engineering practices in a high-scale environment, and advocate for them through code review.
Communicate publicly about GitLab initiatives, projects, and contributions from people not working for GitLab Inc. Reflect GitLab's values in these communications.
Ship moderately sized features and improvements with moderate guidance and support from other team members, and collaborate on larger projects, including the build-out of GATE.
Participate in the maintainer trainee program at your own comfortable pace while working toward becoming a project maintainer.
What you'll bring
Professional experience with Go and/or Ruby in scaling or mission-critical SaaS products.
Familiarity with authentication and authorization technologies or techniques, such as OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SSO, SCIM, LDAP, JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), role-based access control (RBAC), or identity and access management (IAM).
Knowledge of token systems, cryptographic signing, and key management.
Experience building or contributing to a service from concept to production, including proposal, discussion, and execution.
Proficiency in written and verbal English, with the ability to communicate complex problems and solutions clearly in a remote, largely asynchronous work environment.
Experience diagnosing, preventing, and resolving performance and optimization problems.
Experience working in an iterative software development process, managing your work effectively, staying organized, and following through on priorities.

Our mission is to empower GitLab system administrators with the toolkit they need to create their desired balance of security and accessibility for their GitLab experience.
Authentication is the first impression a new customer has when they configure a new GitLab instance. We aim to make it as seamless as possible, from that first login to onboarding users and managing security rules for their instance in a secure, flexible, and scalable way.

In the Environment Automation specialization, your focus is on operating and automating hundreds of GitLab environments—from initial provisioning to day-to-day maintenance tasks. 
Unlike other SRE roles, this position centers on automating the lifecycle of many tenant environments, ensuring they remain secure, consistent, and reliable at scale.
Some examples of the projects you could work on:
Designing infrastructure automation that provisions and operates GitLab environments using Terraform, Ansible, and Kubernetes
Creating and maintaining deployment packages for GitLab, such as Helm Charts and omnibus-gitlab
Building and operating Dedicated GitLab instances integrated with cloud-native services (e.g., GCP, AWS)
Developing tools to orchestrate infrastructure-as-code workflows across multiple tenants
Deploying and managing microservices on Kubernetes clusters at scale
Enhancing GitLab’s observability stack (e.g., Prometheus, ELK) to support proactive monitoring and incident response
Integrating with and operating infrastructure in cloud provider ecosystems (e.g., IAM, networking, storage)
Championing and implementing cloud security best practices across automated infrastructure
What You’ll Do
Build & Scale Multi-Tenant Infrastructure: Design and implement automation that provisions and manages hundreds of isolated GitLab environments using Terraform, Ansible, and Kubernetes. Manage complex state strategies and workspace configurations to support scale and maintainability.
Debug & Resolve Production Issues: Troubleshoot issues across Kubernetes clusters, cloud services, and GitLab apps—identifying root causes of failed deployments, crash loops, and scheduling conflicts to ensure service continuity.
Automate Operations at Scale: Replace manual workflows with infrastructure-as-code solutions, including automated version upgrades, configuration rollouts, and provisioning pipelines that operate reliably across all tenants.
Monitor & Predict Capacity: Build observability systems that detect bottlenecks, predict usage trends, and optimize resource consumption using tools like Prometheus, ELK, and Grafana.
Respond & Lead During Incidents: Lead incident response and postmortem efforts, applying technical depth to resolve issues and establish operational standards that reduce future risk.
Architect & Collaborate: Influence architectural decisions around automation, scalability, and operational excellence. Partner with engineering teams to improve automation, platform resilience, and production-readiness.

Comfortable solving state isolation issues and building reliable, reusable infrastructure code. Experience with Ansible and templating tools like Jsonnet is a plus.

GitLab Platform Proficiency: Comfortable using GitLab as a daily tool for infrastructure automation, collaboration, and operational workflows.

You'll take ownership of large deliverables from early ideas through implementation, working directly with product, design, frontend, and engineering partners to shape the technical and product roadmap. You'll stay hands-on across GitLab's Ruby on Rails application and newer services, including greenfield projects, while helping the team build its expertise in modular service design.
What you’ll do
Lead large technical deliverables from initial problem definition through delivery, often across multiple months or quarters.
Design and develop backend systems for vulnerability and dependency management, including security report ingestion, storage, indexing, querying, and integrations with key third-party systems.
Build and improve systems using Ruby on Rails and PostgreSQL, and contribute to newer services using technologies such as Go or Rust where appropriate.
Shape technical plans, break down complex work, and help other engineers deliver effectively.
Work directly with product, design, frontend, and engineering partners to make clear decisions, resolve constraints, and deliver measurable progress.
Influence the team's product and technical roadmap through hands-on investigation, clear proposals, and iterative delivery that demonstrates progress in each monthly release cycle.
Apply a security mindset when designing systems, including considering how GitLab identifies and handles malicious or vulnerable software packages.
Define patterns for modular services, provide technical leadership when vulnerability management work spans multiple GitLab areas, and share that expertise across GitLab Security.
What you’ll bring
Experience leading complex backend projects from idea through delivery while remaining hands-on with design and development.
Strong PostgreSQL experience, including evidence of query optimization, table optimization, and write-ahead log management in data-intensive systems.

About NCR Atleos
NCR Atleos Corporation (NYSE: NATL) is a global technology company that enables financial access and commerce through assisted and self-service solutions and comprehensive support services. NCR Atleos serves financial and public-sector organizations in more than 100 countries and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.
The opportunity
As an Application Security Compliance Lead, you will help ensure that NCR Atleos software products and development practices meet applicable security, privacy and regulatory requirements. Working within our global Application Security team, you will turn complex requirements into practical guidance, prepare teams for assessments, and help demonstrate that security and privacy are embedded throughout the software lifecycle.
A major focus is organization-level PCI Software Security Framework (SSF) activities: support product teams to achieve and retain PCI Secure Software Standard listings and maintain validation of our Secure Software Lifecycle practices. This role suits someone who combines compliance expertise with software development and application security knowledge.
What you will do
Govern the Secure SDLC. Maintain and improve practices aligned with the PCI Secure SLC Standard.
Enable PCI SSF validation. Guide teams through external assessment, self-assessment, annual attestation and periodic revalidation activities.
Interpret requirements. Translate security, privacy, legal and industry requirements into clear, proportionate guidance.
Assess readiness and close gaps. Coordinate reviews, evidence, gap analysis, remediation and resolution of findings.
Engage and influence. Partner with engineering, Legal, risk, compliance and security teams, QSAs and the PCI SSC.
Build capability. Create training and reusable guidance; monitor developments and communicate material changes.
Drive continual improvement. Use industry changes, stakeholder feedback, internal audits, assessment outcomes, recurring findings, and incidents to strengthen controls and processes.
What you will bring
Essential experience and capabilities
Typically, 7+ years of relevant experience in application security, software security assurance, secure software development, technology risk, privacy, compliance, or audit.
Practical experience developing, operating, governing or assessing a Secure SDLC.
Experience interpreting security or compliance requirements and supporting assessments, evidence collection, gap analysis and remediation.
Working knowledge of threat modelling, vulnerability management, security testing, and risk-based decision-making.
Technical understanding of cloud services, source-code management, and CI/CD practices sufficient to engage credibly with engineering teams.
Ability to convert complex requirements into pragmatic guidance and make evidence-based recommendations.
Strong stakeholder management, communication, analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to influence without direct authority.
Ability to work independently and effectively within a globally distributed team.
Comfortable using AI assistants, such as Copilot, responsibly in day-to-day work to improve personal productivity, quality, and speed of delivery.
A bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience and qualifications.
Desirable experience and capabilities
Direct experience of PCI SSF validation or a comparable software security assurance framework.
Knowledge of payment-card security, GDPR requirements, NIST CSF and OWASP standards and guidance.
Experience delivering application security or compliance-related training.
Knowledge of security and governance for AI-enabled software development and products.
A relevant certification, such as CISSP, CSSLP, CIPP, CIPT or CIPM.
How you will succeed
Teams receive clear, timely, and actionable compliance guidance.
PCI SSF validation activities are well planned, appropriately evidenced, and progressed effectively.
Compliance gaps and findings are clearly owned, prioritized, tracked, and resolved.
Secure SDLC requirements remain practical, current, and consistently understood.
Assessment and incident lessons lead to sustainable improvements and strong stakeholder relationships.
Evidence we value
In your application, we would particularly welcome examples of how you have interpreted a security standard, prepared a product or organization for assessment, resolved a significant compliance gap, or influenced an engineering team to adopt a more effective security practice.

Security Officer (Physical Security Operations)
Experience: 8–10 Years
Role Purpose:
The Security Officer is responsible for managing end-to-end physical security operations, including day-to-day security activities, manpower deployment, creation and implementation of SOPs, vendor coordination, monthly billing validation, and management of security automation systems. The role requires strong operational control, process orientation, and coordination with internal and external stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
1. Physical Security Operations
Manage day-to-day physical security operations across assigned sites/facilities.
Ensure protection of employees, visitors, assets, and infrastructure.
Oversee access control, perimeter security, surveillance, and patrolling activities.
Conduct routine inspections, audits, and compliance checks.
2. Manpower Management & Deployment
Plan, deploy, and supervise security manpower as per operational and risk requirements.
Prepare duty rosters, shift schedules, relievers, and leave planning.
Monitor guard performance, discipline, and adherence to SOPs.
Address issues related to absenteeism, misconduct, and operational gaps.
3. SOP Development & Compliance
- Create, implement, and periodically review security SOPs and post orders, including:
Visitor management
Material movement (inward/outward)
Access control procedures
Emergency response and incident handling
Ensure SOP compliance through training, audits, and mock drills.
Maintain documentation for audits and management review.

CCTV and Video Management Systems (VMS)
Access Control Systems (ACS)
Alarm and intrusion detection systems
Coordinate with vendors for installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
Ensure system uptime, reporting, and basic first-level issue resolution.

Coordinate with security service providers and related vendors.
Validate monthly security bills, attendance sheets, OT claims, and deployment strength.
Ensure billing accuracy as per contract, SLA, and approved manpower.
Highlight discrepancies and follow up for corrective action.

Respond to security incidents, breaches, thefts, and emergencies.
Conduct preliminary investigations and prepare incident reports with root-cause analysis.
Recommend corrective and preventive measures.
Liaise with local authorities and emergency services when required.
7. Reporting & MIS
Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly security reports and MIS.
Track incidents, manpower, audits, automation uptime, and billing data.
Present observations and improvement plans to management.
Key Skills & Competencies
Strong knowledge of physical security operations
Experience in manpower management and deployment
SOP drafting and process implementation skills
Working knowledge of CCTV, ACS, VMS, and security automation
Vendor coordination and billing validation experience
Good communication, leadership, and reporting skills
Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, and basic reporting tools
Qualification
Graduate in any discipline (preferred)
Defense, paramilitary, or professional security background is an advantage
Relevant security or safety certifications are an added advantage
Experience Requirement
Minimum 8–10 years of relevant experience in physical security operations
Experience in corporate offices, factories, pharma, IT parks, or large facilities preferred
Exposure to multi-site operations and security automation is highly desirable

jobs.title: Applications Engineering, Sr Engineer
jobs.description:
We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You have spent the last few years deep in FPGA design and implementation, and you have learned that the real work begins when a customer's design does not compile the way they expected or when partitioning across multiple FPGAs creates timing issues no one saw coming. You are the engineer who stays on the call until the problem is solved, not because you have to, but because leaving something half-fixed bothers you.
You are comfortable reading Verilog or SystemVerilog that someone else wrote, understanding what they were trying to do, and figuring out why the synthesis tool is choking on it. You know your way around FPGA architecture well enough to explain why a design that worked fine in simulation is failing in hardware, and you can do it in a way that does not make the customer feel like they missed something obvious.
Working with customers energizes you. You like the variety of problems, the pressure of real deadlines, and the satisfaction of helping someone get unstuck. You do not need everything documented perfectly to move forward. You ask the right questions, dig into log files, reproduce issues locally, and escalate to R&D when needed with enough context that they can actually help.
At Synopsys, you will work with some of the most complex emulation and prototyping workflows in the industry, supporting global customers who depend on Zebu and Protocompiler to verify chips that power everything from automotive systems to data centers.
What You'll Be Doing
Provide technical support to global customers using Synopsys Zebu Emulation and Protocompiler Prototyping software, troubleshooting issues across partitioning, synthesis, place and route, and hardware debug
Work directly with customers to migrate their designs to new software releases, ensuring compatibility and resolving any regressions or performance issues that surface
Deploy new software features on live customer designs, helping them adopt capabilities like advanced partitioning algorithms, new debug modes, or updated FPGA target support
Deliver technical training sessions to customers, ranging from basic tool usage to advanced workflows for multi-FPGA partitioning and hardware-software co-verification
Collaborate with Synopsys HAV R&D teams to report customer issues, provide reproducible test cases, and advocate for product improvements based on real-world usage patterns
Support pre-sales evaluations by running customer designs through the Synopsys emulation and prototyping flow, demonstrating performance and identifying potential adoption blockers
Travel occasionally to customer sites for onsite support, training, or critical issue resolution
The Impact You Will Have
Enable customers to bring up complex SoC designs on emulation and prototyping platforms faster, reducing their verification cycle time by weeks or months
Improve product quality by surfacing real customer pain points to R&D with enough technical detail that fixes can be prioritized and implemented effectively
Build customer confidence in Synopsys HAV solutions through responsive, expert-level support that helps them solve problems they could not solve on their own
Expand adoption of new software features by showing customers how to use them on their actual designs, not just in demos
Reduce escalations and support load over time by delivering training that helps customers become more self-sufficient with the toolchain
Strengthen customer relationships by being the engineer they trust to pick up the phone when something is broken and production timelines are at risk
Contribute to the technical knowledge base and internal best practices that make the entire support organization more effective
What You'll Need
Bachelors in Electronics Engineering with 2-3 years of experience, or Master's in Electronics Engineering with 1-2 years, specifically in emulation or prototyping environments
Hands-on experience with logic design and implementation using FPGAs, including synthesis, place and route, and timing closure
Strong working knowledge of Verilog, System Verilog, or VHDL, including the ability to read, debug, and modify RTL written by others
Practical experience with FPGA architecture and back-end implementation flows, including understanding of resource utilization, clock domain crossing, and design partitioning
Exposure to Xilinx or Altera synthesis tools is a plus, as is familiarity with Synopsys Prototyping or Emulation hardware and software
Experience with interface protocols like PCIe, AXI, UART, or I2C is a plus, particularly in the context of hardware-software integration
Scripting experience in Python, Tcl, or shell is desirable for automating workflows and analyzing log files
Who You Are
You can take a vague customer complaint like 'the compile is failing' and turn it into a specific, reproducible issue with enough detail that R&D can act on it
You stay calm when a customer is frustrated or under pressure, and you focus on solving the problem rather than defending the tool
You are comfortable working across time zones and managing multiple customer issues in parallel without losing track of who needs what by when
You do not mind digging through synthesis logs, waveform dumps, or FPGA utilization reports to find the root cause of a problem
You can explain a complex technical tradeoff, like why a design needs to be repartitioned or why certain optimizations are not possible, in a way that makes sense to someone who is not an FPGA expert
You are open to occasional travel for customer support, training, or onsite troubleshooting when remote support is not enough
The Team You'll Be Part Of
You will join Synopsys Technical Sales Group (TSG) as part of the Hardware Assisted Verification (HAV) team, working alongside expert-level field engineers who support customers globally on Zebu Emulation and Protocompiler Prototyping solutions. The team works closely with R&D and directly with customers at all stages of the emulation and prototyping cycle, from pre-sales evaluation through post-deployment support. You will collaborate with engineers across geographies and gain exposure to Synopsys HAV hardware platforms as part of your technical development.

Drive customer deployments of VCS/Verdi simulation/debug technology, working closely with product teams and R&D to ensure successful adoption and integration.
Diagnose and troubleshoot complex technical issues in verification flows, utilizing good product knowledge and analytical skills.
Collaborate with global domain experts to gather requirements and contribute to the development of a robust product roadmap.
Drive competitive engagements by demonstrating Synopsys VCS/Verdi advantages and supporting customers in benchmarking scenarios.
Interface directly with customers, product validation, and R&D teams to propose solutions and suggest improvements in implementation and validation processes.
Develop and optimize scripts (Perl, TCL, Shell, Make,Python) to enhance productivity and workflow automation.

Drive innovation in verification methodologies by integrating advanced features and AI-driven productivity tools.
Enhance Synopsys’ product offerings by providing actionable feedback from customer engagements and competitive benchmarking.
Facilitate seamless collaboration across global teams, ensuring consistent delivery of high-quality solutions.

Who You Are:
Excellent written and oral communication skills, comfortable interfacing with global teams and customers.
Collaborative team player with a proactive and innovative mindset.

Run security analysis as part of the cybersecurity lifecycle, from planning through design, implementation, verification, and release.

Author customer-facing security integration guidance that describes the threat landscape, implemented controls, and how customers should integrate the IP.

Use Python to automate analysis, transform inventories and threat-model data, and produce repeatable reports other analysts can run and review.
Use agentic workflows (AI agents, structured prompts, and human-in-the-loop review) to speed research, first drafts, consistency checks, and routine tasks without handing off ownership of findings.
Run the job in Jira, Confluence, Git, and GitLab: track analysis and incident work, keep project documentation current, and version work products through merge requests and review.

Give product teams threat analysis they can trust and act on without re-deriving the work.
Leave cybersecurity requirements and verification objectives that design and verification teams can execute.
Produce integration guidance that customers can follow without a security specialist in the room.
Strengthen the cybersecurity lifecycle for IP products so security work stays current as the design changes.
Improve consistency of analysis across similar IP classes through shared working sessions and clear written conclusions.
Help the organization respond to in-field issues with clear assessment and practical advisories.

Ability to identify assets, attackers, attack surfaces, and attack paths, and to map each path to a mitigation (in-product control or integration requirement).
Comfort working without a single known end-system: analysis must cover representative integration scenarios and state assumptions clearly.
Experience applying a cybersecurity lifecycle across planning, requirements, design, implementation, verification, and release.
Ability to turn threat-analysis results into requirements, design guidance, verification objectives, and release evidence.
Hands-on understanding of embedded systems: SoC or MCU integration, firmware, hardware/software interfaces, memory-mapped registers, boot and debug, and on-chip interconnects.

Hands-on proficiency as a digital designer or a digital verification engineer. Either path is sufficient.
Ability to read and discuss RTL (Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VHDL), architecture, interfaces, and register maps with designers and verification leads.
Ability to judge whether a claimed cybersecurity control is implemented in the design and whether it is verifiable.
Experience delivering analysis or engineering work inside agile product teams, including re-scoping when product content changes.

Practical experience using AI agents and agentic workflows to speed research, drafting, and repetitive analysis, while keeping the human as owner of technical conclusions.
Hands-on use of Jira, Confluence, Git, and GitLab (or an equivalent Git forge) for tickets, documentation, and review.
Clear written and spoken English; able to lead technical sessions with geographically distributed teams.
Working knowledge of ISO/SAE 21434 or a comparable product-cybersecurity standard is helpful, as is analog or mixed-signal background, semiconductor IP product experience, vulnerability handling, or applied embedded cryptography.

jobs.description:
We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You have spent over a decade architecting test solutions for chips that power everything from autonomous vehicles to data centers, and you understand that DFT is not an afterthought, it is the difference between a design that ships on time and one that bleeds money in yield loss. You know the nuances of scan compression versus hierarchical DFT, not from a textbook, but from making the call on a 10-billion-gate SoC where the wrong decision costs months.
You are the person design teams call when ATPG coverage is stuck at 97% and manufacturing is demanding 99.5%. You have debugged IJTAG networks that span multiple chiplets, written the Tcl that automated what used to take three engineers a week, and sat in rooms with VPs explaining why their test access strategy needs to change before tapeout. You do not just know the IEEE standards, you have deployed them in production silicon and lived with the consequences.
At Synopsys, you will work on methodologies that define how the world's most complex chips get tested. The problems are hard, the customers are sophisticated, and what you build will matter.
What You'll Be Doing
Define and drive DFT methodologies for next-generation ASIC and SoC designs across strategic customer programs, translating architecture decisions into deployable best practices
Lead deployment of advanced test solutions including scan compression, hierarchical DFT, IEEE 1500 wrappers, IJTAG instrumentation networks, and embedded test IP across multi-billion-gate designs
Architect scalable test access infrastructures using IEEE 1149.1, IEEE 1149.6, IEEE 1687, and IEEE 1500 standards for complex multi-die and chiplet-based systems
Develop automation frameworks, signoff criteria, and reusable methodology packages using Tcl, Python, and Perl that accelerate adoption across business units
Serve as technical leader and subject matter expert for Synopsys TestMAX DFT, TestMAX ATPG, diagnosis, and silicon lifecycle solutions in customer engagements and internal escalations
Collaborate directly with R&D teams to influence TestMAX product roadmap based on real deployment challenges and customer requirements
Provide technical leadership for strategic customer engagements, methodology reviews, and complex DFT architecture decisions that impact tapeout schedules and silicon success
The Impact You Will Have
Enable successful deployment of industry-leading DFT methodologies across the world's most advanced semiconductor programs in AI, automotive, and hyperscale computing
Drive measurable improvements in test coverage, pattern count reduction, and manufacturing yield through methodology standardization and best-practice development
Influence next-generation TestMAX capabilities by translating customer deployment challenges into product requirements that shape future releases
Accelerate adoption of standards-based test architectures across strategic accounts, reducing time-to-market and improving silicon reliability
Improve engineering productivity across multiple programs through automation frameworks and reusable methodology packages that eliminate redundant work
Establish Synopsys as the trusted technical advisor in DFT and manufacturing test, strengthening customer relationships and competitive positioning
Contribute to breakthrough technologies powering autonomous vehicles, AI accelerators, and next-generation networking infrastructure
What You'll Need
Bachelor's or Master's in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field
10+ years in semiconductor or EDA industry with at least 5 years focused on DFT architecture, ATPG, and manufacturing test methodologies
Demonstrated expertise architecting and implementing DFT solutions for large-scale ASIC and SoC designs, including successful tapeouts
Hands-on experience with Synopsys TestMAX DFT and TestMAX ATPG solutions in production design environments
Deep technical knowledge of scan insertion, scan compression, hierarchical DFT, ATPG and diagnosis, stuck-at/transition/path-delay/bridge/cell-aware fault models, and coverage optimization techniques
Expertise deploying IEEE 1149.1 (JTAG), IEEE 1149.6 (AC JTAG), IEEE 1687 (IJTAG), and IEEE 1500 standards in complex test access architectures
Experience integrating DFT IP including Codec/embedded compression, OCC, LBIST, TAP controllers, JTAG and IJTAG infrastructure, TDR networks, and IEEE 1500 wrappers
Strong understanding of RTL-to-GDSII flows and how DFT interacts with synthesis, physical design, timing closure, and signoff
Proficiency with Tcl, Python, Perl, or Shell scripting for methodology automation and deployment
Experience defining enterprise-wide DFT standards and signoff methodologies is a strong plus
Background supporting advanced-node ASICs, multi-billion-gate SoCs, silicon bring-up, diagnosis, or yield improvement is highly valued
Knowledge of functional safety standards and automotive test requirements is a plus
Contributions to industry test standards, technical publications, patents, or conference presentations strengthen your candidacy
Who You Are
You can walk into a room with a customer's design team, diagnose a coverage gap in their hierarchical DFT strategy, and sketch a solution on the whiteboard that they trust enough to implement before tapeout
You mentor engineers not by telling them what to do, but by asking the questions that help them see the tradeoff they missed between test time and pattern count
You are comfortable presenting a methodology roadmap to a VP in two slides and then diving three levels deep with an engineer debugging an IJTAG network the same afternoon
You push back when a proposed DFT architecture does not align with manufacturing realities, and you do it in a way that builds trust rather than friction
You treat automation as a first-class deliverable, not an afterthought, because you know the methodology only scales if the Tcl actually works
You stay current with industry trends, standards evolution, and emerging test challenges because you know that what worked on 7nm will not necessarily work on 3nm
The Team You'll Be Part Of
You will join the Digital Methodology Center of Excellence, a highly visible organization responsible for defining and advancing Synopsys' DFT methodologies, best practices, and customer deployment strategies. Working closely with R&D, product engineering, customer success, and strategic accounts, you will help shape the future of Design-for-Test and drive successful adoption of the industry's most advanced test solutions worldwide.
Rewards and Benefits

Lead deployment of advanced test solutions including scan compression, hierarchical DFT, IEEE 1500 wrappers, IJTAG instrumentation networks, and embedded test IP across multi-billion-gate designs

Develop automation frameworks, signoff criteria, and reusable methodology packages using Tcl, Python, and Perl that accelerate adoption across business units
Serve as technical leader and subject matter expert for Synopsys TestMAX DFT, TestMAX ATPG, diagnosis, and silicon lifecycle solutions in customer engagements and internal escalations
Collaborate directly with R&D teams to influence TestMAX product roadmap based on real deployment challenges and customer requirements
Provide technical leadership for strategic customer engagements, methodology reviews, and complex DFT architecture decisions that impact tapeout schedules and silicon success
The Impact You Will Have

Drive measurable improvements in test coverage, pattern count reduction, and manufacturing yield through methodology standardization and best-practice development
Influence next-generation TestMAX capabilities by translating customer deployment challenges into product requirements that shape future releases
Accelerate adoption of standards-based test architectures across strategic accounts, reducing time-to-market and improving silicon reliability
Improve engineering productivity across multiple programs through automation frameworks and reusable methodology packages that eliminate redundant work
Establish Synopsys as the trusted technical advisor in DFT and manufacturing test, strengthening customer relationships and competitive positioning
Contribute to breakthrough technologies powering autonomous vehicles, AI accelerators, and next-generation networking infrastructure
What You'll Need
Bachelor's or Master's in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field
15+ years in semiconductor or EDA industry with at least 5 years focused on DFT architecture, ATPG, and manufacturing test methodologies
Demonstrated expertise architecting and implementing DFT solutions for large-scale ASIC and SoC designs, including successful tapeouts
Hands-on experience with Synopsys TestMAX DFT and TestMAX ATPG solutions in production design environments
Deep technical knowledge of scan insertion, scan compression, hierarchical DFT, ATPG and diagnosis, stuck-at/transition/path-delay/bridge/cell-aware fault models, and coverage optimization techniques
Expertise deploying IEEE 1149.1 (JTAG), IEEE 1149.6 (AC JTAG), IEEE 1687 (IJTAG), and IEEE 1500 standards in complex test access architectures
Experience integrating DFT IP including Codec/embedded compression, OCC, LBIST, TAP controllers, JTAG and IJTAG infrastructure, TDR networks, and IEEE 1500 wrappers
Strong understanding of RTL-to-GDSII flows and how DFT interacts with synthesis, physical design, timing closure, and signoff
Proficiency with Tcl, Python, Perl, or Shell scripting for methodology automation and deployment
Experience defining enterprise-wide DFT standards and signoff methodologies is a strong plus
Background supporting advanced-node ASICs, multi-billion-gate SoCs, silicon bring-up, diagnosis, or yield improvement is highly valued
Knowledge of functional safety standards and automotive test requirements is a plus
Contributions to industry test standards, technical publications, patents, or conference presentations strengthen your candidacy
Who You Are
You can walk into a room with a customer's design team, diagnose a coverage gap in their hierarchical DFT strategy, and sketch a solution on the whiteboard that they trust enough to implement before tapeout
You mentor engineers not by telling them what to do, but by asking the questions that help them see the tradeoff they missed between test time and pattern count
You are comfortable presenting a methodology roadmap to a VP in two slides and then diving three levels deep with an engineer debugging an IJTAG network the same afternoon
You push back when a proposed DFT architecture does not align with manufacturing realities, and you do it in a way that builds trust rather than friction
You treat automation as a first-class deliverable, not an afterthought, because you know the methodology only scales if the Tcl actually works
You stay current with industry trends, standards evolution, and emerging test challenges because you know that what worked on 7nm will not necessarily work on 3nm

You will join the Digital Methodology Center of Excellence, a highly visible organization responsible for defining and advancing Synopsys' DFT methodologies, best practices, and customer deployment strategies. jobs.title: Senior Layout Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Layout Design, Sr Engineer
We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You have spent years translating analog circuit schematics into physical layouts that actually perform, not just pass DRC. You know that a GPIO layout is not just about routing metal, it is about understanding how a 2pF mismatch or a 10-micron shift can break ESD performance or skew I/O timing in ways the schematic never predicted. You think in cross-sections and current density maps, and you have learned to spot a latchup risk or a substrate coupling problem before it ever hits silicon.
You are comfortable sitting with a circuit designer who hands you a half-finished schematic and a set of constraints, and you know which questions to ask to turn that into a layout that meets area, performance, and reliability targets. Matching does not scare you, it is something you have done enough times to have opinions about dummy placement and orientation strategies. You have debugged parasitic extraction results at 2 a.m. and lived to tell the story.
Automation is not a nice-to-have for you, it is how you stay sane. You write scripts to check spacing rules, generate array structures, or pull reports because doing it manually fifteen times is not an option. At Synopsys, you will work on IO and analog IP that ships in real products, with a team that knows the difference between a layout that works and one that just closes.
What You'll Be Doing
Design and own full custom analog layouts for GPIO, specialty IO, and general-purpose analog IP blocks including I2C, I3C, SMBUS, eMMC, SVID, Quad SPI, and JTAG interfaces
Develop high-performance LVDS layouts and crystal oscillator circuits with attention to signal integrity, noise coupling, and parasitic management
Collaborate with circuit designers to translate schematics into physical implementations that meet area, performance, matching, and reliability specifications
Perform layout verification including DRC, LVS, and parasitic extraction analysis, iterating with design teams to close on performance targets
Build and maintain layout automation scripts to improve design efficiency, consistency, and quality across IP families
Provide technical guidance and layout reviews for junior engineers, helping them develop skills in analog matching, IO frame design, and technology-specific layout techniques
Work across global teams in the US, Europe, and Asia to align on design standards, schedules, and deliverables for multi-site IP development programs
The Impact You Will Have
Your layouts will directly enable GPIO and specialty IO performance in Synopsys IP that powers AI, automotive, and high-performance computing chips used by leading semiconductor companies
You will help reduce design cycle time and improve first-pass silicon success rates through high-quality layout and proactive parasitic management
The automation scripts and layout methodologies you develop will become reusable assets across multiple IP families and process nodes
Your technical reviews and mentorship will raise the skill level of the layout team and reduce costly respins caused by layout-induced performance issues
You will contribute to IP roadmaps by identifying layout-driven design constraints early, influencing architecture decisions before they become problems
The IO and analog blocks you design will ship in millions of devices, affecting real-world product performance and time to market for Synopsys customers
You will help establish layout best practices and design guidelines that scale across a global engineering organization
What You'll Need
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electronics Engineering, VLSI Design, or equivalent practical experience
3 to 6 years of hands-on experience in analog or mixed-signal custom IC layout design
Strong understanding of CMOS layout fundamentals including device matching, parasitic effects, electromigration, latchup, and ESD protection strategies
Proficiency with industry-standard layout tools such as Cadence Virtuoso, Calibre, or equivalent verification and extraction platforms
Working knowledge of scripting languages such as Python, Perl, TCL, or SKILL for layout automation and design checks
Experience with IO frame design, pad ring assembly, or specialty interface IP layout is a strong plus
Familiarity with parasitic extraction tools and the ability to interpret and act on R/C extraction results to meet circuit performance targets
Who You Are
You can sit in a layout review, spot a symmetry issue or a metal density violation in seconds, and explain the fix without needing to pull up the full design
You do not wait for perfect specs, you work with what circuit designers give you, ask clarifying questions about critical matching pairs or bias routing, and move forward
You treat layout as a craft, not a checklist, and you care about the difference between a layout that barely passes LVS and one that is actually manufacturable and reliable
You are comfortable working across time zones with teams in different geographies, coordinating handoffs and reviews without losing momentum
You are the person junior engineers come to when they are stuck on a tricky matching problem or cannot figure out why their extraction numbers are off, and you enjoy that role
You know when to escalate a layout-driven performance issue to the circuit designer and when to solve it yourself with a smarter floorplan or routing strategy
The Team You'll Be Part Of
You will be part of a strong development team focused on GPIO, specialty IO, and general-purpose analog IP development. The team works on a range of interface IP including I2C, I3C, SMBUS, eMMC, SVID, Quad SPI, JTAG, high-performance LVDS, and crystal oscillators. You will collaborate closely with experienced engineers locally in Bangalore and across global sites, contributing to multi-site IP programs that serve customers worldwide.
Rewards and Benefits
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.
