jobs.title: Applied Scientist II, Cross Border Science and Analytics
jobs.description: DESCRIPTION The Cross-Border (XB) Science & Analytics team is at the heart of Amazon's international marketplace expansion, powering science-driven solutions that enable customers across 20+ countries to discover and purchase products seamlessly across borders. Our work directly impacts millions in annualized business value through ML models, algorithms, and data-driven systems that solve some of Amazon's most complex cross-border challenges. We are a lean, high-impact team of scientists working across various programs spanning search ranking, demand forecasting, pricing optimization, product recommendations, language understanding, and generative AI. We partner closely with product, engineering, and business teams across Amazon's global retail organization to take science from ideation to production at scale. Key job responsibilities We are looking for a passionate and technically strong Applied Scientist to join our team. In this role, you will design, develop, and deploy machine learning models and algorithms that directly improve the cross-border shopping experience for millions of Amazon customers worldwide. You will work on challenging, ambiguous problems—from improving search relevance across languages to building ML-powered pricing and recommendation systems—with significant autonomy and end-to-end ownership. The code you ship, the decisions you make, and the care you show a customer all add up to real impact. Today, tens of millions of workers start and end their days with our workforce operating platform. Helping people get paid, grow in their careers, and shape the future of their industries. That’s what we do. We never stop learning. We never stop challenging the norm. We push for better, and we celebrate the wins along the way. Here, you’ll get flexibility that’s real, benefits you can count on, and a team that succeeds together. Because at UKG, your work matters—and so do you. Role Overview We are seeking a highly accomplished Principal Software Engineer to join the engineering team for the WFM platform product. This role is focused on leading the technical direction, architecture, and engineering strategy for a modern, scalable, resilient, and intelligent enterprise SaaS product platform. As a Principal Software Engineer, you will play a key role in defining the technology stack, shaping the technical roadmap, driving architectural decisions, and leading complex engineering initiatives across multiple teams. You will be expected to bring deep technical expertise, enterprise-scale thinking, and a strong understanding of performance, reliability, observability, and operational excellence. This role requires a hands-on technical leader who can guide engineering teams through agentic SDLC, complex design decisions, lead technical discussions, troubleshoot critical technical issues, and build scalable and secure platform. The ideal candidate will have strong proficiency in Java, database technologies, cloud-native engineering, distributed systems, and modern AI-assisted software engineering practices. We are looking for an engineer who combines strategic technical vision with practical execution, mentors senior engineers, raises engineering standards, and helps build a product platform that is scalable, secure, observable, performant, and ready for the future. Responsibilities Technical Leadership & Architecture Define and drive the architectural vision for the WFM platform, ensuring scalability, resiliency, performance, maintainability, and long-term extensibility. Lead the evaluation, selection, and evolution of the core technology stack, including application frameworks, cloud-native services, database technologies, observability tools, messaging systems, and AI-enabled engineering capabilities. Define and influence the technical roadmap in partnership with engineering leadership, product management, architecture, and cross-functional stakeholders. Lead architecture reviews, design discussions, and technical decision-making for complex product and platform initiatives. Provide technical direction across multiple teams and ensure alignment with enterprise engineering standards, security expectations, and operational goals. Evaluate emerging technologies, frameworks, and engineering practices to continuously improve product capabilities, developer productivity, and system reliability. Software Engineering & Platform Development Design and build highly scalable, secure, and reliable cloud-native enterprise platform. Lead the development of distributed systems, APIs, backend services, event-driven workflows, and data-intensive applications. Drive modernization initiatives that improve system performance, scalability, maintainability, and engineering velocity. Establish and promote engineering best practices around code quality, testing, automation, design patterns, performance optimization, and maintainable architecture. Lead complex cross-functional engineering initiatives that require coordination across multiple teams, systems, and stakeholders. Ensure the product is built with an enterprise-level mindset, including strong consideration for scalability, compliance, security, availability, customer experience, and operational readiness. Observability, Reliability & Operational Excellence Drive platform-wide improvements in observability, monitoring, logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, and service health management. Define and implement observability standards using platforms and tools such as OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Kibana, Prometheus, Datadog, Splunk, or similar technologies. Lead troubleshooting and root-cause analysis for complex production issues, performance bottlenecks, system failures, and reliability concerns. Partner with engineering, operations, and SRE teams to define service-level objectives, operational metrics, error budgets, incident response practices, and reliability improvement plans. Lead post-incident reviews and ensure corrective actions result in long-term improvements to architecture, automation, resiliency, and monitoring. Champion proactive engineering practices that improve product stability, reduce operational risk, and enhance customer trust. Performance Engineering & Scalability Drive performance tuning across application services, database layers, APIs, integration points, and distributed system components. Identify and resolve scalability challenges in high-volume, enterprise-grade SaaS environments. Lead capacity planning, load testing, profiling, query optimization, caching strategies, and performance benchmarking efforts. Ensure that technical designs account for throughput, latency, concurrency, data growth, resiliency, and cost efficiency. Partner with teams to establish measurable performance goals and continuously improve system responsiveness and efficiency. AI-First Engineering & Agents Bring strong insight into AI trends, AI-assisted engineering, intelligent automation, and agent-based capabilities. Drive adoption of AI tools and practices to improve software design, development, testing, documentation, troubleshooting, and operational workflows. Identify opportunities to leverage AI and agents within the engineering lifecycle and product ecosystem to improve productivity, quality, and customer value. Guide teams on responsible AI usage, including security, privacy, governance, explainability, and reliability considerations. Evaluate AI-enabled platforms, developer tools, observability assistants, coding agents, and automation frameworks that can improve engineering outcomes at scale. Database & Data Architecture Provide technical leadership in database design, data modeling, query optimization, transaction management, and scalable data access patterns. Work with relational and non-relational database technologies to support enterprise-grade application requirements. Guide teams in designing reliable, performant, and maintainable database solutions that support high-volume data processing and business-critical workflows. Lead troubleshooting of complex database performance issues, including indexing, locking, query plans, connection management, data partitioning, and schema evolution. Ensure data architecture decisions align with security, compliance, scalability, performance, and long-term maintainability goals. Security, Compliance & Enterprise Readiness Champion secure software design and development practices across the product. Ensure systems are designed with strong consideration for authentication, authorization, data protection, encryption, auditability, and secure integration patterns. Promote enterprise readiness through resilient architecture, operational maturity, compliance awareness, and high-quality engineering standards. Partner with security, architecture, and platform teams to ensure technical solutions align with organizational governance and risk management expectations. Technical Mentorship & Influence Mentor senior engineers, technical leads, and development teams on architecture, design, engineering practices, troubleshooting, and technical decision-making. Lead technical discussions with clarity, influence, and strong engineering judgment. Build consensus across teams on complex architecture and design decisions. Raise engineering standards through design reviews, technical coaching, documentation, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement. Act as a trusted technical advisor to engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 16+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant experience building enterprise-scale software products. Strong proficiency in Java, including modern Java frameworks, backend service development, concurrency, performance tuning, and scalable application design. Deep experience with database technologies, including relational databases, SQL optimization, schema design, transaction management, indexing strategies, and performance troubleshooting. Proven experience designing and building large-scale distributed systems, microservices, APIs, and cloud-native enterprise applications. Strong understanding of observability platforms, monitoring, logging, tracing, metrics, alerting, and production diagnostics. Hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP. Experience with performance engineering, including profiling, load testing, capacity planning, caching, query optimization, and system tuning. Strong understanding of enterprise SaaS architecture, operational readiness, resiliency, availability, security, and scalability. Demonstrated ability to lead architecture discussions, define technical roadmaps, and influence engineering direction across multiple teams. Experience troubleshooting complex technical issues across application, infrastructure, database, and integration layers. Strong understanding of AI-assisted software engineering practices, AI tools, and emerging agent-based development or automation models. Excellent communication, collaboration, mentoring, and technical leadership skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience working on large-scale enterprise SaaS products serving global customers. Experience defining or evolving a product-level technology stack and long-term technical roadmap. Expertise with Kubernetes, containers, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps practices, and Infrastructure as Code. Experience with event-driven architecture, messaging platforms, distributed caching, and asynchronous processing patterns. Hands-on experience with observability tools such as OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Prometheus, Kibana, Splunk, Datadog, or similar platforms. Experience leading platform modernization, cloud transformation, or large-scale architecture evolution initiatives. Strong knowledge of secure software development, compliance-aware design, and enterprise integration patterns. Experience with AI coding assistants, engineering agents, intelligent automation, or AI-enabled operational tooling. Demonstrated ability to mentor senior technical talent and establish engineering standards across teams. Ability to balance strategic architecture vision with hands-on technical problem solving and delivery execution. Key Attributes Strategic technical thinker with strong execution discipline. Hands-on engineering leader who can guide architecture while also diving deep into technical issues. Strong enterprise mindset with focus on reliability, performance, observability, scalability, and security. Clear communicator who can lead technical discussions and influence decisions across teams. Passionate about engineering excellence, innovation, AI-first development, and continuous improvement. Comfortable working in complex environments with multiple stakeholders, systems, and priorities. With the world's largest collection of workforce insights, and people-first AI, our ability to reveal unseen ways to build trust, amplify productivity, and empower talent, is unmatched. It's this expertise that equips our customers with the intelligence to solve any challenge in any industry — because great organizations know their workforce is their competitive edge. By joining the global BC (Cross-Programme) organization as a founding member of the newly created Airbus PM Office in India , you will play a pivotal role in operating projects, programmes, portfolios, and performance management to enable efficient decision-making and execution with a high level of PM standard. We are looking for passionate talent, whether you want to develop your Project Management skills toward seniority or are an experienced PM Expert ready to mentor and innovate , to help us reshape the future of Aircraft programmes through PM excellence . Driven by an entrepreneurial mindset and our Vision 2028 ambition to build an autonomous, high-performing PM Team in India, our mission rests on three core pillars: Driving PM Excellence & Global Competitiveness : Enabling strategic impact and operational standards locally. Delivering Smart PM Digital Ecosystem: Deploying data-driven solutions and optimizing cost structures. Ensuring Seamless PMBP Experience & Beyond: Simplifying ways of working across Airbus India and broader BC activities. In this role, you will be directly embedded in the ERP Transformation Program , one of Airbus’s most strategic enterprise initiatives, and the Digital PM Office (BCXX). We are modernizing and simplifying our legacy landscape of over 110 SAP instances, shifting to a standardized, Clean Core S/4HANA Cloud platform. Our ambition is to turn our ERP into a high-velocity engine powered by embedded AI, advanced analytics, and real-time data continuity. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to harmonize end-to-end business processes, deploy reusable assets, and drive structured governance across a global portfolio of execution projects. As a PM specialist within this programme, you will co-pilot critical operations, streamline execution routines, and help pave the way for the future of digital operations at Airbus. Come sharpen your craft, unleash your potential, and build the future with us! About the Role Are you passionate about turning project data into strategic business value? In this role, you will provide autonomous project management support across complex initiatives. By delivering and analyzing integrated schedules, budgets, and risk profiles, you will deliver predictive performance insights that optimize project delivery. The Project Management Business Partner (PMBP) is an execution-focused PM specialist embedded within project teams to drive day-to-day project performance. Accountable for maintaining project schedule baselines, generating real-time performance dashboards, tracking risks, and enforcing standardized PM methods, the PMBP bridges technical project execution with strategic business objectives Key Accountabilities & Main Responsibilities Project Execution & Operational Support: Provide expert project management support across complex initiatives to secure baseline execution: daily project schedule structures, resource loading, and cost monitoring in accordance with Airbus PM standards (e.g., MP.PP.01/02). Maintain Top-Down / Bottom-Up planning synchronization within single-source-of-truth systems. Track milestone maturity, quality gates, and deliverables against time, cost, quality, and performance target Performance Management & Data Analytics: Define, develop, and maintain integrated PM dashboards and project status reports for internal stakeholders. Leverage data analytics to perform data sanity checks, monitor planning adherence, and proactively flag potential project delays before they occur. Secure Planisware data integrity as the Single Source of Truth Core PM Governance & Risk Tracking: Facilitate project routines, steering meetings, risk reviews, and decision-making workshops. Execute Risk & Opportunity management processes (ARM), log mitigation action plans, and maintain project registers. Support the capture of lessons learned and process improvement feedback loops. Process Standardization & AI Adoption: Promote a "Digital-First" mindset by actively identifying repetitive PM tasks for automation. Utilize AI tools to summarize technical alignment meetings, draft executive status updates, and track operational action items. Dimensions Team Leadership: Individual contributor role; coordinates project work packages, cross-functional contributors, and local subcontractor task units. Stakeholder Network: Direct operational interfaces with Project Leaders, Engineers, Domain Experts and Transnational Project Contributors. Scope: Dedicated support to specific project work packages or domain portfolios Desired skills and qualifications Educated to a Degree level in Business Administration, Engineering, Project Management, or an equivalent field. Solid professional experience 3 to 5+ years in applied project management across traditional Waterfall and Agile environments. Explicit S/4HANA Migration Track Record: Add a mandatory or strongly preferred requirement for 3+ years of direct experience in SAP S/4HANA transformation projects Clean Core & Cloud Architecture Familiarity: Require working knowledge of SAP S/4HANA Cloud / Clean Core principles, including SAP BTP (Business Technology Platform), SAP Activate Methodology, and extensibility frameworks. SAP Module & Data Mapping Experience: Include experience with legacy SAP ERP (ECC 6.0) data migration, business process re-engineering, and harmonizing multi-instance landscapes. Proven experience with enterprise scheduling tools for baseline control, resource planning, and schedule tracking. Proficiency in analyzing operational data using advanced platforms and dedicated dashboarding tools. Excellent stakeholder engagement and negotiation skills with fluent English language Proficiency. Certifications : PM Certification (Iron / Bronze) or PMI-PMP is preferred. Agile/SAFe certifications are highly valued. SAP S/4HANA certifications as highly valued is preferred. SAP Activate Project Manager Certification is highly valued Competencies : PM Processes, Methods & Tools (Advanced) PM Operations (Advanced) Project Management Fundamentals (Advanced) Integrative Project Planning (Advanced) Risk & Opportunity Management Execution (Advanced) Stakeholder Management (Advanced) Soft Skills : High adaptability, structured thinking, proactive problem-solving, active listening, and strong workshop facilitation capabilities. Languages : Fluent / Negotiation level English (mandatory). German, French is a plus Technical Stack & Tooling Core PM Workplace: Planisware (E7 / Enterprise), Zoho, Agility Data Analytics & Ecosystem: Palantir (Skywise), Qlik Sense Risk & Opportunities: ARM (Active Risk Manager) Collaboration & Automation: Google Workspace, Gemini AI Your Benefits Challenging tasks and unique high-tech products and services Good work-life balance in a big international company Actively lived values "We are one", diversity really matters On-the-job trainings for personal development and technical skills Mentoring programmes Flexible working hours and working time compensation Home office is possible Compatibility of family and career Attractive salary and company benefits Your Location Site-based position with hybrid working options This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth. This information will only be used by Airbus. Airbus is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief. Airbus is, and always has been, committed to equal opportunities for all. As such, we will never ask for any type of monetary exchange in the frame of a recruitment process. jobs.title: Senior Android Developer
jobs.description: As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you. About the Role: Join CrowdStrike's IT Go-to-Market team as an Android Developer and build the mobile applications that empower our sales and partner teams to stop breaches worldwide. You'll maintain and enhance business-critical Android apps used daily by our partners, working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment where your code directly impacts how we serve our customers. This role offers the opportunity to solve complex technical challenges, implement cutting-edge Android technologies, and grow your expertise with a leader in cybersecurity. What You’ll Do: Design, develop, and maintain Android applications with a focus on performance, security, responsiveness, and exceptional user experience Collaborate cross-functionally with business analysts, alliances/channel team, backend engineers, and stakeholders to conceptualize, scope, and deliver new features and enhancements Write clean, maintainable code following Kotlin best practices, design patterns, and architectural principles (MVVM, Clean Architecture, MVI, etc.) Conduct comprehensive testing including unit tests, instrumentation tests, UI tests (Espresso), and debugging to ensure applications meet CrowdStrike's quality and security standards Optimize application performance for speed, memory efficiency, and compatibility across Android devices, screen sizes, and OS versions Participate actively in code reviews, providing constructive feedback and mentoring team members to elevate code quality Troubleshoot and resolve complex issues related to app performance, crashes, ANRs (Application Not Responding), functionality, and third-party integrations Integrate with backend services using RESTful APIs, ensuring secure and efficient data communication Stay current with Android ecosystem updates (Jetpack Compose, Kotlin Coroutines, Flow, Hilt), Material Design guidelines, and industry best practices to drive continuous improvement Contribute to technical planning, including effort estimation, sprint planning, and architectural decisions What You’ll Need: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or similar work experience A minimum of 5+ years of progressively responsible experience in a directly related area, during which both technical and professional capabilities have been clearly demonstrated. Strong proficiency in Kotlin with hands-on experience using Android SDK, Jetpack (Compose, ViewModel, LiveData, Room, Navigation) Platform knowledge of activity/fragment lifecycle, intents, services and broadcast receivers. Knowledge of permissions, background tasks and notifications. Experience with Gradle build system, Android Studio and Google Play Store provisioning and signing Experience with Salesforce concepts such as Lightning Web Components (LWC), Salesforce platform capabilities and integration patterns and the ability to create responsive and accessible UI components highly preferred Bonus points for familiarity with Jira, Coupa, MuleSoft and Salesforce Experience Cloud Ability to work independently, and as a team player, while using discretion in decision making and sound judgment in problem solving. Must have excellent analytics, organizations, problem-solving, interpersonal and communication skills, both written and oral, possess the ability and desire to quickly learn new skills and technologies. Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes. Benefits of Working at CrowdStrike: Market leader in compensation and equity awards Competitive vacation policy Paid parental leave, including adoption Flexible work environment Wellness programs Shift time - 2:00 PM - 11:00 PM IST LI-RM2 Benefits of Working at CrowdStrike: Market leader in compensation and equity awards Comprehensive physical and mental wellness programs Competitive vacation and holidays for recharge Paid parental and adoption leaves Professional development opportunities for all employees regardless of level or role Employee Networks, geographic neighborhood groups, and volunteer opportunities to build connections Vibrant office culture with world class amenities Great Place to Work Certified™ across the globe CrowdStrike is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. If the answer to these questions is yes, we would like to talk with you. ConvergeCONSUMER™ is a product-driven business that combines differentiated consumer insights with robust prediction and optimization capabilities to help consumer-focused businesses improve decision-making and deliver personalized experiences to drive growth, consumer loyalty, and profitability. We operate with the speed and agility of a startup within the world’s largest professional services firm. We drive value for our clients by optimizing decisions and actions at a level of granularity only made possible with today’s data and technology. ConvergeCONSUMER’s suite of solutions helps consumer-facing businesses prosper in a world being re-shaped by convergence, where the lines between industries, competitors and collaborators, consumers and suppliers, and even human and artificial intelligence have blurred. Our approach for addressing this complexity is simple: we combine Deloitte’s next-generation technology platforms with decades of experience in the consumer sector and a deep understanding of its unique issues and challenges to drive profitability and future growth for our clients. This role requires both technical fluency in data engineering and an analytical mindset capable of assessing data quality and real-world representativeness. jobs.title: Senior Privacy Engineer – Automation & Data Mapping
jobs.description: Job Description The Senior Privacy Operations Engineer bridges privacy compliance and technical implementation, architecting, building, and maintaining the tooling, automation, and data infrastructure that powers the company’s global privacy program across UK/EU, US, APAC, and other regions. This role works closely with engineering and product teams to operationalize privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default requirements, and owns the technical backbone connecting privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust), work-management systems (e.g., Azure DevOps, Jira), and the organization’s broader data and cloud infrastructure. This is a senior, hands-on engineering role requiring both strong technical depth and working knowledge of global privacy regulatory concepts. Key Responsibilities Privacy Automation Engineering Design, build, and maintain automation for privacy operations workflows, including data subject rights fulfillment, data discovery, data mapping, and privacy assessment triggering. Build and maintain API and Power Automate integrations between privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust) and internal systems (ticketing/ADO/Jira, identity, data stores), including field mapping, assignment logic, bi-directional status sync, and error handling/logging so systems do not drift apart. Implement risk-based conditional logic and trigger workflows for privacy assessments (PIAs/DPIAs/TIAs) tied to intake or procurement systems, including escalation paths for high-risk triggers and governance/audit trails over the trigger rules themselves. Design and maintain automated redaction and exception-flagging pipelines (e.g., keyword/pattern matching, ML classifiers) for DSAR fulfillment, ensuring a mandatory human-review checkpoint before release and maintaining an audit log of redaction decisions. Data Mapping & ROPA Infrastructure Build and maintain an automated, event-driven data flow inventory and data mapping pipeline, tied to system/vendor intake and procurement processes rather than periodic manual surveys. Build and maintain integrations with data discovery and classification tooling (e.g., OneTrust Data Discovery, BigID, Collibra, AWS Macie, Azure Purview, database crawlers) to automatically feed classifications and data flows into ROPA records. Implement drift-detection mechanisms that reconcile ROPA records against discovery/mapping tool outputs, and support metrics such as percentage of ROPA records reviewed within a defined window. Support technical aspects of privacy impact assessments, including data flow diagrams and system/architecture review. Privacy-by-Design Engineering & Product Collaboration Partner with engineering and product teams to implement privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default controls within products and internal systems. Assist in the technical implementation of data retention and deletion requirements across structured and unstructured data sources. Advise engineering teams on technical architecture considerations for new products and features from a privacy and data protection perspective. Program Tooling, Reporting & Observability Build and maintain KPI dashboards and reporting pipelines (e.g., ADO Analytics, Power BI) that translate raw work-item and automation data into executive-ready privacy program metrics (DSAR SLA compliance, assessment backlog, incident response times). Monitor and report on the health of privacy tooling and automated processes, troubleshooting integration or data-quality issues as they arise. Maintain governance over report definitions and automation/trigger rule changes so metrics and workflows remain consistent and trustworthy over time. DSAR & Assessment Automation at Scale Design and maintain automated routing of DSAR tasks with data-owner mapping across multiple systems, SLA tracking tied to statutory deadlines, and tiered escalation as deadlines approach. Build scalable automation and surge-capacity mechanisms (triage automation, templated responses) to support DSAR volume spikes, incorporating lessons learned into ongoing process improvements. Support automation of assessment intake quality, including conditional required fields, real-time validation, and automated reminders to reduce incomplete submissions. Required Qualifications 5-7 years of experience in a data engineering, software engineering, or technical privacy/compliance engineering role, ideally supporting privacy or compliance operations at a global or multinational organization. This is a product role, not a project role. The Senior Product Owner owns the vision, the backlog and the outcomes — deciding what gets built and why, in what order, and being accountable for whether it actually improved anything. Success is measured in adoption, effort saved and experience improved, not in tickets closed or features shipped. The role sits between three constituencies that rarely agree: employees who want their devices to just work, Security who want them locked down, and Finance who want them cheaper. Turning that tension into a prioritised, defensible backlog is the core of the job. Key Responsibilities Own and articulate the product vision for end user services and mobile device management — a clear statement of what the service will be in 18 months and why that matters to the business. Maintain a rolling roadmap that balances new capability, technical debt, security and compliance obligations, and experience improvement; keep it honest about capacity. Translate the EUC strategy and architecture direction into a sequenced, deliverable product backlog. Own the business case and benefits realisation for product investment; be accountable for the value claimed, not just the spend approved. Own, refine and prioritise the product backlog as the single source of truth for the squad; make prioritisation calls transparently and defend them. Write clear user stories and acceptance criteria that engineers can build from and testers can verify — specific about the outcome, not prescriptive about the solution. Lead sprint planning, refinement, review and retrospective alongside the Scrum Master; accept or reject work against acceptance criteria. Manage dependencies across adjacent squads — identity, security, networking, service management — and escalate early when they threaten delivery. Own the release and change approach for user-visible change, including pilot rings, communications and rollback triggers. Be the voice of the employee in every prioritisation conversation, and hold the evidence to back it: research, telemetry, ticket analysis and direct observation. Run continuous discovery — user interviews, shadowing in the field and on the shop floor, surveys, usability testing — with the populations who are least like head office. Convert digital experience (DEX) telemetry and service desk data into prioritised, root-cause-addressing backlog items; treat every recurring ticket category as a product defect until proven otherwise. Own adoption: define what good adoption looks like before launch, measure it after, and act when it does not materialise. Own the product for the mobile estate: enrolment and provisioning experience, BYOD vs. corporate-owned models, app catalogue and distribution, and the employee-facing side of mobile security policy. Own the BYOD proposition end to end — the privacy commitment, the employee terms, the enrolment journey and the trust that makes people willing to participate. Manage the mobile OS release cycle as a recurring product event: annual iOS and Android major releases, beta assessment, compatibility validation and controlled rollout. Own the product relationship with mobile carriers, MDM platform vendors and app suppliers. Build and maintain relationships across business units, regions and functions; run a stakeholder forum or product council that makes trade-offs visible rather than fought in private. Partner with Cyber Security to land control changes in ways employees will accept and comply with — security outcomes delivered through good product design rather than mandate. Engage works councils, employee representatives and Privacy where mobile telemetry, BYOD or device monitoring is in scope. Report on product performance to senior stakeholders in outcome terms. Professional Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline, or equivalent demonstrable professional experience. Product ownership certifications desirable (e.g., Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO), SAFe POPM, Professional Scrum Product Owner (PSPO), ITIL v4 Foundation, Microsoft Endpoint Administrator Associate). Area of Specialisation Product ownership at scale for end user services and mobile device management, with direct working familiarity with an enterprise MDM/UEM platform (e.g., Microsoft Intune). Mobile estate strategy across iOS and Android, corporate-owned and BYOD, standard knowledge-worker devices and specialised field, clinical, lab and manufacturing devices. Digital employee experience (DEX) and service-desk-driven product improvement, using telemetry and ticket analysis to prioritise root-cause fixes. Related Experience Required Overall 15 years and 12+ years in technology delivery, including 5+ years as a Product Owner or Product Manager with genuine backlog authority (not a business analyst writing another team's requirements). Product or service ownership serving 10,000+ users across multiple countries. Demonstrable hands-on product experience in end user computing, digital workplace or mobile device management — including direct familiarity with an enterprise MDM/UEM platform. Sustained experience owning a backlog for a cross-functional agile squad, through multiple release cycles, in a scaled delivery environment. Track record of using user research and quantitative telemetry to drive prioritisation, with a specific example of a decision the data changed. A demonstrable product outcome delivered and measured — adoption, experience, effort or cost — not merely a feature shipped. Proven ability to manage senior and conflicting stakeholders across business units and regions, and to hold a prioritisation decision under pressure. Fluent English; credible with both engineers and executives in a global matrixed organisation. Willingness to travel internationally, approximately [10–15]% of the time — including to sites, labs and field locations where the devices are actually used. Desirable: Experience in a regulated industry — pharmaceutical, life sciences, biotech, financial services or healthcare — including GxP-validated systems and the change control that comes with them. Product ownership for specialised or frontline mobile devices: rugged handhelds, lab and clinical devices, field-force tablets, shared/kiosk devices, scanners and shop-floor endpoints. Experience with deskless and frontline worker populations — employees without a corporate laptop, whose primary device is shared or personal. Works council and employee-representation engagement, particularly on BYOD, mobile telemetry and device monitoring. Mobile app product experience — internal app store curation, in-house mobile app lifecycle, MAM policy design. Experience delivering a major platform migration or transition as a product owner — MDM platform change, MSP transition, or BYOD programme launch. Service design or UX research background; journey mapping and service blueprinting. Carrier and telecom management — mobile contracts, eSIM, international roaming, expense management. AI-enabled workplace tooling product experience — Copilot, virtual agents, AI-assisted support deflection. Accessibility and assistive technology as a designed-in part of the device proposition. Sustainability — device longevity, refurbishment and circular IT built into the product roadmap. Skills/Background Deep product craft across backlog ownership, outcome-based requirements, continuous discovery, and value definition and measurement. Endpoint management platform fluency (Microsoft Intune or comparable MDM/UEM tooling) — enough to have credible conversations with engineers and challenge estimates. jobs.title: Sr Software Engineer - Engineer
jobs.description: About the role and team At Uber, AI agents are increasingly writing, reviewing, testing, and debugging code in production. They deliver high-quality results efficiently, without wasting tokens, only when they understand Uber's codebases. The AI Context Engineering team builds the context foundation that every software-development AI agent at Uber relies on: AI Context Graph: a unified graph of services, ownership, domain entities, and business flows Code Graph: a graph representation of Uber's monorepos built for agents to consume AI-Generated Documentation: documentation that stays fresh as code changes Agentic Memory: a memory layer that lets agents learn across sessions As a Senior Software Engineer, you will own major parts of this platform end to end. You'll take them from prototype to production at monorepo scale, and work with partner teams to integrate foundational context products with the agents running in production for workflows such as root-cause analysis, code authoring, test planning, and library upgrades, etc What will you do Context Graph and Ontology: Enrich the graph with new entity types, such as data streams, metrics, and observability signals, and link them to code so agents can reason across systems. Code Graph Infrastructure: Build and scale code graphs across multiple monorepos and microrepos, covering symbols, call edges, dependencies, and links between code and tests. Add incremental updates, versioned (historical) graphs, and function-level embeddings, and serve the graphs to agents with low latency through local and remote interfaces. AI-Generated Documentation: Extend automated documentation from backend services to mobile (screens, UI components), libraries, and data pipelines. Use refresh strategies that keep context current as code changes. Agentic Memory: Design the memory layer that lets agents persist and reuse decisions, past fixes, and team preferences across sessions. Standards and Governance: Define and roll out standards for agent instruction files (AGENTS.md), including structure, content, and token budget, and generate them systematically across modules. Context Quality Evaluation: Build continuous evals that measure the accuracy and freshness of every context product, and run A/B experiments that prove the impact on agent outcomes. Tooling and Integration: Build MCP servers, skills, and tools that deliver context to agents. Partner with AI Platform, Developer Experience, and product teams to integrate them into production workflows. Technical Leadership: Drive design reviews, mentor engineers, and turn ambiguous problems into well-scoped, measurable projects What will you need Experience: 8+ years of software engineering experience building production systems, with a degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Programming: Strong in Go, Java, or Python, writing clean, well-tested, maintainable code. LLMs and Agentic Systems: Hands-on experience building with LLMs and agents, including prompt and context design, tool use, and retrieval, and a good sense of what context makes agents succeed or fail. Code Understanding: Experience with static analysis, ASTs, parsers such as tree-sitter, or build and dependency systems in large codebases. Data at Scale: Experience building reliable data pipelines and working with graph or other large-scale data stores. Emerging Protocols: Familiarity with MCP and agent-to-agent protocols and how to apply them. Problem Solving: Strong analytical skills and a habit of measuring outcomes, not just shipping features. Success Metrics More agentic workflows use curated context in production, with a measured improvement in each workflow's business metric, such as accuracy, cost, latency, or CI time. Agents provide higher-quality, better-grounded answers while using fewer tokens and tool calls than when they rediscover context from scratch. Context coverage grows across languages, repos, and entity types, with measurable accuracy and freshness. Bonus Points If you have Graph Databases: Experience with Neo4j or similar graph databases, including query optimization and schema design. Embeddings and RAG: Experience with embedding generation, vector databases, and retrieval pipelines. Evaluation: Experience designing LLM evals, LLM-as-judge methods, or A/B experiments for AI systems. Developer Platforms: Experience in developer tooling, CI, or monorepo infrastructure. Observability: Experience with Prometheus, Grafana, Langfuse, or similar tools for monitoring AI systems. Ready to Ride? This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook — it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves — we'd love to hear from you. You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits. Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. If you bring deep experience building production services and have started building with LLMs, we'd love to Roles & Responsibilities Architect and build the tool-calling layer that powers our agents: wrap internal services, data platforms, and external APIs as well-defined tools with clear schemas, contracts, and permissions. Engineer reliable tool execution at scale, including parallel and chained tool calls, timeouts, retries, idempotency, error recovery, and graceful handling of tool failures or bad model outputs. Develop high-performance Python backend services for LLM orchestration, covering async job handling, streaming responses, caching, rate limiting, and distributed workflows supporting high-throughput Gen AI operations. Engineer state, memory, and context management subsystems so agents can maintain session continuity across long, multi-step, tool-heavy interactions. Architect multi-agent and skills-based agent systems using frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or similar, enabling autonomous reasoning, tool use, inter-agent coordination, and adaptive decision-making at enterprise scale. Build observability for agent behavior, including end-to-end tracing of tool calls, measuring tool-selection accuracy, and debugging multi-step agent runs in production. Build retrieval systems (RAG and Graph-RAG) where agents need grounded knowledge, using vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, pgvector, OpenSearch) and knowledge graphs (e.g., Neo4j, AWS Neptune). Establish LLMOps and MLOps pipelines on Databricks (AWS), covering MLflow, prompt and agent evaluation, model lineage tracking, CI/CD, and monitoring. Design multimodal generative AI pipelines that unify text, image, tabular, and graph data using modern transformer-based and foundation models. Guide fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and alignment strategies (e.g., PEFT, LoRA, instruction tuning, RLHF) to adapt foundation models for specialized enterprise use cases, working closely with ML specialists. Implement Responsible AI practices, including hallucination mitigation, bias detection, output safety guardrails, explainability, and compliance with data ethics standards. Evaluate and productionize advances in agentic AI, multimodal models, and frontier foundation models, benchmarking them against enterprise performance and safety requirements. Lead, mentor, and grow a team of engineers, and set the engineering standard for Gen AI development across the program. On this platform, agents make extensive tool calls into enterprise services and APIs and must run securely, reliably, and at scale. You'll set the standards teams build on across tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, self-correcting agents, memory, retrieval, and LLMOps. You'll also make the key decisions on models, platforms, and trade-offs. Working closely with engineering, product, security, and business leaders, you'll shape the long-term direction of Gen AI across B&MI and mentor architects and senior engineers. You'll also stay hands-on with prototypes that de-risk big bets. The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale. If you've solved them as a backend or distributed systems architect and have started applying that experience to LLM systems, we'd love to hear from you. Roles & Responsibilities Own the architecture and technical roadmap for the Operational Intelligence Gen AI platform, defining reference architectures and standards that teams across the program can reuse and scale. Architect the enterprise tool-calling layer, setting standards for how internal services, data platforms, and external APIs are exposed to agents as tools. This covers schemas, contracts, versioning, access control, and resilient execution (parallel and chained calls, retries, timeouts, idempotency, circuit breakers, and fallbacks). Set the architecture for multi-agent and skills-based agent systems (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen), including when to use agents versus deterministic workflows and how agents coordinate, delegate, and share context. Design self-correcting agent patterns: tool critics and verifiers that check tool selection, arguments, and results, plus reflection and plan-and-execute loops that catch errors before agents act or respond. Architect agent memory and state for long-running, multi-step sessions, including short- and long-term memory (e.g., Mem0, Zep, LangGraph memory), session persistence, and memory scoping and retention. Define retrieval architecture for grounded reasoning, including Self-RAG, Corrective RAG (CRAG), adaptive retrieval, and Graph-RAG, built on vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, pgvector, OpenSearch) and knowledge graphs (e.g., Neo4j, AWS Neptune). Design the inference and orchestration layer for high throughput, covering async processing, streaming, caching, rate limiting, and model routing across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and open-source models. Establish the LLMOps architecture on Databricks (AWS), including MLflow, CI/CD for prompts and agents, and model lineage. Set platform-wide evaluation and observability standards: end-to-end tracing of tool calls, tool-selection accuracy, task success rates, cost, and latency. Build security and Responsible AI into the architecture, including guardrails, prompt-injection defenses, hallucination mitigation, data privacy, and audit trails that meet Mastercard's data ethics and regulatory standards. Own key architecture decisions and trade-offs, such as build versus buy, model and vendor selection, and cost versus latency versus accuracy, documented through architecture decision records. Assess emerging models, frameworks, and standards such as MCP for production readiness. Lead design reviews and partner with engineering, product, security, and data teams to align on architecture and raise the engineering bar across the program. Stay hands-on, building prototypes and reference implementations that de-risk decisions and give teams a working starting point. All About You Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, AI/ML, or Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Significant experience architecting large-scale distributed systems in production, including microservices, event-driven systems, data platforms, and cloud-native infrastructure. Deep expertise in API design and systems integration, including contracts, security models, and reliability patterns for services consumed by many teams. You understand what changes when the consumer is an LLM. Hands-on experience designing and shipping LLM-powered systems in production, especially agents that use tool/function calling, memory, and retrieval, and a clear view of how they fail. Strong Python skills for hands-on prototyping (async programming, FastAPI or similar), plus SQL proficiency. Deep experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS preferred; Azure or GCP welcome), including its AI services such as Bedrock, SageMaker, Azure OpenAI, or Vertex AI. A solid grounding in security, privacy, and compliance for enterprise systems, ideally in financial services or another regulated industry. The ability to influence without authority, aligning engineering, product, and leadership around a technical direction and explaining trade-offs in business terms. Nice to have: hands-on experience with tool critics, Self-RAG, CRAG, reflection loops, memory frameworks such as Mem0 or Zep, MCP tool servers, or agent evaluation frameworks. Nice to have: exposure to fine-tuning (LoRA, PEFT, RLHF), multimodal models, or knowledge graphs. Coming from backend or distributed systems architecture? The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale, and you've solved them before. If you've started applying that experience to LLM systems, we want to hear from you, even if you haven't used every tool listed here. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II who is a strong, independent builder with growing design maturity. jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Amazon’s global fulfilment network enables any merchant in any of the geography ship items that you order on Amazon, to any place on earth. Amazon Logistics’ (AMZL) delivery stations (DS) receive packages from Fulfilment Centers (FCs) and Sort Centers (SCs) and sort them to route level. Drivers come into the DS and pick up the packages for their route and deliver them to Amazon’s customers. This operation is also called the “Last Mile”. An integral component in the Last Mile ecosystem are Amazon's WW delivery hubs where packages are received, sorted and prepared for on-road delivery. Station Tech team, in Last Mile, is responsible for building scalable tools and technology for delivery hubs that scale across multiple programs and businesses including Amazon Logistics (AMZL), Global Specialty Fulfilment (GSF), to increase associate productivity, site throughput, and operational quality and scalability of our delivery network. Our primary customers are delivery station associates (our actual on-ground rockstars who sort millions of packages a day), station managers (who manage Amazon hubs WW to ensure customer promises are met), COs (central operations team who supervise stations across regions) and on-road delivery agents (drivers who sail through all obstacles to get your packages at your doorstep). The team build tools and process which guide our customers to reduce their cognitive load, eliminate decision points to drive standardisation, prioritise work to focus on the highest impact tasks, and take steps for correcting operational defects to reduce the impact of human error and meet our customer SLAs. UTR Tech is an organisation within Last Mile supporting all the delivery stations in the delivery network. A delivery station receives an input set of packages from upstream and performs the required set of operations and processes on the packages to ultimately get them out of the delivery stations for on-road delivery. The associates within the delivery stations use a mobile based application called Dolphin for running the execution operations. As an SDE II on the UTR Tech team, you'll build and scale the systems powering Amazon's fastest delivery promises - Same-Day Delivery (SSD), Grocery, and Rush (1-hr/3-hr) programs across NA, EU, JP, and the Middle East. You'll own services spanning package injection, staging, sortation, and routing that keep millions of time-critical orders on-time, and directly move quality metrics like slot-level DEA and defect BPS. This role blends deep technical ownership with high operational impact: your code runs in a live, sub-hour delivery network where reliability and latency are non-negotiable. You'll partner with product, science, and operations to launch new speed programs and expand grocery (including perishable/chill-chain) into new regions. We're looking for an engineer who thrives on distributed-systems challenges at scale and wants their work to be visible to customers the same day. Key job responsibilities As an Engineer in the team, you will take part in in the architecture, design, implementation and deployment of large-scale and complex software systems. You will get to leverage your experience and expertise to deliver innovative solutions to challenging problems. You will communicate your ideas effectively to achieve the right outcome for your team and customer. You enjoy collaborating with others to increase the effectiveness of the overall team. Your code, design, and implementation decisions should set a great example to other engineers. You will also have the opportunity to impact the technical decisions in the broader organization as well as mentor other engineers in the team. What You'll Do Design, build and maintain highly available, scalable and secure infrastructure on AWS . Build automation to reduce manual operational effort and improve engineering productivity. Design, develop and manage robust CI/CD pipelines for application and infrastructure deployments. Drive Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automation-first engineering practices. Troubleshoot complex production issues across AWS infrastructure, Linux, networking, applications and deployment pipelines . Create and maintain architecture documentation, operational runbooks and engineering best practices. What We're Looking For 8–12 years of hands-on experience in DevOps, AWS Cloud Engineering, Platform Engineering, SRE or similar engineering roles. Strong hands-on experience designing and operating infrastructure on Amazon Web Services (AWS) . Experience with AWS services and capabilities such as: EC2 EBS S3 VPC and VPC Endpoints Transit Gateway Security Groups and NACLs AWS CodePipeline AWS CodeBuild Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting skills, including process management, memory, file systems, system performance and shell scripting. Solid understanding of networking fundamentals , including TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, routing, load balancing, firewalls and VPN concepts. Strong scripting or programming skills in at least one of Python, Go, Java or Bash . Hands-on experience building and managing CI/CD pipelines and a good understanding of modern software delivery practices. Experience with GitHub Actions for build and deployment automation. Strong production troubleshooting, debugging and root-cause analysis capabilities. Experience building reusable automation or self-service tooling. Strong communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across engineering teams. Good to Have Hands-on experience with Terraform and/or AWS CloudFormation . Experience with containers and orchestration technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes and Amazon EKS . Experience with monitoring and observability platforms such as AWS CloudWatch, Grafana, Prometheus or Datadog . Experience with configuration management tools such as Ansible . Understanding of AWS cloud security and infrastructure security best practices. AWS certification(s). What Will Make You Successful in This Role You are someone who: Thinks automation first and looks for opportunities to engineer manual work out of the system. Has a strong builder mindset and enjoys solving difficult infrastructure problems. Takes ownership of production systems rather than simply operating them. Capability to delve into details and explain the importance of each activity to team members. Keeping all stakeholders updated on task progress. Ensuring adherence to processes throughout the lifecycle. Ownership of responsibility for code quality, application security, functionality, and code performance. Designing, coding, and debugging products and features. Analyzing and resolving technical queries from the team. Collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams such as Product Management, Business Development, and Operations. Working with frontend engineers to implement features. Designing appropriate solutions/architecture for products/features based on requirements, estimating efforts, and managing development. Managing and enhancing systems by innovating and implementing best practices. jobs.description: Job Summary AI Evaluation & Observability Architect(CoE)- The AI Evaluation & Observability Architect makes AI systems measurable, reliable, and safe to run in production. The role designs the full evaluation lifecycle (offline and online evaluations, ground truth, golden datasets, deterministic and LLM-as-judge scoring) and turns it into enforceable engineering controls: regression gates, observability, SLOs, and resilience patterns. It also provides Responsible AI assurance and packages everything into reusable evaluation assets and production-readiness scorecards that Solutions and Advisory teams apply to client engagements. The role is a hands-on, Al-native engineer-architect who uses agent harnesses in daily delivery and sets the quality bar for how the organization ships AI. Design offline/online evaluations, ground truth, golden datasets, deterministic and LLM-as-judge scoring, regression gates, observability, SLOs, resilience and Responsible AI assurance; create reusable evaluation assets and production-readiness scorecards. Mandatory across all roles: practical AI-native engineering; strong modern application development; cloud-native, API, microservices and DevSecOps grounding; hands-on experience with at least one agent harness such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Kiro or Cursor; enterprise security, governance, evaluation, observability and cost awareness. Key Responsibilities A. Evaluation Strategy & Design • Define evaluation strategy per use case: what "good" means, which dimensions matter (accuracy, groundedness, relevance, safety, tone, latency, cost), and how each is measured. Design offline evaluations (pre-release benchmarks, experiment comparison, model/prompt/retrieval variants) and online evaluations (shadow testing, A/B tests, canary releases, user feedback loops, production sampling). • Cover the full AI system stack: LLM calls, RAG/GraphRAGretrieva1, tool use, multi-step agents, and end-to-end workflows. B. Ground Truth & Golden Datasets Build and govern ground truth and golden datasets: sourcing, labeling guidelines, subject-matter-expert review, inter-annotator agreement, versioning, and coverage Of edge cases and adversarial inputs. • Generate and curate synthetic test data responsibly, with human validation and bias checks. Maintain dataset lifecycle: drift detection, refresh cadence, and protection against test- set leakage and contamination. C. Scoring Methods Design deterministic scoring (exact/fuzzy match, schema and format validation, citation checks, retrieval metrics such as recall@k and MRR, tool-call correctness, latency and cost metrics). Design LLM-as-judge scoring: rubric design, judge prompt engineering, calibration against human labels, bias and consistency checks (position, verbosity, self-preference), and judge-model selection and cost control. Define when to use each method and how to combine them into composite quality scores with confidence intervals. D. Regression Gates & Release Governance • Implementregressiongatesin CI/CD: threshold-based, statistical, and trend-based gates that block or flag releases for model, prompt, retrieval, or tool changes. • Define release criteria, rollback triggers, and approval workflows with clear ownership. • Integrate evaluation into pull requests, pre-production, and post-deployment verification. E. Observability, SLOs & Resilience Design observability for AI systems: distributed tracing across agent steps and tool calls, prompt/response logging with privacy controls, quality and drift dashboards, anomaly alerting, and usage and cost telemetry. Define SLIs/SLOs and error budgets for quality, latency, availability, cost, and safety. Design resilience patterns: fallbacks and model failover, timeouts, retries and circuit breakers, graceful degradation, rate-limit handling, and chaos/fault-injection testing for AI components. F. Responsible AI Assurance Design assurance for fairness and bias, safety and harmful content, privacy and PII leakage, security (prompt injection, jailbreaks, data exfiltration, tool misuse), transparency, and human oversight. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. jobs.title: Associate Director — PR&D Delivery & Operations
jobs.description: At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. At Lilly, the data and digital capability that underpins every regulatory submission, batch investigation, and process decision across CMC (Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls) is being rebuilt rather than maintained. Time-to-insight for scientists and process engineers, audit- and inspection-readiness, and the cost of running PR&D's platforms all depend on these capabilities. This role is the mechanism by which the portfolio moves from sustaining the current estate to reshaping it: from request-taking to business partnership, from manual data and process work to AI- and agent-supported execution, and from vendor dependence to retained Lilly capability. The Associate Director, PR&D Delivery & Operations leads broader delivery teams across CMC data platform modernization (structured and unstructured data, platform operations), scientific workflow automation (LIMS, MES, ELN), data governance and business alignment, and AI & Analytics (AI-use-case delivery) — accountable for delivery, technical direction, team capability and measurable business outcomes across all three. The role sits where CMC scientific and data process meets engineering: credible enough to lead a design review and challenge an architecture, fluent enough in regulated CMC data work to shape how a scientific or process team actually works. Split roughly 60% delivery and technical leadership and 40% strategy, business partnership and vendor leadership, it owns the demand relationship with PR&D business owners, directs the partner teams delivering a material share of the work, and supports the portfolio's AI and agentic capability agenda as one part of a broader delivery mandate. Key Responsibilities Portfolio Delivery Ownership — own delivery across the portfolio — scope, schedule, quality, dependencies, release readiness and production health — for CMC data and semantic infrastructure (knowledge graph, ontology, document and structured-data ingestion), platform modernization and operations, and AI-use-case delivery, directing the broader teams accountable for each track. Run delivery on real signals: flow, predictability, defect escape and adoption by scientific and process teams, not status reporting. Technical Direction & Engineering Standards — set and defend the technical direction of the portfolio, contributing to how CMC data platforms support the goals of the wider PR&D business area; review architecture and design, challenge weak decisions, and own standards for APIs, data contracts, ontology and knowledge-graph modeling (RDF/OWL/SPARQL, property graphs), and tool-calling interfaces (MCP) across CMC data platforms. Raise the engineering bar on test automation, CI/CD, observability and the deliberate reduction of technical debt, staying close enough to the work to judge trade-offs credibly. AI & Agentic Delivery Support — support delivery of AI and agentic use cases already on the portfolio roadmap — document and schema intelligence, retrieval over CMC content, and knowledge-graph-powered Q&A or summarization agents — ensuring these initiatives get the same delivery rigor, resourcing and release discipline as any other workstream. Help the team bring new use cases forward for evaluation, and support them through validation and into production with appropriate guardrails and human-in-the-loop review. Build AI-assisted engineering into the team's everyday practice, in step with the broader AI strategy set elsewhere in the portfolio. Business Partnership & Stakeholder Management — act as the technology partner for PR&D business owners and domain product managers across the portfolio's data, platform and AI-use-case tracks — the person they call first, and the person who tells them when an idea will not work. Capture and challenge incoming demand, agree priorities against capacity, and keep one honest view of the roadmap and what has been traded away. Translate CMC and scientific need into technical options and constraint, risk and cost into language a business owner can act on; set a rhythm of business reviews and early warning so there are no surprises at release; and build the case for modernization investment, with the benefit measurement that follows it. Vendor & Partner Delivery Management — get the work done through partner teams: define scope, outcomes and acceptance criteria, and hold suppliers to the same engineering, quality and GxP standards as internal teams. Shape the sourcing mix for the portfolio, plan partner ramp-up and ramp-down against the roadmap, manage supplier performance on predictability, quality and knowledge retention, and work with sourcing, legal and finance on statements of work, capacity models and change requests. Integrate partner engineers into one team, one backlog and one set of standards, and protect institutional knowledge through documentation, code ownership and cross-training. Quality, Risk & GxP Compliance — deliver in a GxP-regulated environment — computer system validation, 21 CFR Part 11, data integrity, inspection and audit readiness. Design for security and data privacy from the start, meet architecture and security review obligations early rather than at release, and own incident response and service levels for the products the teams run. People Leadership & Capability Building — manage, coach and grow broader delivery teams spanning multiple sub-teams and disciplines: clear expectations, specific feedback, honest check-ins and a development plan each person recognises as their own. Hire for the capability the portfolio needs next — engineering depth across data, knowledge-graph and AI-use-case delivery, product thinking, CMC domain fluency — address underperformance without delay, build bench strength and succession, and remove single points of failure. Hold high standards and psychological safety at the same time across a distributed team. Decision-Making Authority — make design, tooling, sequencing and sourcing decisions within the guidelines set by architecture, engineering and validation standards; challenge product, engineering or vendor approaches where delivery or compliance risk exists; forecast resource needs across the portfolio and manage the allocated budget against plan; contribute to PR&D's business-area plans by translating the modernization roadmap into resourced, executable delivery cycles; and escalate policy-level or cross-platform decisions with a recommendation rather than a question. Technical & Capability Areas CMC Data Systems (LIMS, MES, ELN) · Data Engineering & Data Platforms · Knowledge Graph & Ontology Engineering (OWL/RDF/SPARQL, Neo4j/property graphs) · Semantic Layer & Retrieval (Vector Databases, Hybrid/Graph-RAG) · AI/ML & Agentic Systems (LLMs, Multi-Agent Orchestration, Model Context Protocol) · Modern Software Development Practices (SDLC, CI/CD, Test Automation) · Cloud Platforms (Azure/AWS) · API & Integration Architecture · Clinical/Scientific Data Standards & Governance · Agile & Product Operating Model · Security & Compliance (GxP, CSV, 21 CFR Part 11) · Vendor & Delivery Governance · Business Stakeholder Management · People Leadership & Coaching Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or a related field (Master's preferred). 10+ years in technology delivery or technical leadership, including 4+ years of direct people management across broader or multi-team delivery organizations. 4+ years supporting CMC, pharma R&D, or manufacturing data and process technology — LIMS/MES/DMS/ELN systems, batch records, process or regulatory submission data. Demonstrated ownership of delivery for a portfolio or platform across multiple concurrent programmes, including work delivered through vendors. Broad technology awareness and working strength across cloud platforms, APIs and enterprise integration patterns, data engineering, AI/ML, and agentic systems — enough to review a design, engage credibly with technical teams across all these areas, ask the right questions, and spot delivery or quality risk, without requiring hands-on ownership of any single one. Working familiarity with AI, machine learning or agentic solutions and how they move from proof of concept into governed production use. Experience operating in regulated (GxP) environments, including computer system validation and inspection-readiness practices. Demonstrated success owning a senior business relationship — shaping demand, negotiating priorities and capacity, and holding credibility through difficult delivery news. Demonstrated success governing multi-vendor or managed-service delivery, with clear separation of Lilly-owned and vendor-executed responsibility, and command of the commercial mechanics. Strong communication skills, translating technical trade-offs into business, scientific and regulatory language for senior stakeholders. Working knowledge of Agile-at-scale and product operating model practices (backlog governance, value-stream mapping) applied to a regulated portfolio. Track record of hiring, coaching, performance management and retention across broader, distributed delivery teams. Additional Qualifications / Competencies Experience with knowledge graph or ontology engineering platforms (Neo4j, GraphDB, Protégé, or comparable), or semantic layer/retrieval tooling; platform training or certification. Exposure to CMC, manufacturing, or process data domains — batch records, equipment/material master data, or regulatory submission content. Strategic and analytical thinking — preparing decisions ahead of delivery rather than reacting to them. Strong vendor governance and negotiation skills; ownership mindset managing multiple priorities, stakeholders and concurrent programmes. Influence with internal and external customers and management — with business stakeholders who do not report to them and partner teams they do not employ; comfort driving clarity in ambiguity. Learning agility and continuous-improvement leadership — challenging the status quo and growing technical capability around them. Experience of shared ownership models between India-based and global organisations. The ETC is a technical resource for training, standards, project implementation, and the center of engineering excellence for the corporation, providing deeply technical resources to solve the most intractable technical problems in manufacturing. DME provides Digital Engineering Platform ownership, OT data integration solutions, engineering data standardization/ownership, and digital manufacturing solutions for Lilly Manufacturing. Our team focuses on connecting our facilities (securely) and leveraging the data from those facilities to deliver digital manufacturing solutions to improve manufacturing productivity, data integrity / compliance, quality, and operational excellence. Digital Manufacturing Technologies include digital twins, computational modeling, edge/IoT, and analytics solutions. Digital Engineering Platforms include CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System), GECMS (Global Engineering Content Management System) and many other digital platforms leveraged by engineers across Lilly Manufacturing. Position Description and Responsibilities The Principal Digital Solutions Engineer will design, develop, support, and continuously enhance digital solutions across Lilly's global manufacturing network, while serving as the owner for one or more digital products developed by the DME team. Representative solutions in scope span the four pillars of the Engineering Digital Strategy and include — but are not limited to — the Intralogistics Monitor (ILM), Audit Trail solutions, Condition-Based Maintenance solutions, RCA and troubleshooting solutions, equipment health and predictive maintenance dashboards, capital project and qualification workflow tools, engineering knowledge search, and inspection-readiness data products. These solutions are developed on standard Digital Engineering Platforms supported by the DME team, and the engineer will partner with data leads to ensure the necessary IT, OT, and ET data is available to support each solution. The engineer is also expected to leverage AI tools and platforms — such as Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot, and Anthropic's Claude — to accelerate development and to embed AI capability into solutions, including building agent skills, prompt-based workflows, and retrieval/automation patterns on top of existing Lilly-approved AI platforms. This role is not focused on training or developing foundation models; it is focused on applying AI tools effectively and responsibly to manufacturing problems. This is a global role, supporting functional initiatives and all Lilly Manufacturing sites globally. This role operates within an evolved Digital Solutions Engineering operating model. The team includes a Rapid Innovation branch that works at speed to prototype concepts and proof-of-value solutions against key business problems surfaced from the manufacturing network. The Principal Digital Solutions Engineer takes ownership of those solutions once they have been validated as worth scaling — maturing them from prototype to production-grade, hardening them for validated-system and data-integrity requirements, deploying and supporting them across sites, and providing long-term ownership over their roadmap, enhancement, and lifecycle. This split lets the Rapid Innovation branch stay focused on speed and discovery while the Principal Digital Solutions Engineer ensures that the most valuable concepts become durable, well-supported solutions that scale across the global manufacturing network. The primary focus of the role is twofold. Second, to assume the role of owner for those solutions: defining the product roadmap, managing the backlog, owning the technical architecture and lifecycle, ensuring compliance with validated-system requirements, and providing direct technical support to global users across Lilly Manufacturing.
