Complex Data Transformation & Deduplication (SAP Data Services): Design and optimize complex SAP Data Services (BODS) data flows, implementing advanced transforms (Match, Associate, User-Defined, and Data Cleanse) to automate record linkage, resolve master data duplicates, and enforce survivorship strategies. Job Description You will define and implement the end-to-end security architecture for Databricks on a major cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP). This is a hands-on role responsible for the access, governance, and data-protection model across the platform. You have designed and implemented enterprise security controls for Databricks environments, and you will act as a cross-account authority on security guardrails, access governance, and compliance. What You Will Do Own end-to-end security architecture. Define and implement the security architecture for Databricks across the platform, from identity through data protection. Manage identity and access. Own SSO/MFA integration and RBAC/ABAC access models, and establish access governance processes across accounts and workspaces. Secure Unity Catalog. Establish the lowest practical access boundary, preventing access to adjacent business-unit data and storage. Control privileged access and configuration drift. Govern privileged elevation and break-glass access, and detect unauthorized changes with monitored alert latency and remediation. Protect data and secrets. Establish controls for encryption, secrets management, and network security aligned to relevant regulatory compliance requirements. Build guardrails and auditability. Set up security guardrails, auditability, and access governance so the platform stays compliant and controllable as it scales. Provide cross-account technical leadership. Act as a go-to security reviewer across multiple accounts, contributing to design reviews and resolving access and governance issues that individual delivery teams cannot. What You Bring (Required) Hands-on experience designing and implementing security for enterprise Databricks environments. Deep Unity Catalog security experience: RBAC/ABAC, fine-grained (row/column/attribute) access, data classification, and Delta Sharing / open sharing controls. Least-privilege and blast-radius design across business units, containing access to adjacent data and storage. Privileged access management experience: controlled elevation, break-glass, configuration-drift detection, and remediation. Strong identity and access management background: SSO/MFA integration and access governance. Expertise in encryption, secrets management, and network security on at least one major cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP). Working knowledge of regulatory compliance requirements relevant to data platforms. Ability to design and run proof-of-control tests and quantify outcomes (e.g., revocation time, data exposure, drift-detection and alert latency), not just implement. Nice to Have (Preferred) Databricks Cloud Platform Architect accreditation (AWS, Azure, or GCP) or Databricks Platform Administrator. Recognized cloud security certification (e.g., AWS or Azure security specialty, or CISSP). Note that Databricks has no standalone security certification, so security credentials come from the cloud provider or an industry body. Multi-cloud experience across two or more of AWS, Azure, and GCP. Regulated-industry experience (financial services, healthcare, or similar). What This Role Is Not This is a Databricks-native security and access architect role. It is not a general enterprise or datacenter security role. The right candidate has genuinely designed and implemented access, governance, and data-protection controls inside Databricks environments, distinct from a generalist security engineer without hands-on Databricks depth. We are seeking a DataOps Engineer who treats spaces, data pipelines, replication flows, and semantic models as configuration, not one-off manual builds — someone who has designed or maintained environments where central metadata and rule tables drive how data assets are onboarded, transformed, partitioned, secured, and federated, rather than hand-crafting individual spaces and views from scratch. You will operate across the full data lifecycle: hybrid ingestion/replication (landing persisted business layer cold store/archive), lifecycle and storage tiering strategies, and the dynamic routing engine that provides filtered, masked, and context-rich semantic views to multiple downstream consumers. Key Responsibilities.. Build and operate resilient real-time and batch ingestion pipelines within SAP Datasphere using Replication Flows, Data Flows, and Transformation Flows from SAP (S/4HANA, ECC, BW/4HANA, SAP BDC) and non-SAP cloud/lake sources. Design and maintain metadata-driven Space and Pipeline generation — where onboarding a new source entity, defining business semantics, or establishing delta replication is driven by configuration registries, templates, and CLI/API automation rather than manual UI workflows. Implement retention and data tiering strategies using Datasphere cold storage integration, partition-based retention, and hybrid connectivity to external cloud object stores (e.g., ADLS Gen2, AWS S3, Snowflake). Build and maintain a governed routing & semantic distribution engine: leverage a metadata rules registry (splittable, target_consumers[], row_filter_expr, column_mask_expr) to programmatically build and manage Data Access Controls (DAC), Analytic Models, and Consumption Views across Spaces. Own Datasphere & BDC platform governance: architect Space hierarchies, user privileges, Space-to-Space sharing topologies, catalog registrations, and cross-system business context lineages. Drive DataOps & CI/CD automation: manage automated asset lifecycle and deployment across environments (Dev/Test/Prod) leveraging Datasphere CLI, Content Network packages, REST APIs, and Git-integrated repositories. Monitor platform health & replication telemetry: track replication lag, task execution logs, memory/storage consumption quotas across Spaces, and semantic view performance; build proactive alerting for SLA breaches and data drift. Collaborate with SAP functional/data modeling teams to align on semantic consistency (CDS views, business context, ODP extractors) and translate consumer access requirements into secure, performant consumption models. Document architecture, data flow patterns, and security topologies to maintain enterprise compliance and accelerate developer onboarding. Required Skills & Experience Core Platform & SAP Datasphere / BDC Hands-on experience with SAP Datasphere (formerly Data Warehouse Cloud) and/or SAP BDC / BTP Data Services. Deep understanding of SAP source integration patterns: CDS Views, ODP/Extractors, SAP Landscape Transformation (SLT), S/4HANA integrations, and federation vs. replication trade-offs. Strong proficiency in SQL and SAP HANA Cloud engine concepts (calculation views, indexing, execution plan analysis, in-memory optimization). Metadata-Driven Engineering & Automation (Critical) Proven experience building or maintaining metadata/config-driven integration frameworks — where schemas, replication tasks, or security policies are programmatically driven by configuration tables or parameterized templates. Experience with SAP Datasphere Command Line Interface (datasphere CLI), REST APIs, or Python scripts to automate tenant management, Space provisioning, CSN/JSON definition generation, and user onboarding. Strong understanding of keeping semantic models and DAC rules synchronized with an authoritative source-of-truth metadata repository. Platform Engineering / DataOps CI/CD & Lifecycle Management: Hands-on experience with Datasphere Content Network, transport management, and version-controlled deployment pipelines (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or GitLab CI). Scripting & Orchestration: Strong scripting skills (Python, PowerShell, Bash) and experience with enterprise orchestrators (Airflow, Azure Data Factory, Control-M, or SAP BTP job scheduling). Observability & Performance Tuning: Experience monitoring space storage quotas, replication queues, performance optimization of complex joined views, and setting up automated incident alerts. Governance & Security Deep expertise in Datasphere Data Access Controls (DAC), object-level authorizations, row-level filters, and column-level masking for sensitive/PII data. Familiarity with enterprise cataloging and metadata lineage (SAP Datasphere Catalog, SAP Purview connector, Collibra, or Alation). Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to bridge the gap between technical data engineering and business analytics teams. Nice to Have Experience with SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) integration and Live Connection optimization. Experience with SAP HANA Cloud / HDI Containers and native HANA database artifacts. Hands-on knowledge of cloud lakehouse platforms (Databricks, Snowflake, Azure Synapse, Fabric) connected via Open Data Mesh / Federation to Datasphere. Familiarity with SAP BTP global account and subaccount administration, Cloud Identity Services (IAS), and single sign-on (SSO). End-to-End DataOps Pipeline: CI/CD deployment routines across Dev/Test/Prod environments are fully automated with zero manual transport bottlenecks. jobs.title: Senior Principal Engineer –E commerce
jobs.description: Job Purpose: We are seeking a Senior Principal Engineer – eCommerce to lead engineering delivery for GSK Direct, GSK's B2B eCommerce platform that enables healthcare professionals to purchase GSK vaccines and pharmaceuticals in the US and international markets. This is a hands-on engineering leadership role: you will manage the vendor technical leads and drive a multi-disciplinary DevOps team of SAP Commerce Cloud, Composable Storefront, UI, and QA engineers. The role demands deep technical expertise in SAP Commerce Cloud, headless commerce architecture, along with the ability to partner with the Business Product Owner, enterprise architecture, and business stakeholders to deliver secure, scalable, and high-impact customer experiences. Key Responsibilities: 1. Engineering Leadership & Platform Ownership Own the technical health, roadmap execution, and engineering quality of the GSKDirect-US and GSKDirect-Global eCommerce platforms built on SAP Commerce Cloud and SAP Composable Storefront. Serve as the design authority for commerce solutions, approving designs across OCC APIs, B2B commerce (company accounts, customer-specific catalogs and pricing, approvals, checkout), SSO, ERP integrations and Backoffice. Make build-vs-configure decisions that favor out-of-the-box SAP capabilities, reduce technical debt, and keep the platform upgrade-ready. Implement and enforce ITMS (IT Management System) controls, ensuring compliance, audit readiness, and operational excellence in a regulated environment. 2. Vendor Management & Delivery Oversight Manage and direct the vendor technical leads, DevOps scrum teams of SAP Commerce, Composable Storefront, UI, and QA engineers. Own sprint delivery across 3–4 week agile cycles: backlog grooming, story analysis, estimation, sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives, and hold vendor teams accountable for quality, velocity, and commitments. Lead daily scrum with GSK leads and business stakeholders, removing blockers and making timely technical decisions. Track vendor performance against SLAs and KPIs (velocity, defect leakage, cycle time, incident resolution), and drive corrective actions and resourcing decisions with the supplier. Foster a “One Team” culture across GSK, onshore, and offshore team members built on collaboration, support, and accountability. 3. Hands-on SAP Commerce Cloud & Headless Commerce Expertise Provide technical direction on SAP Commerce Cloud environment management and deployments. Guide the headless storefront architecture on SAP Composable Storefront (Spartacus) and Angular, including SSR, lazy loading, performance optimization, accessibility, and reusable component and design-system patterns. Lead code quality through GitHub pull request reviews, coding standards, unit testing expectations, and secure development practices. Drive root cause analysis of complex production issues. 4. Strategic Partnerships & Business Alignment Partner with the GSK Business Product Owner and business stakeholders in the US and global markets to translate commercial needs into scalable technical solutions and a prioritized roadmap. Align with enterprise architecture, security, and integration teams (ERP, identity, data) within a federated architecture model. Influence roadmap and investment decisions by providing technical insights, feasibility assessments, and effort estimates, and explain technical trade-offs in clear, non-technical language. 5. Innovation & Continuous Improvement Modernize engineering practices: CI/CD pipelines (GitHub, Jenkins, Azure DevOps), test automation, release management, and environment strategy on CCv2. Drive AI-assisted engineering across the vendor DevOps team. That means GitHub Copilot for coding, unit tests and pull request reviews; AI help with story grooming and writing acceptance criteria; and tracking the impact on velocity and quality. Apply AI-driven monitoring to detect anomalies in site performance, checkout and order flows, cutting time to detect and resolve production issues. Plan and lead SAP Commerce Cloud and Composable Storefront/Angular version upgrades to stay current and secure. Stay ahead of SAP Commerce, composable/headless commerce, and B2B eCommerce trends, and mentor the vendor team's engineers. Prepare the platform for agentic commerce by exposing secure, well-governed OCC/REST APIs that AI agents can use, with clear guardrails for authentication, permissions and auditability. Deep hands-on expertise in SAP Commerce Cloud: Java/J2EE, Spring, OCC APIs, ImpEx, CronJobs, Backoffice, ASM, PCM/OMS, and CCv2 deployments. Strong experience with headless commerce architecture and SAP Composable Storefront (Spartacus) on Angular (v15+), TypeScript, SSR, and front-end performance optimization. Experience delivering B2B commerce capabilities: company accounts and roles, customer-specific catalogs and pricing, approvals, checkout, order status, SSO, and ERP integration. Proven track record running agile delivery: sprint planning, estimation, backlog management, and release management with Jira, Confluence, and GitHub. Experience with CI/CD, code review practices, and production monitoring and troubleshooting (e.g., Dynatrace). Experience managing ITMS controls, security, and compliance in a regulated environment. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence technical and business leaders. Preferred Qualifications: Experience in Pharma, Healthcare, or Life Sciences industries, ideally B2B commerce for healthcare professionals. Experience with multi-country/multi-site commerce (localization, multiple currencies and languages) and integrations with SAP S/4HANA. Hands-on experience using AI/GenAI to improve engineering productivity and digital commerce experiences (e.g., GitHub Copilot, AI-driven search and personalization, conversational commerce), in a regulated environment. jobs.description: GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centred on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems. Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines. Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges. Job Purpose: The Principal, IAM Lifecycle Management will drive the design, engineering and delivery of enterprise identity and account lifecycle capabilities and act as the senior technical authority for the capability. This senior individual contributor role translates business, security, architecture and regulatory requirements into scalable lifecycle controls, automation and integrations across cloud, on-premises and SaaS environments. The role owns complex implementations, establishes reusable engineering practices and guides technical delivery across joiner, mover, leaver, rehire, contractor, partner and non-human identity scenarios. About the team: IAM Lifecycle Management owns the identity and account lifecycle end to end. The team ensures that workforce, contractor, partner and non-human identities receive appropriate access when created, joining, moving, changing status or returning, and that access is suspended or removed promptly when no longer required. It improves lifecycle automation, identity-data quality, governance controls and service reliability across on-premises, cloud and SaaS systems. Key responsibilities: This role will provide you the opportunity to take ownership of key activities to progress your career. These responsibilities include some of the following: Own complex IAM lifecycle workstreams from discovery and requirements analysis through solution design, configuration, testing, deployment and operational transition. Act as the senior technical subject matter expert for IAM Lifecycle Management, advising product, architecture, engineering, security, risk, audit and business stakeholders. Mentor engineers, review solution designs and code, and establish reusable patterns, standards, documentation and engineering practices. Design and deliver end-to-end identity and account lifecycle capabilities, including creation, provisioning, modification, suspension, recertification and deprovisioning across on-premises, cloud and SaaS systems. Drive joiner, mover, leaver, rehire, contractor, partner and non-human identity lifecycle scenarios, including trigger events, approval orchestration, account states, exception handling and recovery controls. Drive complex application onboarding initiatives and integrations between authoritative HR and identity sources, directories, IGA platforms and target applications using connectors, APIs and event-driven services. Implement and improve governance controls for least privilege, segregation of duties, birthright and role-based access, account ownership, orphan-account prevention, access reviews and policy compliance. Drive improvements in identity correlation, reconciliation, source-data quality, reporting, monitoring, observability and engineering telemetry to improve lifecycle accuracy and service reliability. Own root-cause analysis and resolution of complex lifecycle defects, control failures, production incidents and cross-platform integration issues. Contribute technical insight to product roadmaps, technology assessments and delivery planning, identifying dependencies, risks and opportunities for automation, resilience and user-experience improvement. Promote secure engineering, automated testing, CI/CD, API governance, accessibility, performance optimisation, observability and controlled deployment practices. Ensure IAM processes, implementation evidence and control operation meet regulatory, audit and risk-management requirements, including those of highly regulated environments. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Ten or more years of relevant IAM experience, including significant hands-on engineering and technical ownership of complex identity and account lifecycle implementations. Strong implementation experience with an enterprise Identity Governance and Administration platform such as SailPoint, Saviynt, LINX or an equivalent product. Proven experience designing and delivering lifecycle solutions for joiner, mover, leaver, rehire, employee, contractor, partner and non-human identity scenarios. Deep understanding of provisioning and deprovisioning workflows, approval orchestration, birthright and role-based access, account-state transitions, exception handling and policy enforcement. Strong knowledge of identity data models, account correlation, reconciliation, access reviews, certification, segregation of duties, orphan-account prevention and audit evidence. Experience integrating IAM platforms with HR systems, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, LDAP, databases, SaaS platforms and custom applications. Strong engineering capability with REST APIs, JSON, SQL, scripting and secure event-driven integration patterns, with the ability to troubleshoot transactions across connected systems. Experience owning application onboarding and complex cross-functional technical delivery from design through testing, deployment and operational handover. Experience delivering secure, observable and resilient IAM services using automated testing, Git-based version control and CI/CD pipelines such as GitHub or Azure DevOps. Strong troubleshooting and root-cause analysis skills across distributed IAM services, integrations, workflows and data flows. Ability to mentor engineers and communicate complex technical concepts clearly to engineering, product, business, risk and audit stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications: Advanced implementation experience with a SaaS-based identity security or leading IGA platform, including workflow, connector and policy configuration. Experience modernising or migrating legacy or bespoke lifecycle solutions to a SaaS IGA platform. Experience designing serverless, containerised or event-driven integration services in Microsoft Azure. Hands-on experience with GraphQL, TypeScript, Node.js, Next.js, NestJS, Apollo, .NET or API federation where these support IAM integration, administration and self-service experiences. Experience applying API-first, microfrontend, reusable component, secure coding and automated testing practices in enterprise applications. Experience with policy-as-code, identity analytics, automated testing and engineering telemetry for IAM capabilities. Experience applying AI or analytics to identity-data quality, access recommendations, anomaly detection or governance improvement, and knowledge of identity controls for AI agents and other non-human identities. Experience with control frameworks such as SOX and GxP and producing evidence suitable for regulated environments. Relevant IAM, cloud or security certification, such as CISSP, SailPoint, Saviynt, CIMP or Microsoft Azure. Experience working in a central IT or cyber security team within pharmaceuticals, healthcare, financial services or another highly regulated industry. jobs.title: Staff, Data Engineer
jobs.description: Job Purpose : Enterprise AI (EAI) builds the data foundations that GSK's AI systems depend on. In our operating model, digital workers do the hands-on data engineering. They generate pipelines, test and deploy them, monitor them in production and remediate failures. Our engineers design the system those digital workers operate in. At the centre of that system is a governed context layer. It makes data, meaning, permissions and history retrievable at the moment they are needed, and sits above our data platforms and beneath every experience and agent built on them. The Staff Data Engineer is accountable for implementing and evolving the governed context layer that humans and digital workers use across EAI, and is EAI's internal authority on data architecture for AI. Responsibilities: Implement and evolve the governed context layer as a product: one layer across enterprise knowledge, structured data, business vocabulary and modelled ontologies, queried by humans and digital workers at run time. Build the capabilities the layer depends on: reliable cataloguing across structured and unstructured data, AI-assisted metadata enrichment, context design for each use case, secure agent access over standard protocols such as MCP, and routing across sources. Make certified meaning machine-readable so that every number a digital worker returns resolves to one governed definition, with clear ownership and lineage. Define the architecture standards and shared frameworks that digital workers use to generate, test, deploy and monitor pipelines, reducing the integration cost of each new AI initiative. Set the operating model for agent-generated engineering work: what digital workers do autonomously, what requires human approval, how quality is evaluated and how incidents escalate. Lead the incidents digital workers cannot resolve, from detection to permanent resolution. Required skills: 10+ years in data engineering, including substantial time defining data architecture for production AI or ML systems at significant scale or complexity. Deep, hands-on experience building AI-grade data infrastructure: feature stores, vector databases, retrieval architectures, streaming data flows and evaluation datasets. Experience building context, metadata or semantic infrastructure that AI systems consume, such as catalogues, business glossaries, knowledge graphs or ontologies, exposed to agents over protocols such as MCP. Experience designing and operating AI agents or LLM-powered systems inside data workflows, including evaluation, guardrails and human-in-the-loop controls. A track record of defining data quality, lineage and governance standards for AI pipelines, including privacy, consent, PII handling and auditability, adopted across multiple data domains. Expert command of cloud data platforms and infrastructure as code, and a record of setting engineering standards that others adopted Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred skills: Prior Staff, Principal or equivalent experience in an organisation operating a non-trivial data platform for AI. Experience in a regulated industry, such as life sciences, where data integrity and auditability are mandatory. Public technical contributions, such as talks, writing or open source, on data architecture for AI, context engineering or agent-operated data engineering. jobs.description: GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Job Purpose: Every person, workload and AI agent at GSK needs an identity it can prove, credentials that cannot be stolen and access that is just enough, just in time. As our applications move to the cloud and AI agents begin working alongside our people, authentication is becoming the foundation of trust for everything we do. The Associate Director, leads the engineering and delivery of that foundation, starting with single sign-on (SSO) and extending the same discipline to Azure and Google Cloud (GCP), non-human identities (NHI) and AI agents. Our vision: One trusted way to authenticate, whoever or whatever is asking for access: passwordless for people, secretless for workloads and tightly scoped for AI agents. Security should be invisible when everything is right and decisive when it is not. We will get there by using AI securely in our own work, setting the example for the rest of GSK. About the team: Authentication and Cloud Security is part of Identity & Access Management. We build and run SSO for GSK’s workforce and applications, and bring the same discipline to securing the accounts, credentials and authentication of cloud, non-human and AI agent identities. Together with PKI & Cryptographic Services, we protect the identities, secrets and keys that GSK’s cloud and AI future depends on. Key responsibilities: In this role, you will turn that vision into reality. Your responsibilities will include: Build one team: Lead and develop a global team of engineers across SSO, cloud, NHI and AI agent identity, working as one team with shared patterns rather than separate product silos. Deliver the roadmap: Own the engineering roadmap, delivery plans and service measures, turning the agreed architecture and standards into reliable services. Make sign-in passwordless and trusted: Run GSK’s SSO services (SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0), moving the workforce to passwordless, phishing-resistant authentication, with conditional access, strong identity verification for registration and account recovery, and the retirement of legacy authentication. Secure the cloud: Protect cloud accounts and access in Azure and GCP with strong authentication, workload identity federation, least privilege and just-in-time access, with no standing admin rights. Bring workloads and AI agents into the fold: Give non-human identities and AI agents unique, accountable identities kept separate from human ones, with protected credentials, scoped and revocable access and full audit logging, and promote integration with GSK’s identity lifecycle and governance processes. Move from secrets to secretless: Drive adoption of secrets vaulting and management, remove hard-coded credentials, favour short-lived and secretless authentication, and build secret scanning into engineering pipelines. Partner with PKI: Work with the PKI & Cryptographic Services lead to secure cloud, AI and secrets, with aligned roadmaps, clear ownership and a joined-up approach for stakeholders and auditors. Use AI ourselves: Apply AI to identity engineering and operations, such as risky sign-in analysis, anomaly detection, faster onboarding and incident triage, with human oversight and clear audit trails. Set the example: Show GSK what secure cloud and AI looks like through secure-by-default implementations, reusable patterns, automation and implementation guidelines. Keep trust earned: Ensure these services meet audit and compliance requirements, including GxP, SOX, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001 and the EU AI Act, and lead major incidents and continual improvement with partner teams. Basic Qualifications: Degree in computer science, information technology, cyber security or a related field, or equivalent experience. At least 10 years’ experience in identity or security, including leading engineering teams that deliver and run enterprise identity or security services in a large organisation. Strong knowledge of SSO and modern authentication (SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0), conditional access, multi-factor authentication and passwordless authentication. Hands-on experience securing identity and access in Azure, including Microsoft Entra ID, Azure role-based access control and workload identities. Experience securing non-human identities and secrets, including vaulting, credential rotation and removing embedded secrets, and integrating them with identity lifecycle and governance processes. Working knowledge of AI and large language model security risks, such as agent permissions, data exposure and prompt injection. Strong leadership, delivery and communication skills, including managing roadmaps, suppliers and audits, and explaining technical risk to senior stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications: Experience delivering SSO at scale with Microsoft Entra ID or Ping Identity, including passwordless authentication and identity verification. Experience securing identity and access in Google Cloud (GCP), and with tools for securing non-human identity credentials and cloud privileged access. Experience with secrets vaulting and management platforms such as Akeyless, CyberArk, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault or Google Secret Manager. Experience securing AI agents or platforms such as Azure AI Foundry, Vertex AI or Copilot, and familiarity with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications. Working understanding of PKI and certificate-based authentication, and experience with Terraform and identity automation. Certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator, Azure Security Engineer or Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer. Experience in pharmaceuticals or another highly regulated industry. jobs.title: Associate Director - IAM Advanced Authentication
jobs.description: GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centered on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems. Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines. Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges. Job Purpose : Every person, workload and AI agent at GSK needs an identity it can prove, credentials that cannot be stolen and access that is just enough, just in time. As our applications move to the cloud and AI agents begin working alongside our people, authentication is becoming the foundation of trust for everything we do. The Associate Director, leads the engineering and delivery of that foundation, starting with single sign-on (SSO) and extending the same discipline to Azure and Google Cloud (GCP), non-human identities (NHI) and AI agents. Our vision: One trusted way to authenticate, whoever or whatever is asking for access: passwordless for people, secretless for workloads and tightly scoped for AI agents. Security should be invisible when everything is right and decisive when it is not. We will get there by using AI securely in our own work, setting the example for the rest of GSK. About the team: Authentication and Cloud Security is part of Identity & Access Management. We build and run SSO for GSK’s workforce and applications, and bring the same discipline to securing the accounts, credentials and authentication of cloud, non-human and AI agent identities. Together with PKI & Cryptographic Services, we protect the identities, secrets and keys that GSK’s cloud and AI future depends on. Key responsibilities: In this role, you will turn that vision into reality. Your responsibilities will include: Build one team: Lead and develop a global team of engineers across SSO, cloud, NHI and AI agent identity, working as one team with shared patterns rather than separate product silos. Deliver the roadmap: Own the engineering roadmap, delivery plans and service measures, turning the agreed architecture and standards into reliable services. Make sign-in passwordless and trusted: Run GSK’s SSO services (SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0), moving the workforce to passwordless, phishing-resistant authentication, with conditional access, strong identity verification for registration and account recovery, and the retirement of legacy authentication. Secure the cloud: Protect cloud accounts and access in Azure and GCP with strong authentication, workload identity federation, least privilege and just-in-time access, with no standing admin rights. Bring workloads and AI agents into the fold: Give non-human identities and AI agents unique, accountable identities kept separate from human ones, with protected credentials, scoped and revocable access and full audit logging, and promote integration with GSK’s identity lifecycle and governance processes. Move from secrets to secretless: Drive adoption of secrets vaulting and management, remove hard-coded credentials, favour short-lived and secretless authentication, and build secret scanning into engineering pipelines. Partner with PKI: Work with the PKI & Cryptographic Services lead to secure cloud, AI and secrets, with aligned roadmaps, clear ownership and a joined-up approach for stakeholders and auditors. Use AI ourselves: Apply AI to identity engineering and operations, such as risky sign-in analysis, anomaly detection, faster onboarding and incident triage, with human oversight and clear audit trails. Set the example: Show GSK what secure cloud and AI looks like through secure-by-default implementations, reusable patterns, automation and implementation guidelines. Keep trust earned: Ensure these services meet audit and compliance requirements, including GxP, SOX, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001 and the EU AI Act, and lead major incidents and continual improvement with partner teams. Basic Qualifications: Degree in computer science, information technology, cyber security or a related field, or equivalent experience. At least 18 years’ experience in identity or security, including leading engineering teams that deliver and run enterprise identity or security services in a large organisation. Strong knowledge of SSO and modern authentication (SAML, OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0), conditional access, multi-factor authentication and passwordless authentication. Hands-on experience securing identity and access in Azure, including Microsoft Entra ID, Azure role-based access control and workload identities. Experience securing non-human identities and secrets, including vaulting, credential rotation and removing embedded secrets, and integrating them with identity lifecycle and governance processes. Working knowledge of AI and large language model security risks, such as agent permissions, data exposure and prompt injection. Strong leadership, delivery and communication skills, including managing roadmaps, suppliers and audits, and explaining technical risk to senior stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications: Experience delivering SSO at scale with Microsoft Entra ID or Ping Identity, including passwordless authentication and identity verification. Experience securing identity and access in Google Cloud (GCP), and with tools for securing non-human identity credentials and cloud privileged access. Experience with secrets vaulting and management platforms such as Akeyless, CyberArk, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault or Google Secret Manager. Experience securing AI agents or platforms such as Azure AI Foundry, Vertex AI or Copilot, and familiarity with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications. Working understanding of PKI and certificate-based authentication, and experience with Terraform and identity automation. Certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator, Azure Security Engineer or Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer. Experience in pharmaceuticals or another highly regulated industry. Typical tools and technologies: Microsoft Entra ID, Ping Identity, passkeys and FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business, Azure, Google Cloud, Akeyless, CyberArk, Azure Key Vault, Microsoft Graph, Terraform and CI/CD pipelines. jobs.title: Staff, AI Product Manager
jobs.description: About the Role: GSK’s Enterprise AI team, a highly skilled applied AI group, translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across every major group at GSK — R&D, Medical, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Legal, Finance, and beyond. Bionic pods — AI product managers, forward deployed engineers, full-stack engineers, data engineers, and AI agents and workers — embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes. We are hiring a Staff, AI Product Manager to own Emerging Tech and AI Tooling, the front edge of GSK’s AI platform estate. You will run structured evaluation of new AI tools and platforms, decide what graduates into a standing tower and what gets retired, and own the AI developer tooling GSK engineers use every day. It suits someone who can hold an evaluation to a decision date and retire tools the organisation is attached to. You will lead a small engineering squad and set direction a far larger estate inherits. Why This Role Exists : Every week brings a new AI tool and a stakeholder who wants it. Without a disciplined front door, evaluations never close and nothing is ever retired. This role runs that front door, and owns the developer tooling estate so the tools engineers depend on daily have a named owner rather than a shared inbox. In this role you will be the person who: Owns the evaluation portfolio for new AI tools and platforms across Enterprise AI. Decides what graduates into a standing platform tower, what holds, and what gets retired. Owns the AI developer tooling estate end to end. Hands graduated platforms over with a working operating model. How This Differs from Traditional Product Management: This is not a traditional enterprise product role managing a source system’s roadmap, releases, and backlog. As an AI Product Manager in Enterprise AI, you: Build new AI products from ambiguous, unsolved business problems. Work with probabilistic systems, defining evaluations, acceptable error, and human oversight. Help lead a bionic pod, deciding which work goes to engineers and which to AI agents and workers, and how they hand off. Prototype hands on and are measured on business outcomes. Key Responsibilities: Evaluation & Graduation: Run every evaluation to a decision. Set the hypothesis, the success bar, the comparison set, and the kill date up front. Build credible adoption and retirement cases that survive finance and architecture scrutiny — engineering hours saved, licence cost avoided, capability gained, duplication removed. Tell new capability from repackaging so overlap with what GSK already runs is caught before it becomes duplicate spend. Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping: Shape the emerging tech portfolio. Keep a living view of in-flight, queued, and retired evaluations with the rationale for each call, and feed it into the AI Platforms & Tools portfolio. Make the graduate, retire, or hold call. Run access, entitlement, support, and adoption for the coding and desktop tools engineers depend on daily. Stay hands on. Prototype alongside the team and form your own judgment on a tool by using it. Stakeholder Alignment & Communication: Operate fluently with VP-level technology and business leaders. Run conversations that turn vendor enthusiasm into a testable hypothesis with a decision date. Build sponsor coalitions that secure evaluation funding, pilot cohorts, and the air cover to retire tools people are attached to. Required skil ls: 16+ years of progressive experience spanning some combination of pharma/life sciences, AI/ML product strategy, and senior product management or strategy roles in technology-led organisations. It also coaches platform engineering teams in reliability practice and error-budget discipline. The role sits in Reliability Engineering & Operations and is deployed into a platform domain while drawing on the central capability, so it holds the central reliability standard inside a team it does not report to. Platform build and engineering direction sit with the Principal Engineers and the Engineering Director, the major incident process sits with the Major Incident Manager, and the reliability standard itself is set by the Reliability Engineering Senior Director. Reliability targets are held jointly with the Platform Manager rather than imposed on them. ROLE SCALE AND COMPLEXITY This is a senior enterprise reliability leadership role operating across globally distributed, business-critical Network and Connectivity services. The post holder is accountable for setting technical direction, resolving systemic and ambiguous reliability risks, and influencing prioritisation across multiple platform teams, suppliers and geographies without relying on direct line authority. The role manages a portfolio of interdependent services with material operational, regulatory, cyber, resilience and financial consequences. It shapes investment and supplier decisions and may influence or govern an annual technology and service portfolio of up to approximately GBP 23 million, where applicable to the assigned scope. Leads reliability outcomes across global enterprise connectivity, including interdependent campus, data-centre, cloud, manufacturing and market network services. The role addresses failure modes that can affect multiple sites or regions simultaneously and coordinates decisions across network engineering, cyber security, cloud, hosting, business continuity and strategic suppliers. MARKET SCOPE Global scope, supporting business operations across regions, countries and markets in which GSK operates. The role establishes consistent reliability outcomes across regional delivery teams while accommodating local regulatory, data-residency, business-continuity and market-criticality requirements. Key Responsibilities Define and monitor SLOs for the platforms served, and instrument those platforms for observability so reliability is measured rather than assumed. Apply AI and automation for anomaly detection, predictive alerting and self-healing, so that recurring conditions are handled without human intervention. Lead incident response for the platforms served, and drive root-cause resolution through to permanent prevention rather than closing on restoration. Improve resilience through capacity, failover and recovery engineering, and test recovery rather than documenting it. Reduce operational toil through automation and reusable tooling, working the identified manual task and toil candidates and evidencing the effort removed. Close observability coverage gaps for the platforms served, prioritising by the reliability risk each gap leaves unmeasured. Coach platform engineering teams in reliability practice and error-budget discipline, so reliability is built in rather than inspected in. Track reliability metrics against SLOs and team OKRs, and act on the trend rather than only reporting it. Support reliability oversight of supplier-run services, holding partner-operated components to the same SLOs as internal ones. Hold the central reliability standard while deployed in a platform domain, escalating to the Reliability Engineering Senior Director where local pressure would erode it. Feed reliability evidence into the platform backlog held by the Product Owner, so that resilience work competes on stated risk rather than on goodwill. Hold the boundaries with the Principal Engineers on platform build, the Major Incident Manager on the major incident process, and the Platform Manager on the reliability targets the platform commits to. Set the multi-year reliability strategy and engineering roadmap for the assigned Network and Connectivity portfolio, translating enterprise risk and business priorities into funded reliability outcomes. Quality, Operations & Cost Define evaluation frameworks for retrieval and context quality (relevance, groundedness, completeness, latency, regression testing). Instrument context services for observability (tracing, quality metrics, usage, drift). Manage cost and performance trade-offs (index sizes, model calls, query patterns, caching). F. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description: Senior Machine Learning Engineer Description - We are looking for a Senior MLOps Engineer to design, build, and operate the infrastructure that enables machine learning models and large language models to be deployed safely, reliably, and at scale. In this role, you will create the end-to-end capabilities required to move models from experimentation into production, expose them through secure and highly available endpoints, and enable users and applications to interact with AI-powered services. You will work across AWS and Databricks to establish robust CI/CD pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, observability, governance, rollback mechanisms, and operational standards. You will partner closely with data scientists, machine learning engineers, software engineers, security teams, and platform engineers. The ideal candidate combines strong cloud and DevOps engineering skills with a practical understanding of machine learning systems, LLM deployment patterns, and production reliability. Key Responsibilities MLOps Platform and Architecture Design and implement a scalable MLOps platform using AWS and Databricks. Define reference architectures and reusable deployment patterns for traditional machine learning models, deep learning models, and large language models. Build standardized workflows that move models from development and validation into staging and production. Develop self-service capabilities that allow data scientists and ML engineers to deploy models without manually managing infrastructure. Establish clear separation between development, testing, staging, and production environments. Design multi-region or multi-availability-zone architectures where required by business continuity and availability objectives. CI/CD and Model Deployment Build automated CI/CD pipelines for model code, inference services, infrastructure, configuration, and model artifacts. Implement automated testing across the deployment lifecycle, including: Unit testing Integration testing Model validation Data contract validation API and endpoint testing Security testing Performance and load testing Regression testing Automate model packaging, containerization, versioning, approval, promotion, and deployment. Support deployment strategies such as blue-green deployments, canary releases, shadow deployments, and controlled traffic shifting. Implement reliable rollback and roll-forward mechanisms for application code, infrastructure, model versions, prompts, and configuration. Ensure deployments are reproducible, auditable, and recoverable. Model and LLM Serving Design and operate secure, scalable, low-latency inference endpoints. Deploy models using appropriate services and patterns across AWS and Databricks, such as: Databricks Model Serving MLflow Model Registry Amazon SageMaker Amazon ECS or EKS AWS Lambda, where appropriate API Gateway Application Load Balancers Build synchronous, asynchronous, batch, and streaming inference capabilities. Design serving architectures for LLM-powered applications, including: Hosted foundation models Open-source models Fine-tuned models Retrieval-augmented generation Embedding services Vector search Prompt and response orchestration Tool-calling and agentic workflows Optimize inference performance, scalability, GPU utilization, concurrency, throughput, latency, and cost. Implement autoscaling, request throttling, queuing, caching, timeout handling, and graceful degradation. Reliability, Recovery, and Business Continuity Build recoverable model-serving endpoints with clearly defined recovery time and recovery point objectives. Implement automated health checks, failover mechanisms, retry policies, circuit breakers, and service recovery procedures. Design backup and recovery processes for: Model artifacts Model registry metadata Feature definitions Deployment configurations Infrastructure state Prompts and application configuration Vector indexes and knowledge-base assets Create disaster recovery procedures and regularly test restoration and failover capabilities. Ensure production services can recover from failed deployments, infrastructure outages, model errors, and upstream dependency failures. Develop operational runbooks and incident response procedures. Monitoring and Observability Implement end-to-end observability for infrastructure, applications, models, data, and user interactions. Monitor: Availability Request volume Latency Error rates Resource utilization Model performance Data quality Data drift Concept drift Prediction distributions LLM response quality Hallucination and safety indicators Token consumption Cost per request Establish dashboards, alerts, service-level indicators, and service-level objectives. Integrate monitoring with incident management and on-call processes. Enable traceability from user requests through model inference, retrieval, orchestration, and downstream services. Support root-cause analysis by maintaining structured logs, metrics, traces, model lineage, and deployment history. Security and Governance Implement security controls for model-serving environments, APIs, data access, and deployment pipelines. Apply least-privilege access using AWS IAM, Databricks permissions, service principals, and role-based access control. Secure secrets, credentials, API keys, certificates, and tokens using approved secrets-management solutions. Implement encryption in transit and at rest. Design private networking, endpoint controls, firewall rules, and secure connectivity patterns. Support authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and tenant isolation for AI services. Ensure models and LLM applications comply with organizational requirements for privacy, security, auditability, and responsible AI. Maintain model lineage, approval records, version history, and deployment audit trails. Implement controls for sensitive data, personally identifiable information, prompt injection, unsafe outputs, and unauthorized model access. Infrastructure as Code and Automation Build and maintain cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or AWS CloudFormation. Automate environment provisioning, policy enforcement, deployment configuration, and platform upgrades. Create reusable modules, templates, libraries, and deployment frameworks. Implement configuration management and environment-specific parameterization. Ensure infrastructure changes are peer-reviewed, tested, version-controlled, and traceable. Collaboration and Engineering Standards Partner with data scientists and ML engineers to productionize models and define deployment requirements. Work with software engineering teams to integrate model endpoints into user-facing products and internal applications. Collaborate with cybersecurity, architecture, legal, privacy, and governance teams. Define MLOps engineering standards, design principles, coding practices, and operational requirements. Conduct architecture reviews, code reviews, and production-readiness assessments. Machine Learning Experience : Significant experience in MLOps, platform engineering, DevOps, site reliability engineering, cloud engineering, or production machine learning. Proven experience deploying and operating machine learning models in production. Strong hands-on experience with AWS services and cloud architecture. Strong hands-on experience with Databricks, including MLflow, model registries, jobs, clusters, permissions, and model-serving capabilities. Experience building CI/CD pipelines using tools such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, or AWS CodePipeline, Docker and containerized application deployment. Experience with REST APIs, asynchronous processing, event-driven architectures, and distributed systems. Strong knowledge of Infrastructure as Code, preferably Terraform. Experience with model versioning, artifact management, experiment tracking, and deployment promotion workflows. Experience implementing monitoring, logging, tracing, alerting, and production support processes. Strong understanding of high availability, disaster recovery, fault tolerance, and rollback strategies. Knowledge of cloud networking, IAM, secrets management, encryption, and secure software delivery. Training and inference workflows Online and batch inference Model serialization and packaging Feature engineering and feature consistency Model validation and evaluation,l drift and data drift Model explainability and reproducibility GPU-based model serving Embeddings and vector databases Retrieval-augmented generation Prompt management and versioning LLM evaluation and guardrails Token limits, context management, and inference cost optimization Responsible AI, content safety, and human-in-the-loop controls This role does not necessarily require the candidate to develop new machine learning algorithms. jobs.title: Senior Azure DevOps Engineer
jobs.description: Job Details: Job Description: Senior Azure DevOps Engineer - Full-Stack and Hybrid Cloud Systems Bangalore, India ' Full-Time About the Role We are looking for an experienced, versatile Azure DevOps Engineer to join our team and become a genuine part of what we are building. This is not a straightforward DevOps role. Our system spans a full-stack web application, a rich and deliberately complex Azure cloud environment, and on-premises Linux lab infrastructure that talks directly to FPGA hardware. The person who thrives here will be someone who gets energized by that kind of variety, not overwhelmed by it. Just as importantly, we are looking for someone who communicates well, enjoys working closely with developers and customers, and takes real pride in the quality and reliability of what they build and maintain. Technical depth matters, but so does being someone the team genuinely enjoys working with. The Environment You Will Be Working In The Application We build and operate a full-stack web application with a Node.js server, TypeScript services, and a React.js client. The application connects to on-premises Linux lab environments where a Python-based layer orchestrates and controls FPGA hardware. The cloud and the physical lab need to talk to each other reliably, securely, and continuously. The Internal Azure Subscription This environment is mature, fully operational, and genuinely complex. Containerized workloads run on Kubernetes. We use the right database for the right job: relational databases for structured data, a document store for flexibility, in-memory caching for performance, distributed file storage for shared access, and large-scale telemetry and analytics through Azure Data Explorer. Identity and access management spans SSO, Active Directory, Kerberos, and Microsoft Entra ID, because our permission model is real-world complex, not textbook simple. We also run an internal HPC-grade job scheduling system that manages compute resource allocation and permissions across lab infrastructure. The External Azure Subscription This subscription is starting now and will serve customers outside our organization. jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager — Multi-Entity Account Scale & Access Lifecycle
jobs.description: Overview Intuit's Identity organization is seeking a Staff Technical Program Manager to focus on how our platform scales for large and complex customers. Our Identity Platform is the primary gateway for millions of customers across TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp — a durable strategic lever that ensures personalized experiences are delivered with world-class security and compliance. This role sits at the center of one of Intuit's largest growth bets: serving customers whose organizations look nothing like a single-owner small business. Accounting firms managing hundreds of clients. Multi-entity businesses running dozens of legal entities across currencies and locations. Mid-market companies with real hierarchies, real headcount, and real governance requirements. The users you build for are the people your customers employ — the staff, contractors, and accountants they invite into their own Intuit account — and the platform they administer today was designed for a much smaller shape of customer. You will own two initiatives end to end. Scale is the work of taking our account model from hundreds of entities to thousands, delivering bulk and group-level administration, and standing up an API-first surface so customers and partners can manage identity programmatically rather than one user at a time. Access automation is the work of making the joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle automatic — permissions applied correctly the moment someone is added, revoked the moment they leave, with the audit trail to prove it — collapsing onboarding that takes weeks and eliminating access that outlives the person who held it. We need an AI Native, results-oriented and empathetic technical leader who can navigate complex system architectures, establish order in ambiguity, and drive technical excellence in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. This role is based in Bengaluru India and partners daily with the engineering and product teams driving both initiatives. Responsibilities Drive Technical Excellence: Own and drive two critical identity programs — multi-entity account scale and automated access lifecycle — from scope definition through launch and adoption. Navigate complex microservice architectures, multi-tenant account and permission models, and intricate system dependencies to deliver capabilities that are secure, performant, and reliable at scale. Own the Scale Initiative: Drive the work of taking our account model from hundreds of entities to thousands — hierarchies, groups, bulk administration, and an API-first surface so customers and partners can manage identity programmatically rather than one user at a time. Dive deep into the technical subject matter and re-emerge with an end-to-end blueprint the delivery teams can execute against. Own the Access Automation Initiative: Drive the joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle to automatic — permissions applied correctly the moment someone is added, revoked the moment they leave, with the audit trail to prove it. Partner with engineering on the provisioning architecture and with product on the administrative experience that sits on top of it. Connect Strategy to Execution: Synthesize business strategy, customer signals, and delivery realities to prioritize across both initiatives and keep teams focused on the highest-impact outcomes. Lead the tradeoff discussions, recommend the execution path, and ensure follow-through with stakeholders. Execute with Rigor: Partner across teams to define program outcomes, build the end-to-end delivery plan, and establish the governance model for both initiatives. Develop and drive the operating rhythm — planning, reviews, cutline sessions, and decision forums — that sets direction and instills accountability. Own Risks and Dependencies: Both initiatives carry committed dependencies from product teams across Intuit. Uncover risks and dependencies before they materialize, proactively escalate blockers, determine the optimal path to green, and hold partner teams to dated commitments. Identity Architecture Partnership: Work with Identity Architects and engineering leaders to ensure account hierarchy, provisioning, and access patterns scale consistently across the Intuit ecosystem, and that both initiatives compose cleanly with the authorization and governance work running alongside them. Lead Change Through Migration and Adoption: Own the path from the current account model to the new one — not just the capability, but how existing customers get there without disruption. Identify the impact of key changes, develop the change plan, and exhibit extreme ownership driving from plan to sustained adoption, tracking that customers actually move rather than that the feature shipped. Enable Scale and Velocity: Build the frameworks, tooling, and instrumentation that make identity program delivery repeatable — and apply AI agent tools to accelerate program analysis, delivery, and stakeholder communication, evaluating AI-generated program artifacts with the same rigor applied to human-generated output. Qualifications Experience: 8+ years in technical program management within platform organizations or high-scale software development environments, including demonstrated ownership of programs spanning multiple engineering organizations. Education: BA/BS in Computer Science, Information Systems, or an equivalent technical degree. Identity Platform Depth: Direct experience delivering customer identity and access management (CIAM) capabilities — authentication, authorization, account and organization modeling, or user provisioning and administration — in a product-facing platform serving external customers at scale. Access Model Fluency: Working knowledge of role- and attribute-based access control (RBAC/ABAC/PBAC), permission and entitlement models, delegated administration, and the failure modes that come with them — over-permissioning, role sprawl, and orphaned access. Multi-Tenant Hierarchy Modeling: Experience with systems that represent a customer's own organizational structure — parent/child entities, groups, delegated admins, cross-organization access — and the design tradeoffs between flexibility and comprehensibility at scale. Technical Domain Expertise: Strong grasp of SDLC methodologies, microservices architecture, and platform design, with the systems thinking to form an end-to-end blueprint in an unfamiliar problem area and the credibility to be treated as a thought partner by technical stakeholders. Fluency with API-first delivery, including developer-facing surfaces and programmatic administration. Scale Judgment: Demonstrated experience taking a platform capability from a small-customer design point to a large-customer design point, including the migration path for customers already on the old model. AI-Native Delivery: Demonstrated use of AI agents and tools in your own program work to accelerate analysis, structure delivery, and sharpen stakeholder communication — with firsthand judgment about where AI accelerates delivery and where it introduces risk. Leadership Style: Proven ability to lead through influence rather than authority, at a scope where you define the program rather than inherit it. Credibility as a boundaryless change leader who drives from plan to sustained adoption. You are a self-starter who values "Leadership as a Coach" and supports the growth of those around you. Communication: Excellent articulate and warm communication skills, with strong written fluency. You can compress a complex program into a page an executive can act on, and simplify technical problems into actionable insight for engineers and leaders alike. Problem Solving: Demonstrated ability to establish order in ambiguous situations and use rapid experimentation to learn fast and pivot when necessary. Analytical Skills: Strong data-driven mindset with the ability to track and report on program health, delivery velocity, and customer impact metrics. Preferred: Experience with identity standards and protocols (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, ReBAC/ABAC engines such as OPA); B2B or B2B2C SaaS serving mid-market or larger customers; experience delivering through partner, reseller, or professional-services channels. jobs.description: Who We Are At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses. The Role The Role: You are the offshore specialist leader for tenant‑to‑tenant endpoint migration readiness and escalation support. You guide Scale squads and the Factory through device migration sequencing, Intune re‑enrolment impacts, Autopilot/join‑state considerations and remediation patterns. This role is critical to avoiding mass disruption: endpoint readiness issues can block user productivity at wave cutovers, so your job is to standardise solutions, reduce repeat failures and provide rapid escalation leadership during cutover windows. Who You Are Key Responsibilities: Provide endpoint readiness guidance and risk assessments for migration waves. Act as escalation authority for complex device migration failures and root cause analysis. Define and maintain runbooks for common remediation scenarios (enrolment failures, compliance issues, profile/application targeting problems). Coordinate dependencies with Identity and Security teams (device trust and access controls). Support cutover events with rapid triage and stabilisation leadership. Maintain known‑issues and fixes catalogue; reduce recurring defects through standard patterns. Provide validation criteria and evidence standards for endpoint readiness and post‑migration acceptance. Support the Factory discipline leads by improving troubleshooting playbooks and telemetry standards. Provide reporting inputs on failure categories, remediation throughput and readiness health metrics. Align to one region and adjust working patterns to support regional cutovers. Must‑Have: Delivered tenant‑to‑tenant endpoint migration work in production (Intune/Windows specialism mandatory). Deep Intune operational expertise and troubleshooting competence. Practical understanding of device join state and provisioning concepts relevant to tenant transitions. Proven ability to create runbooks, validation steps and known‑fix playbooks for repeatable execution. Willingness to align working hours to regional cutovers (early/late calls) and support extended hours when required. Strong documentation discipline and evidence‑first practices. Ability to coach engineers and improve delivery maturity at pace. Good‑to‑Have: Experience with workstation/profile migration tooling (e.g., PowerSyncPro or equivalent) and hands‑on understanding of real‑world constraints. Microsoft certification alignment relevant to endpoint management (or equivalent experience). PowerShell scripting for diagnostics, readiness reporting and bulk remediation. Experience with large, globally distributed device estates and remote workforce constraints. Interpersonal & Consulting Skills: Calm escalation leadership in user‑impacting cutover events. Clear communicator: logs, evidence and precise guidance rather than guesswork. Strong coaching and collaboration behaviours across shifts and teams. Risk and dependency management mindset; prevents avoidable disruption. High integrity around access/security and change discipline. Strong written communication: tickets, handovers, playbooks. Typical Deliverables / KPIs: Lower endpoint migration failure rate and improved first‑time success. MTTR for endpoint migration blockers during cutovers. Repeat issue reduction via improved runbooks and known‑fix catalogues. Evidence completion rate for endpoint acceptance checks. Readiness pass rate for endpoint components at wave entry. Shift / Working Pattern Notes: Scale teams operate as a cohesive unit within a follow‑the‑sun project delivery model. Each scale team works an 8‑hour shift, scheduled across a 24‑hour global working day. Structured handovers between scale teams are mandatory and cutover periods may require rota flexibility. The Metal/Plastic Forming & Processing Technology Project Team is responsible for innovating and optimizing the core manufacturing processes that give shape to LG's appliance components — from sheet metal stamping and forming to plastic injection molding and secondary processing. We bridge the gap between advanced material discovery, component design, and mass production. The ideal candidate will join us as a Process Engineer to drive the next generation of forming and processing technologies that deliver lighter, stronger, more cost-effective, and sustainable components. Responsibilities Metal Forming Process Development Process Optimization: Design and optimize sheet metal stamping, bending, drawing, piercing, and assembly processes for appliance chassis, drums, baskets, and structural parts. Tooling & Die Development: Collaborate with internal tooling partners and die makers to develop new tooling strategies, including progressive dies, transfer presses, and fine-blanking tooling. Material Utilization: Evaluate and reduce material waste through nesting optimization, scrap minimization, and lightweight gauge optimization while maintaining structural integrity. Formability Analysis: Perform limitation diagram analysis (LDI / FEM simulation) to predict cracking, wrinkling, and earing in sheet metal processes; validate through physical testing. Plastic Processing Process Development Injection Molding Optimization: Develop process windows for gate design, runner layout, cooling channel configuration, and mold flow analysis to achieve balanced fill, minimal warpage, and zero shorts. Intelligent Molding Systems: Leverage LG's proprietary intelligent injection molding systems — including real-time cavity pressure monitoring, AI-driven process control, and adaptive feedforward/feedback loops — to improve cycle time and first-pass yieldlgcorp.com +1. Mold Flow Simulation: Use Moldflow or equivalent software to simulate and optimize flow patterns, weld-line location, sink marks, shrinkage, and residual stress in complex molded parts. Material Compatibility: Evaluate thermoplastics (ABS, PP, PC/ABS, PA blends), reinforced composites, and recycled-content materials for formability, mold release, and post-processing compatibility. Cross-Functional Collaboration Work closely with the HS Material Application Technology Team to ensure material characteristics align with processing windows and product performance targets. Support DFM / DFA (Design for Manufacturing / Assembly) reviews with industrial and design engineers to reduce costs, improve manufacturability, and shorten time-to-market. Partner with Quality Engineering to define process capability studies (Cp/Cpk), Root Cause Analysis (8D/FMEA), and control plans for new programs. Sustainability & Cost Innovation Reduce scrap rates and improve material yield (target: 21%+ productivity gain through intelligent process integration. Explore lightweight die casting, hot-stamping, and high-strength steel applications to reduce the weight of appliance structures without compromising durability. Evaluate biodegradable, bio-based, or recycled plastics for processing feasibility in injection molding, supporting LG's carbon-neutral and ESG. Documentation & Specification Develop and update Process Specification Sheets, Control Plans, PFMEA, and Traveler Documents for manufacturing release. Maintain Material Master Data and Bill of Process documentation in PLM systems (Teamcenter) Technical Requirements M.Tech (Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or related field) ideally from reputed institutes (NITs / IITs). 1+ years of relevant experience in metal forming, plastic injection molding, or advanced manufacturing process engineering. Proficiency in CAE/FEA tools (Moldflow, AutoForm, PAM-STAMP, DEFORM, LS-DYNA); hands-on experience with process simulation and DOE (Design of Experiments) methodology; working knowledge of mold design and die construction. Familiarity with quality standards: IATF 16949, ISO 9001, GD&T (ASME Y14.5), AIAG Core Tools (APQP, FMEA, SPC, MSA). Fluent in Business-level English; Korean language skills are a plus Core Competencies and Working Attitude Technical Depth: Deep understanding of material behavior during deformation, flow, and phase change — metal plasticity and polymer rheology. Problem Solving: Analytical data-driven approach to identify root causes of process variation, surface defects, dimensional instability, and scrap generation. Systems Thinking : Ability to see the forming and processing workflow holistically — from raw material receipt through in-process quality gates to final assembly. Communication: Clear documentation and presentation of complex technical findings to cross-functional audiences including design, quality, procurement, and manufacturing. Ownership: Self-motivated with ability to manage multiple project streams simultaneously, driving each from concept through deployment. Innovation Mindset: Curious about emerging technologies — additive manufacturing for tooling, self-healing materials, and cold spray metallurgy — and assessing their commercial viability.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Title and Summary Senior Data Engineer Overview We are the global technology company behind the world’s fastest payments processing network. We are a vehicle for commerce, a connection to financial systems for the previously excluded, a technology innovation lab, and the home of Priceless®. We ensure every employee has the opportunity to be a part of something bigger and to change lives. We believe as our company grows, so should you. We believe in connecting everyone to endless, priceless possibilities. Our team within Mastercard – Data & Services: The Data & Services team is a key differentiator for Mastercard, providing the cutting-edge services that are used by some of the world's largest organizations to make multi-million dollar decisions and grow their businesses. Focused on thinking big and scaling fast around the globe, this agile team is responsible for end-to-end solutions for a diverse global customer base. Centered on data-driven technologies and innovation, these services include payments-focused consulting, loyalty and marketing programs, business Test & Learn experimentation, and data-driven information and risk management services. Data Analytics and AI Solutions (DAAI) Program: Within the D&S Technology Team, the DAAI program is a relatively new program that is comprised of a rich set of products that provide accurate perspectives on Portfolio Optimization, and Ad Insights. Currently, we are enhancing our customer experience with new user interfaces, moving to API and web application-based data publishing to allow for seamless integration in other Mastercard products and externally, utilizing new data sets and algorithms to further analytic capabilities, and generating scalable big data processes. We are looking for an innovative software engineering lead who will lead the technical design and development of an Analytic Foundation. The Analytic Foundation is a suite of individually commercialized analytical capabilities (think prediction as a service, matching as a service or forecasting as a service) that also includes a comprehensive data platform. These services will be offered through a series of APIs that deliver data and insights from various points along a central data store. This individual will partner closely with other areas of the business to build and enhance solutions that drive value for our customers. Engineers work in small, flexible teams. Every team member contributes to designing, building, and testing features. The range of work you will encounter varies from building intuitive, responsive UIs to designing backend data models, architecting data flows, and beyond. There are no rigid organizational structures, and each team uses processes that work best for its members and projects. Here are a few examples of products in our space: Portfolio Optimizer (PO) is a solution that leverages Mastercard’s data assets and analytics to allow issuers to identify and increase revenue opportunities within their credit and debit portfolios. Ad Insights uses anonymized and aggregated transaction insights to offer targeting segments that have high likelihood to make purchases within a category to allow for more effective campaign planning and activation. Help found a new, fast-growing engineering team!
