jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Amazon moves millions of packages daily through a global logistics network of Fulfillment Centers, Sort Centers, and Delivery Stations. Every facility has a trailer yard — the physical space where line-haul vehicles arrive, get loaded or unloaded, and depart. Tracking what's happening in these yards in real time (which trailers are where, what state they're in, who's arriving and departing) is a hard problem that sits at the intersection of physical operations and software systems. The Relay Yard Automation (RYA) team builds the software that manages these trailer yards across 6,000+ Amazon facilities on three continents. Our products handle 200K+ gate transactions per day and facilitated the arrival and departure of 55M vehicles last year. We integrate computer vision, RFID, GPS, ultrasonic sensors, and IoT edge devices to automate what were historically manual, associate-staffed processes, from gate check-in/check-out to in-yard trailer movements. Our gate automation program has already eliminated millions of manual transactions, with a long-term goal of fully autonomous yard operations. The tech stack is diverse by necessity: Android mobile apps for yard associates and drivers, React web applications for remote gate agents and yard operators, Java/TypeScript backend services on AWS, and hardware integrations running on edge compute devices deployed in the field. Systems are loosely coupled, event-driven, and must operate reliably in environments ranging from 1M+ sq ft North American fulfillment centers to small urban European delivery stations. As an SDE on this team, you will design and build features and services that power yard automation across Amazon's logistics network. You will write high-quality code across the full stack, contribute to system design discussions, and deliver projects from technical design through production launch. The role involves working across backend services, web and mobile applications, and integrations with physical sensor systems at the edge. You will make thoughtful engineering trade-offs, participate in design and code reviews, and contribute to the team's operational excellence practices — supporting tier-1 systems where your work directly impacts driver experience and Amazon's ability to meet customer delivery promises. Key job responsibilities Design and implement software for yard and gate automation products across tier-1 systems. Your code runs in production where defects directly impact driver experience and customer delivery promises. Lead large projects end-to-end: define the technical approach in ambiguous problem spaces, decompose work into parallel workstreams, and deliver cohesive launches. Own system architecture for your team's services. Proactively simplify code, resolve architecture deficiencies, and remove bottlenecks across Java backend services, TypeScript/React web apps, Android mobile apps, and IoT edge devices. Make short-term vs. long-term trade-off decisions and communicate them clearly to your team and stakeholders. Integrate with physical systems — RFID readers, computer vision cameras, ultrasonic sensors, GPS — running on edge compute in variable warehouse environments. Debug problems that span hardware and cloud software. Own operational excellence for services you build: monitoring, alarming, runbooks, incident response, and root-cause corrective actions. Influence technical direction beyond your team through design reviews with partner teams across Transportation Technology. Act as a force multiplier. jobs.description: Company: Qualcomm India Private Limited Job Area: Engineering Group, Engineering Group > Systems Engineering General Summary: As part of Qualcomm's AI Software organisation, this role focuses on developing embedded software and hardware drivers for next-generation low-power accelerator and multi-DSP platforms on Qualcomm Snapdragon products. The engineer will design and optimise low-level software across operating-system services, memory subsystems, device drivers and inter-processor communication, enabling reliable, power-efficient operation across mobile and edge platforms. Key Responsibilities Design, implement, integrate and test embedded software, firmware and runtime components for low-power accelerator and DSP subsystems. Develop and maintain hardware drivers for machine-learning accelerators, including device initialisation, resource management, interrupt handling, power-state transitions and error recovery. Design software for multi-DSP and heterogeneous compute architectures, including workload partitioning, synchronisation and coordination across processors. Implement and optimise inter-processor communication mechanisms such as shared-memory transport, message queues, signalling, interrupts and remote procedure calls. Develop robust memory-management solutions covering static and dynamic allocation, memory pools, shared memory, virtual-to-physical address translation, cache coherency and DMA handling. Analyse and optimise embedded software for latency, throughput, memory footprint and power consumption on target platforms. Debug complex system-level issues involving operating systems, drivers, firmware, concurrency, memory corruption and processor interactions using target debugging and profiling tools. Build unit, integration and system-level test frameworks for embedded software and hardware-driver validation. Collaborate with hardware, systems, firmware and platform software teams on architecture, bring-up, integration, validation and commercialisation. Required Skills and Experience Strong embedded C programming skills, with hands-on experience in low-level software development; working knowledge of C++ is desirable. Strong understanding of operating-system concepts, including processes and threads, scheduling, synchronisation, interrupts, timers, virtual memory and device-driver models. Hands-on experience with RTOS and/or embedded Linux environments, including board bring-up, kernel-facing interfaces and system debugging. Deep understanding of memory handling in embedded systems, including stack and heap usage, memory pools, alignment, fragmentation, memory protection, cache behaviour and coherency. Experience with multi-core, multi-DSP or heterogeneous processor architectures and associated concurrency challenges. Experience implementing inter-processor communication using shared memory, mailboxes, message queues, interrupts, RPC or equivalent mechanisms. Experience developing hardware drivers, preferably for accelerator, DSP, NPU or other high-performance compute blocks. Good understanding of computer architecture, including CPU/DSP pipelines, caches, MMU/IOMMU, DMA, bus interfaces and memory-mapped I/O. Experience with multi-threaded programming, POSIX/Pthreads, synchronisation primitives and race-condition analysis. Proficiency with embedded debugging and profiling tools such as JTAG, trace tools, crash dumps, logic analysers and performance profilers. Strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, software design and fixed-point programming. Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with cross-functional, geographically distributed teams. Preferred Qualifications Strong system-level understanding of SoC architecture, including CPU, DSP, NPU/AI accelerators, memory hierarchy, cache coherency, DMA engines, buses, and interconnects, with the ability to analyze hardware-software interactions effectively. Proven experience interpreting hardware architecture specifications, programming guides, register descriptions, and functional specifications to design, develop, and optimize low-level software and hardware drivers. Hands-on experience developing and debugging hardware drivers based on hardware documentation, including device initialization, interrupt handling, power management, resource management, error recovery, and performance optimization. Strong understanding of system bring-up, boot flows, clock and reset frameworks, power domains, memory subsystems, and platform resource management. Familiarity with secure execution environments, memory protection mechanisms, fault-tolerant embedded software design, and system reliability considerations. Experience with performance analysis and optimization using hardware performance counters, processor-specific instruction sets, compiler optimizations, and low-level profiling techniques. Expertise in transistor-level design and analysis of static CMOS circuits, including state-retaining elements such as latches and flip-flops. jobs.description: Job ID 2026-17387 Date posted Jun. 01, 2026 Location Bengaluru, India Category Software Engineering Staff Firmware Engineer - Memory Subsystem Lead Arm has built the world’s most pervasive compute architecture, powering computing wherever it happens – from embedded and automotive systems to cloud and data center infrastructure. As Arm continues to grow its presence in server and infrastructure markets, system software plays a critical role in enabling high-quality, production-ready platforms for customers and partners. This role sits within Arm’s System Solutions software organization, working on software for Arm Neoverse–based platforms, from early bring-up and validation on pre-silicon platforms through to production-quality firmware on real silicon, while providing technical and people leadership in a focus group responsible for memory subsystem enablement, platform bring-up, system configuration, performance, and firmware quality. We are looking for an experienced Staff Firmware Engineer with strong low-level software expertise and leadership capability to lead firmware development for the memory subsystem across next-generation infrastructure platforms. This role requires deep technical judgment, strong cross-team collaboration, and the ability to guide a small team through complex hardware/software integration challenges from early models through silicon bring-up and production readiness. Job purpose and accountabilities Responsibilities: Lead technical delivery (development, integration and validation) of the memory subsystem focus area across pre-silicon platforms and silicon bring-up environments, ensuring robust operation across development and production milestones. Collaborate closely with hardware, validation, platform firmware and system architecture, teams to ensure coherent memory subsystem bring-up and integration across the wider platform. Debug complex system-level issues across hardware/software boundaries, using strong understanding of firmware flows, platform configuration, memory behavior, and system interactions. Optimize memory subsystem behavior for correctness, performance, latency, bandwidth, reliability, and power efficiency, making clear trade-offs based on platform goals and customer needs. Remain technically engaged by reviewing designs, implementation plans, validation results, and critical code, while contributing hands-on when needed to guide or unblock delivery. Line manage 3-5 engineers, including goal setting, coaching, feedback, performance evaluation, and development of technical capability within the team. Mentor engineers and provide technical leadership across teams in the memory subsystem domain, helping establish good engineering practices, documentation, debug discipline, and long-term software quality. Required Skills and Experience : Solid industry experience building complex firmware or low-level system software, combined with demonstrated leadership or mentoring and a strong track record of delivery. Experience of 10-15 Years is Must Background in firmware development on pre-silicon and silicon platforms, preferably on Arm-based systems, demonstrated through ownership, review, and guidance of complex technical designs. Extensive knowledge of enabling the memory subsystem in system software, including areas such as memory initialization, platform configuration, controller/PHY interaction, training flows, error handling, performance tuning, or bring-up debug. Sound technical judgment, including assessing trade-offs, managing technical risk and debugging ambiguous system-level failures Experience working at the intersection of hardware and software, showing capacity to work effectively with hardware build, validation, system architecture, platform firmware, and QA teams. Strong communication skills and a history of effective collaboration across teams and sites. Able to explain complex memory subsystem issues clearly to both specialists and broader platform collaborators. “Nice To Have” Skills and Experience : Experience working on server or infrastructure platforms, including customer- or production-facing environments. Understanding of system architecture, preferably Arm, including boot flows, firmware interfaces, OS fundamentals, device drivers, and platform configuration. Experience with DDR, LPDDR, memory controllers, PHY initialization, ECC, RAS, memory performance analysis, or board/silicon bring-up. Understanding of software development standard processes, including testing strategies, CI, validation planning, release readiness, and defect triage. Experience working in globally distributed teams. In Return: You will have the opportunity to lead critical firmware work for the memory subsystem on groundbreaking infrastructure technology, with scope to influence technical direction, platform bring-up, performance, delivery outcomes, and team culture within a highly skilled global engineering organization! jobs.title: Scaled AI & Solution Architect
jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY The Scaled AI & Solution Architect is the senior technical design authority for the Digital Quality (DQ) organisation, which delivers the solutions that transform Quality, Safety and Environmental Operations (QSEO) across Pfizer. The role is a global individual contributor position accountable for setting and driving the AI and solution architecture direction across the entire DQ product portfolio, rather than for the delivery of any single product. The incumbent defines the target architecture, reference patterns, reusable components and engineering standards that every DQ solution is built against, so that capability is built once and reused many times rather than rebuilt product by product. The role leads the scaled adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and agentic AI across the portfolio, translating enterprise AI platforms and emerging technology into GxP-compliant, validated, production-grade capability that measurably improves quality, safety and environmental outcomes at site level. Recognised as an expert within and beyond Digital Quality, the incumbent influences the strategic technology direction of the QSEO business, and partners with Solution Leads, the Platform and Solution Engineering team, Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security to ensure architectural coherence, compliance and pace across a complex global portfolio. ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES Cross-Product Solution Architecture Own the target-state solution architecture for the Digital Quality portfolio, spanning quality management, laboratory, manufacturing quality, and safety, environment and occupational health solutions. Define how products, platforms, data and integrations fit together, and drive convergence of point solutions onto common architecture, avoiding duplicated capability and unmanaged technical debt across the portfolio. Architecture Standards, Patterns and Reusable Components Establish, publish and maintain the architecture standards, reference patterns, reusable components and engineering guardrails that DQ solutions are designed and built against, covering integration, data, identity, AI, validation and cyber security. Make reuse the path of least resistance for delivery teams, and measure adoption, reuse and the resulting delivery efficiency. Scaled AI Enablement Define and drive the AI and agentic AI architecture for the DQ portfolio, including use case patterns such as deviation and incident triage, leading-indicator prediction, automated document and content generation, and conversational access to standards and procedures. Determine where AI capability should be built once as a shared service versus configured per product, and ensure AI is delivered on enterprise platforms with appropriate human oversight, evaluation, model monitoring and lifecycle management. Design Authority and Technical Governance Act as design authority for significant DQ investments, reviewing and approving solution designs at key lifecycle gates and providing architectural assurance on build-versus-buy, platform selection and vendor technical fit. Identify multiple viable options for highly complex problems, set out the trade-offs in cost, risk, compliance and time to value, and make clear recommendations to Digital and business leadership and relevant governance forums. Technical Leadership and Capability Building Provide hands-on architectural leadership to Solution Leads, Product Managers, engineers and vendor teams across the portfolio without direct reporting authority, influencing through expertise, credibility and evidence. Mentor and raise the technical capability of architects and engineers across Digital Quality, and lead architecture and AI Communities of Practice that spread good practice across DQ and the wider Digital organisation. Compliance, Data Integrity and Security by Design Ensure architectural decisions embed GxP computerised system compliance, data integrity, data privacy and cyber security requirements from the outset, in partnership with Quality, Legal, Privacy, Compliance and Cyber Security. Define validation-efficient architecture patterns that allow AI and cloud capability to be deployed at pace while remaining inspection-ready. Innovation and Emerging Technology Exercise foresight in evaluating emerging AI, data and platform technologies, and act independently on self-initiated proofs of concept and technical experiments that challenge the status quo and shape the multi-year DQ technology roadmap. Take appropriate, well-governed technical risk, and translate proven experiments into scaled, supportable production capability with a defined adoption path. QUALIFICATIONS Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree required in Information Technology, Engineering, Environmental or Occupational Health Sciences, Life Sciences or a related discipline. 10+ years of relevant experience in in solution architecture, technical leadership or enterprise software delivery (9+ years with an MS/MBA; 7+ years with a PhD), including demonstrable accountability for architecture across a portfolio of products rather than a single application. Demonstrated experience designing and delivering AI or machine learning capability into production, including an understanding of large language model and agentic architecture patterns, retrieval, evaluation and model lifecycle management. Strong experience with cloud, integration and data architecture, and with modern software engineering and Agile ways of working; SAFe preferred. Experience setting and driving adoption of technical standards across teams that do not report to the incumbent, influencing senior stakeholders through technical credibility. Experience across all stages of the system and application lifecycle, from value analysis and business case through deployment to value realisation and technical debt management. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical trade-offs to non-technical senior leaders. Preferred Qualifications Experience in the pharmaceutical industry or another highly regulated manufacturing environment, including GxP computerised system validation and data integrity expectations (e.g. GAMP 5, 21 CFR Part 11, Annex 11). Working knowledge of quality, or EHS business processes and the platforms that support them (for example Veeva, LIMS, Cority). Experience deploying AI in a regulated context, including responsible AI governance, model risk assessment and human-in-the-loop design. Recognised architecture certification (e.g. TOGAF) or equivalent cloud architecture certification. Track record of external technical contribution — industry forums, working groups, publications or conference speaking. PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS Typical desk job; no specific physical or mental requirements beyond standard office work. NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS Occasional travel up to 20% Ability to work with colleagues virtually across different regions and time zones, including occasional out-of-hours working to support deployment go-lives and hypercare. ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIONSHIPS Reports into Pfizer Digital, PGS, Enabling Functions & Enterprise Platforms – Digital Quality Lead. Key internal relationships include Enterprise Architecture, the enterprise AI and Data organization, Cyber Security, Digital Compliance and Computerized System Validation, Legal and Privacy, and senior business stakeholders across Quality and EHS in Pfizer Global Supply. External: strategic software and AI vendors, cloud and platform providers, implementation and managed service partners, and relevant industry and regulatory technical forums. RESOURCES MANAGED Financial Accountability No direct budget ownership. Influences the architecture and technology decisions underpinning the Digital Quality portfolio representing approximately $10M of annual software, services and transformation investment, and is accountable for identifying reuse and rationalization opportunities that improve return on that investment Supervision Individual contributor with no direct reports. Provides technical direction and design authority to matrixed teams of product, engineering, data, validation and vendor resources across the Digital Quality portfolio, and mentors architects and senior engineers across the organization. Work Location Assignment: Hybrid Pfizer is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable equal employment opportunity legislation in each jurisdiction in which it operates. jobs.title: Platform & Solution Engineering Lead
jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY The Platform and Solution Engineering Lead owns the technical foundation on which the entire Digital Quality (DQ) portfolio is built, delivered and operated. Digital Quality delivers the solutions that transform Quality, Safety and Environmental Operations (QSEO) across Pfizer, and this role is accountable for the platforms, engineering capability and delivery pipelines that allow that portfolio to move at pace while remaining compliant, secure and supportable. The incumbent leads a global engineering organisation covering platform engineering, solution architecture and design, integration and data engineering, DevSecOps, environment and release management, and vendor delivery oversight. Accountability spans the full technology mix — Software as a Service (SaaS), commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and in-house developed solutions — ensuring each is engineered, integrated, validated and operated to a consistent standard rather than as isolated stacks. The role is the engineering counterpart to the DQ Solution Leads, who own product strategy and business outcomes, and to the Scaled AI and Solution Architect, who sets cross-portfolio architecture direction and standards; this role is accountable for making those standards real in code, configuration, pipelines and operations. It is also the principal point of alignment between Digital Quality and the wider enterprise technology landscape, including Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security, the enterprise AI and Data organisation, and central platform and infrastructure teams. The role is global in scope, spanning the PGS network, R&D, commercial markets and corporate locations. ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES Platform Engineering and Technical Foundation Own the strategy, engineering and lifecycle of the shared technical foundation for Digital Quality, including cloud footprint, runtime platforms, shared services, reusable components, developer tooling and non-production environments. Build the foundation as a product used by delivery teams across the portfolio, with defined service levels, roadmaps, adoption measures and a managed path for retiring legacy and duplicated technology. Solution Engineering Across SaaS, COTS and Custom Build Provide engineering leadership and design accountability across the full technology mix, establishing how SaaS platforms are configured and extended, how COTS products are deployed and integrated, and how in-house applications are designed, built and maintained. Ensure engineering rigour, supportability and consistent quality regardless of delivery model, and prevent unmanaged customisation that undermines upgradability and cost of ownership. Integration and Data Engineering Own the integration and data engineering layer connecting Digital Quality solutions to each other and to the wider Pfizer landscape, including manufacturing, laboratory, enterprise resource planning and enterprise data platforms. Establish reusable integration patterns, interfaces and data contracts, and ensure integrations are resilient, monitored, documented and compliant with data integrity requirements. DevSecOps, Release and Environment Management Define and run the engineering operating model for Digital Quality, covering source control, continuous integration and delivery pipelines, automated testing, security scanning, infrastructure as code, and environment and release management. Drive automation of validation and compliance evidence so that release frequency, deployment reliability and lead time improve without weakening GxP control. Own the release calendar and change governance across the portfolio, including coordination of platform vendor release cycles. Vendor and Managed Service Delivery Hold strategic technology vendors, systems integrators and managed service partners to account for engineering quality, delivery commitments, security posture and service performance. Shape sourcing strategy and the internal-versus-partner capability mix, define technical standards and acceptance criteria in statements of work, and manage capacity and demand across internal and external engineering teams. Enterprise Technology Alignment Act as the principal interface between Digital Quality and enterprise technology functions, ensuring DQ solutions adopt enterprise platforms, standards and services rather than building parallel capability. Influence enterprise roadmaps, standards and investment decisions on behalf of the QSEO domain, and represent Digital Quality in enterprise architecture, cyber security and technology governance forums. Organisational Leadership Lead, develop and grow a global engineering team of approximately 8–10 direct reports, spanning platform engineers, solution architects, integration and data engineers, DevSecOps and release specialists, alongside matrixed and contract resources. Build engineering capability, talent pipelines and succession plans; set technical performance expectations and career pathways; and foster a culture of engineering excellence, automation, innovation, accountability and continuous improvement across Digital Quality. Compliance, Risk and Governance Ensure the technical foundation and all solutions built on it are maintained in a validated and compliant state in accordance with GRC (Governance, Risk and Compliance) guidelines, computerised system validation expectations, data integrity, data privacy and cyber security requirements. Maintain audit and inspection readiness for engineering processes and evidence, support internal audits and regulatory inspections, and balance pace of innovation with regulatory compliance through effective governance and risk management. QUALIFICATIONS Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree required in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology or a related discipline. 10+ years of relevant experience in software or platform engineering, technical delivery leadership or engineering management (9+ years with an MS/MBA; 7+ years with a PhD), including accountability for engineering across a portfolio rather than a single application. Demonstrated experience leading, hiring and developing engineering teams at scale, including matrix leadership of vendor and contract resources across multiple geographies. Deep hands-on grounding in cloud platform engineering, integration architecture and modern software engineering practice, with practical experience of CI/CD, infrastructure as code, automated testing and security-in-the-pipeline. Experience delivering and operating across SaaS, COTS and custom-developed solutions, including vendor platform configuration, extension and upgrade management. Strong experience with Agile ways of working; SAFe preferred. Knowledge of financial management and procurement activities, with the ability to manage complex budgets, vendor contracts and internal-versus-partner capacity decisions. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence senior technical and non-technical stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications Experience in the pharmaceutical industry or another highly regulated manufacturing environment, including GxP computerised system validation, data integrity and inspection readiness Experience automating validation and compliance evidence within CI/CD pipelines in a regulated context. Working knowledge of quality, or EHS platforms and their integration landscape (for example Veeva, LIMS, Cority, Enablon). Experience engineering or operating AI and data capability in production, in partnership with architecture and data functions. Demonstrated success leading technology rationalisation, platform consolidation or large-scale migration programmes. Recognised cloud or architecture certification. PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS Typical desk job; no specific physical or mental requirements beyond standard office work. Metrics, Reporting, and Insights: Establish and review service metrics and reporting to inform decisions and drive continuous improvement. Influence and Innovation: Align internal and external stakeholders to a clear service direction and champion innovation through automation, AI adoption, and better ways of working. Governance and Compliance Alignment: Ensure platform services and engineering align with enterprise standards, security requirements, architectural principles, and operational controls. Essential Skills/Experience: Significant experience in DevOps engineering, enterprise platforms, or technical service delivery in a complex interpersonal environment. Proven people management experience, including leadership of technical teams, performance management, coaching, and capability development. Sophisticated technical expertise in enterprise engineering platforms and tooling, particularly Jira, Confluence, GitHub, GitHub Actions, SonarQube, and Artifactory, Microfocus ALM and Load Runner. Demonstrated experience in leading or coordinating the solving of complex technical and operational issues across platforms, services, and integrations. Strong experience in operational service leadership, including support models, prioritization, SLA delivery, incident management, and continuous improvement. Ability to solve difficult but defined problems that may span multiple areas, applying expert judgment to develop practical solutions. Exposure to Kubernetes, containers, or related modern engineering platforms. Experience with REST APIs, platform integrations, and interoperability. When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash ambitious thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world. The role will contribute to applied research and development of scalable AI capabilities spanning the full computer vision lifecycle—from data preparation and model development to deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement. The work will address practical challenges such as limited or imbalanced training data, rare events, changing image conditions, data drift, and model-performance degradation in operation. This role offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced AI research and real-world deployment, translating novel Generative AI and computer vision methods into reliable and scalable solutions across a range of industrial and business applications. Roles & Responsibilities : Generative AI and Synthetic Data: Research, design, and implement Generative AI approaches for creating realistic and diverse synthetic image datasets. Computer Vision Model Development: Develop and evaluate deep learning models for industrial image inspection tasks such as image classification, defect detection, anomaly detection, object detection, segmentation, and representation learning. Data-Efficient Learning: Investigate methods including transfer learning, self-supervised learning, few-shot learning, domain adaptation, active learning, and synthetic data augmentation to reduce annotation effort and improve model performance under limited-data conditions. Model Monitoring and Robustness: Develop methods for continuously monitoring deployed inspection models and image-data pipelines. This includes detecting data drift, changes in image conditions, model-performance degradation, confidence shifts, unusual defect patterns, and out-of-distribution inputs. Research and Experimentation: Formulate research hypotheses, design controlled experiments and ablation studies, establish appropriate evaluation benchmarks, and analyze results with scientific rigor. Compare state-of-the-art methods and identify approaches suitable for industrial deployment. Prototype and Product Integration: Build proof-of-concept solutions and research prototypes using Python and modern deep learning frameworks. Collaborate with software, cloud, MLOps, manufacturing, and domain teams to integrate validated methods into scalable AI platforms and applications. Document technical findings, communicate results to technical and business stakeholders, and contribute to publications, invention disclosures, patents, reusable frameworks, and Bosch’s intellectual-property portfolio. This role will focus on leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance network visibility, automate anomaly detection, and provide actionable insights for our customers. Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure product success and identify areas for improvement. AI and Machine Learning Integration: Drive the integration of AI and machine learning capabilities into our network observability platform. Work with marketing and sales teams to develop product messaging and go-to-market strategies. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, design, marketing, sales, and support, to ensure alignment and successful product delivery. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with large-scale data processing and analysis. Knowledge of cloud-native technologies and microservices architectures. Experience with Agile development methodologies. Experience in the networking industry. Benefits: Broadcom offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including health insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off. The primary objective of this role is to ensure the security, production readiness, maintainability, and compliance of functional, technical, and editor Docker images. The ideal candidate will be responsible for securing container images throughout their lifecycle, implementing automated security checks, identifying and remediating vulnerabilities, and integrating security practices into CI/CD pipelines. The candidate will work closely with development, infrastructure, platform, and security teams to ensure that container images meet organizational security standards and are reliable for production deployment. Build, harden, optimize, and maintain secure Docker images by following container security best practices. Implement and maintain security controls within CI/CD pipelines to automate image scanning and compliance checks. Establish and enforce Docker image standards, including the use of trusted base images, minimal image layers, non-root users, and secure configurations. Manage Docker image repositories and registries, including access controls, image tagging, versioning, and lifecycle management. Ensure compliance with organizational security policies, industry standards, and applicable regulatory requirements. Monitor security advisories and CVEs, and proactively update or rebuild affected images. Implement image signing, provenance verification, and software supply chain security controls where applicable. Collaborate with development, DevOps, infrastructure, and cybersecurity teams to resolve container security issues. Automate security checks, image validation, and remediation workflows using scripting and DevSecOps tools. Maintain technical documentation, security assessment reports, remediation records, and compliance evidence. Support production deployments, incident investigations, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement of container security practices. CI/CD Pipelines: Experience integrating security scanning and compliance gates into automated build and deployment pipelines. Container Registries: Familiarity with Docker Hub, Harbor, Amazon ECR, Azure Container Registry, or similar image repositories. Linux Administration: Strong understanding of Linux operating systems, package management, permissions, and system security. Scripting and Automation: Experience with Shell/Bash, Python, or similar scripting languages. Security Best Practices: Understanding of container security, access control, secure configuration, and software supply chain security. Troubleshooting: Strong analytical skills to investigate security findings, resolve image build issues, and support production readiness. Experience with image signing and verification tools such as Cosign and policy enforcement using admission controls. Familiarity with Software Bill of Materials (SBOM), SPDX, CycloneDX, and software supply chain security. Knowledge of DevSecOps frameworks and security standards such as CIS Docker Benchmarks, NIST guidance, and OWASP practices. In this senior, escalated technical role, you will act as the highest level of internal technical escalation for operating system incidents, complex systems engineering, system migrations, and operational resilience across mission critical enterprise IBM Z environments. The successful candidate will lead complex problem resolution, drive major operating system upgrades—including migrations from z/OS 3.1 to z/OS 3.2—oversee JES3 spool/batch subsystems, manage advanced MVS console alerting, and ensure robust disaster recovery and storage redundancy utilizing CSM (Copy Services Manager). This position works closely with architecture, storage, automation, and application infrastructure teams to guarantee non stop system availability, strict SLA compliance, and continuous modernization of the mainframe landscape. Key Responsibilities 1. Level 3 Incident Management & Advanced Triage . Serve as the final technical escalation point (L3) for complex, high impact system incidents, critical outages, and recurring system anomalies across production Sysplex environments. . Perform in depth root cause analysis (RCA) on system abends, wait states, hard/soft loops, and system crashes; analyze standalone dumps (SADUMP), IPCS dump captures, and SYSLOG / OPERLOG data. . Deliver rapid remediation during major system incidents, orchestrating complex emergency actions, IPL sequencing, and dynamic system reconfiguration. 2. Operating System Migrations & SMP/E Engineering . Plan, architect, and execute operating system release upgrades, specifically leading migration paths from z/OS 3.1 to z/OS 3.2. . Oversee SMP/E environments for installing, upgrading, and maintaining z/OS software products, PTFs, APARs, PUT buckets, and RSU maintenance levels. . Validate system compatibility, upgrade pre requisites, hardware co existence, fallback procedures, and validation test suites across all sandbox, QA, and production LPARs. . Maintain and customize critical system configurations: PARMLIB (IEASYSxx, LOADxx, LPALSTxx, LNKLSTxx), PROCLIB, and system symbolics. 3. MVS Console Operations, Alerts & Automation . Direct MVS console operations, console topology configuration, message routing, command security, and master console failover policies. . Monitor, triage, and configure critical system alert mechanisms, WTO/WTOR handling, console flood prevention, and system automation intercept routines. . Partner with automation engineers to develop and refine automated operator interventions, incident suppression rules, and auto ticketing triggers. 4. Job Entry Subsystem (JES3) Administration . Administer, tune, and maintain complex JES3 multi system complex (JES3plex) environments, including Global and Local processor setups. . Manage JES3 initialization streams, spool space allocations, spool offload/reload procedures, dynamic device reconfiguration, and job routing rules. . Provide deep diagnostic troubleshooting for JES3 spool stalls, communication timeouts, converter/interpreter errors, and complex batch queue blockages. 5. High Availability, Storage Redundancy & CSM . Administer and configure CSM (Copy Services Manager) to manage replication sessions (Metro Mirror, Global Mirror, and HyperSwap) for critical system redundancy and data resiliency. . Coordinate with Enterprise Storage teams on DASD/tape allocation, coupling facility structures, SMS constructs, and catalog recovery. . Ensure automated failover capabilities and continuous availability across multi site Parallel Sysplex environments. 6. Archiving & Output Management Tools . Oversee administration and L3 troubleshooting for enterprise report and log archiving tools, specifically CA View (Broadcom Output Management) and Flasher. . Manage archival database maintenance, index recoveries, automated purging cycles, bundle definitions, and report distribution stability. . Support end user and operations team inquiries related to archived Syslog retrieval, batch utility output retention, and compliance auditing. 7. Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity . Lead technical planning, script development, and technical execution for enterprise Mainframe Disaster Recovery (DR) and business continuity drills. . Validate disaster recovery readiness utilizing CSM failover scripts, alternative site IPLs, and catalog synchronization. . Maintain and update disaster recovery runbooks, recovery time objective (RTO) targets, and recovery point objective (RPO) guarantees. 8. Mentorship, Governance & Continuous Improvement . jobs.description: Meet the team: The AI Agent platform team builds the cloud platform for AI agents that hold natural voice and chat conversations and take actions in business systems through APIs. We build and run the real-time services underneath: low-latency streaming services that hold a live, two-way session with each user, stream audio and messages between services, and integrate with external systems, at enterprise scale across multiple regions. Confident, compelling communicator in both executive business settings and technical deep dives and comfortable representing Cloudflare publicly at industry events. Bonus: Familiarity with enterprise architecture frameworks (TOGAF), security standards (NIST SP 800-207, ISO 27001), and IT risk management principles relevant to regulated industries. Preferred Qualifications Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security, or related field. Experience in regulated industries (FSI, Government, Telco) or complex multi-cloud/hybrid environments. Prior experience in a role that required navigating cultural and linguistic diversity across multiple APAC markets. What Makes Cloudflare Special? Develop the leaders who report to you: coach managers on hiring, performance, feedback, and technical judgment, and build a succession bench so the organization is not dependent on any single person. Design the team topology — how AI product, platform, and applied research responsibilities are split so teams have clear, durable ownership and minimal hand-off friction. Create an environment where strong engineers do their best work: focused roadmaps, low process overhead, honest retrospectives, and visible career growth. Own the technical direction for Workforce AI in India Set and defend the AI architecture and technical strategy for the systems your teams own — model selection and hosting, retrieval and RAG design, vector and feature stores, agent orchestration, and inference patterns. Establish rigorous evaluation and quality practices for AI systems: offline and online eval harnesses, golden datasets, regression gates, human-in-the-loop review, and quality metrics tied to customer outcomes. Drive build-vs-buy decisions across foundation models, AWS-native AI services (Bedrock, SageMaker), and third-party tooling — with a clear-eyed view of cost, lock-in, latency, and differentiation. Own cloud and cost accountability for AI workloads on AWS: inference cost per request, GPU and token spend, caching and model-routing strategy, rightsizing, and FinOps discipline. Lead architecture and design reviews personally, and raise the standard for how the organization writes design documents, reasons about trade-offs, and validates assumptions before building. Keep the platform and product layers healthy together — shared services, SDKs, observability, and CI/CD that let AI product teams ship quickly and safely. Deliver AI products at scale Own end-to-end delivery for your teams’ commitments: multi-quarter roadmap, dependency management, realistic sequencing, and predictable shipping without heroics. Partner with Product Management, Design, Data, Security, and SRE to turn ambiguous problem statements into shipped, measurable AI capabilities. Move AI work from promising prototype to durable production system — reliability targets, monitoring, graceful degradation, rollback, and on-call ownership. Make disciplined trade-offs between customer-visible quality, delivery speed, and long-term platform investment, and explain those trade-offs credibly to executives. Partner globally with US teams Operate as a peer to AI Engineering, product, and architecture leaders in the US — jointly owning strategy rather than receiving it. Negotiate clear charter and ownership boundaries across sites so India-based teams own meaningful, end-to-end product surfaces and are accountable for outcomes. Maintain a workable overlap rhythm with counterparts in US Eastern and Pacific time zones, and design async-first practices — written proposals, decision records, recorded demos — so progress does not depend on meeting time. Represent India AI Engineering in global planning, architecture councils, and executive reviews, and bring back context that helps your teams make better local decisions. Build the talent brand and AI bench in Hyderabad Own the AI hiring mandate for Hyderabad: workforce planning, sourcing strategy, interview loop design, calibration, and closing senior candidates. Raise the technical interview bar for AI roles — practical system design, applied ML and LLM depth, evaluation thinking — and train interviewers to assess it consistently. Strengthen Cornerstone’s employer brand as an AI destination in Hyderabad through meetups, conference talks, technical blogs, open-source contributions, and university and intern programs. Build internal capability alongside external hiring: upskilling paths for engineers moving into AI work, mentorship structures, and a credible senior technical ladder in India. Responsible AI, trust, and compliance Own responsible AI practice for your organization — bias and fairness testing, explainability, human oversight, model and data documentation, and clear escalation paths. Ensure AI systems handling sensitive workforce and HR data meet privacy, residency, and security obligations (GDPR, India’s DPDP Act, customer contractual commitments, SOC 2 / ISO controls). Partner with Legal, Security, and Privacy on AI governance, vendor and model risk review, and customer-facing AI transparency commitments. Build guardrails into the engineering process rather than bolting them on: data-handling standards, prompt and output safety review, tenant isolation, and auditability by default. jobs.title: AI Performance Modeling Engineer
jobs.description: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. The Role We're building GPUs to run the most demanding AI in the world — Transformers, LLMs, and large vision models — and we need an experienced hands-on engineer who can tell us how fast those workloads will run before the silicon exists . This is an AI performance projection/modeling role: your job is to model AI workloads on our GPU architecture, predict their performance with confidence, and use those projections to shape the hardware we build. You'll work across the full modeling spectrum — analytical models for fast architectural what-ifs, and architectural and cycle-accurate simulators for precision — choosing the right level of fidelity for the question at hand. Because these workloads live on the GPU, you'll need real GPU architecture depth to do it. If you think in rooflines, arithmetic intensity, tensor/pipeline/data parallelism, and KV-cache bandwidth budgets — and you want your models to change the microarchitecture, not just describe it — this is the role. What You'll Do Project AI workload performance (your core mission) Build and use models — analytical, architectural, and cycle-accurate — to project the performance of generative AI and LLM workloads (attention, GEMMs, collectives, training and inference, vision models etc) on our GPU architecture. Choose the right fidelity for the question: analytical bounds and rooflines for rapid trade-off exploration, architectural and cycle-accurate simulation for precise answers. Find where performance will be won or lost — compute-engine occupancy, L1/L2 hierarchy, memory bandwidth, SoC fabric — and quantify the impact of each. Characterize workloads & shape the hardware Characterize AI workloads end to end — trace and profile execution, extract structural footprints, and translate them into microarchitectural bottlenecks and performance bounding boxes. Run architecture experiments to evaluate GPU configurations, scaling limits, and trade-offs against real AI workloads, backing every recommendation with sensitivity analysis and data. Extend and maintain the cycle-accurate / cycle-approximate simulators for the GPU subsystems AI workloads depend on — compute engines, cache hierarchies, memory subsystems, interconnects. Prove it on silicon (post-silicon) Run AI workloads on early silicon, capture telemetry, and correlate results back to your pre-silicon models to sharpen fidelity. Root-cause AI performance mismatches on physical silicon using low-level performance counters, register dumps, and Linux tracing. Collaborate across the stack Partner with compiler, runtime, and framework teams to turn model insights into optimizations, and to ground your projections in how workloads actually execute. Act as the bridge between architecture/RTL and software, translating AI workload requirements into concrete architectural constraints. What You'll Bring AI workload expertise: Deep, hands-on understanding of LLM and Transformer performance — scaling techniques, parallel training/inference strategies (tensor, pipeline, data parallelism), kernel execution graphs — and how they map to hardware. Performance modeling breadth: Hands-on experience with analytical performance models and execution-driven / architectural / cycle-accurate simulators, and sound judgment about which to reach for. Track record of turning models into decisions. GPU architecture depth: Strong command of GPU execution pipelines, SIMD/SIMT models, cache hierarchy, memory technologies, and high-bandwidth interconnects (PCIe, custom fabrics). The ML / Software Engineer – ChipStack SuperAgent Team will be responsible for designing, implementing, and evaluating AI agents that enhance productivity across the semiconductor design lifecycle. This engineer will contribute to the development of robust agent infrastructure, evaluation systems, and production-grade AI capabilities integrated within Cadence’s electronic design automation (EDA) ecosystem. The role focuses on building reliable, scalable agentic systems that operate within complex engineering workflows. The ideal candidate combines strong software engineering fundamentals with practical experience in ML systems and agent infrastructure, enabling deployment of high-impact AI solutions in production environments. Build robust evaluation frameworks to measure agent performance, reliability, and alignment with engineering workflows. Develop data pipelines, retrieval systems, and context-engineering strategies to support consistent and grounded agent behavior. Contribute to continuous integration, automated testing, and observability systems to ensure production-quality deployment of AI-enabled systems. Optimize system performance across latency, cost, reliability, and scalability dimensions. Required Qualifications Bachelors/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related technical field with 15+ Years of relevant experience in software development. Strong software engineering fundamentals, including design, refactoring, debugging, and testing of complex distributed systems. Demonstrated experience building production-quality systems. Understanding of large language models (LLMs) and practical considerations for deploying them in real-world systems (latency, cost, reliability, monitoring). Interest in semiconductor design, EDA workflows, and high-performance computing environments. You will be responsible for the full lifecycle: designing the agent and its guardrails, grounding it with retrieval, connecting it to enterprise systems through robust API and agent-to-agent (A2A) integrations, evaluating its behavior, and deploying and monitoring it in production by collaborating with extended team across various time zones. jobs.description: Meet the Team Join Cisco’s Commerce Operations Engineering Center (COEC) as an AI Engineer, where you will be part of a dynamic team driving innovation through AI-powered automation. Collaborate with multi-functional AI, engineering, and operations teams to transform sophisticated operational challenges into reliable, scalable AI solutions that advance Cisco’s AI-first future. Your Impact As an AI Engineer in COEC, you will design, build, and operate production-ready AI agents that power Cisco’s Commerce Operations. You will translate complex operational needs into automated workflows by orchestrating LLM reasoning, tool/function calling, retrieval, enterprise integrations, and agent-to-agent communication. You will be responsible for the full lifecycle of AI agent delivery—from solution design, guardrails, and system integration to evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement. Your work will help eliminate manual tasks, improve speed and accuracy, and drive operational excellence. What You’ll Do Design and build AI agents that automate manual and repetitive Commerce Operations tasks. Implement agent orchestration using frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, or equivalent. Build agent-to-agent integrations using emerging standards such as A2A and MCP to enable reliable coordination and delegation. Design secure API integrations with commerce platforms and enterprise data sources using REST, GraphQL, webhooks, event-driven services, authentication, rate limiting, and error handling. Build and optimize retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines using documents, structured data, and knowledge repositories. Implement guardrails, human approval gates, LLM routing, and failover mechanisms to ensure reliability, safety, and cost control. Apply prompt and context engineering to ensure AI agents deliver accurate, safe, and consistent outcomes. Build evaluation and observability capabilities, including offline test sets, online monitoring, tracing, audit logging, and quality regression detection. Own deployment and production operations, including CI/CD, progressive rollout, rollback, monitoring, model/version control, and cost tracking. Supervise AI solution performance and report business impact through critical metrics such as efficiency gains, cycle-time reduction, incident reduction, and operational accuracy. Continuously improve AI workflows, tools, and methodologies to increase reliability, scalability, and business value. Partner with Commerce Operations, application development, infrastructure, and business teams to integrate AI solutions into existing systems and workflows. Minimum Qualifications 7+ years of experience in software engineering or a related field within an enterprise environment. Shown experience building and deploying LLM-powered or agentic AI applications in production. Strong Python skills and tactical experience with LLM/agent frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenAI SDK, Anthropic SDK, or equivalents. Practical expertise in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt engineering, tool/function calling, agent orchestration, and multi-agent communication or workflow orchestration. Experience with API and system integrations, including REST, GraphQL, event-driven services, authentication, and enterprise data sources. Demonstrated ability to lead technical delivery and collaborate effectively with multi-functional business and engineering teams. Familiarity with AI governance and safety practices, including RBAC, audit logging, PII handling, and controls for high-risk automated actions. jobs.title: AI Principal Architect
jobs.description: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Title and Summary AI Principal Architect Mastercard's Business & Market Insights (B&MI) group empowers organizations to achieve growth and innovation goals by delivering unparalleled data-driven intelligence and cutting-edge AI solutions. By harnessing proprietary data, frontier generative AI, and global expertise, B&MI helps businesses make smarter, faster, and more impactful decisions. We transform complex, multi-modal data into agentic systems and generative applications that drive measurable business outcomes and sustained competitive advantage. We're looking for a Principal Architect, Generative AI & ML Engineering, for the Operational Intelligence Program within B&MI. As a principal-level technical leader, you'll define the architecture vision and technical strategy for our agentic AI platform. On this platform, agents make extensive tool calls into enterprise services and APIs and must run securely, reliably, and at scale. You'll set the standards teams build on across tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, self-correcting agents, memory, retrieval, and LLMOps. You'll also make the key decisions on models, platforms, and trade-offs. Working closely with engineering, product, security, and business leaders, you'll shape the long-term direction of Gen AI across B&MI and mentor architects and senior engineers. You'll also stay hands-on with prototypes that de-risk big bets. The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale. If you've solved them as a backend or distributed systems architect and have started applying that experience to LLM systems, we'd love to hear from you. Roles & Responsibilities • Own the architecture and technical roadmap for the Operational Intelligence Gen AI platform, defining reference architectures and standards that teams across the program can reuse and scale. • Architect the enterprise tool-calling layer, setting standards for how internal services, data platforms, and external APIs are exposed to agents as tools. This covers schemas, contracts, versioning, access control, and resilient execution (parallel and chained calls, retries, timeouts, idempotency, circuit breakers, and fallbacks). • Set the architecture for multi-agent and skills-based agent systems (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen), including when to use agents versus deterministic workflows and how agents coordinate, delegate, and share context. • Design self-correcting agent patterns: tool critics and verifiers that check tool selection, arguments, and results, plus reflection and plan-and-execute loops that catch errors before agents act or respond. • Architect agent memory and state for long-running, multi-step sessions, including short- and long-term memory (e.g., Mem0, Zep, LangGraph memory), session persistence, and memory scoping and retention. • Define retrieval architecture for grounded reasoning, including Self-RAG, Corrective RAG (CRAG), adaptive retrieval, and Graph-RAG, built on vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, pgvector, OpenSearch) and knowledge graphs (e.g., Neo4j, AWS Neptune). • Design the inference and orchestration layer for high throughput, covering async processing, streaming, caching, rate limiting, and model routing across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and open-source models. • Establish the LLMOps architecture on Databricks (AWS), including MLflow, CI/CD for prompts and agents, and model lineage. Set platform-wide evaluation and observability standards: end-to-end tracing of tool calls, tool-selection accuracy, task success rates, cost, and latency. • Build security and Responsible AI into the architecture, including guardrails, prompt-injection defenses, hallucination mitigation, data privacy, and audit trails that meet Mastercard's data ethics and regulatory standards. • Own key architecture decisions and trade-offs, such as build versus buy, model and vendor selection, and cost versus latency versus accuracy, documented through architecture decision records. Assess emerging models, frameworks, and standards such as MCP for production readiness. • Lead design reviews and partner with engineering, product, security, and data teams to align on architecture and raise the engineering bar across the program. • Stay hands-on, building prototypes and reference implementations that de-risk decisions and give teams a working starting point. All About You • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, AI/ML, or Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. • Significant experience architecting large-scale distributed systems in production, including microservices, event-driven systems, data platforms, and cloud-native infrastructure. • Deep expertise in API design and systems integration, including contracts, security models, and reliability patterns for services consumed by many teams. You understand what changes when the consumer is an LLM. • Hands-on experience designing and shipping LLM-powered systems in production, especially agents that use tool/function calling, memory, and retrieval, and a clear view of how they fail. • Strong Python skills for hands-on prototyping (async programming, FastAPI or similar), plus SQL proficiency. • Deep experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS preferred; Azure or GCP welcome), including its AI services such as Bedrock, SageMaker, Azure OpenAI, or Vertex AI. • A solid grounding in security, privacy, and compliance for enterprise systems, ideally in financial services or another regulated industry. • The ability to influence without authority, aligning engineering, product, and leadership around a technical direction and explaining trade-offs in business terms. • Nice to have: hands-on experience with tool critics, Self-RAG, CRAG, reflection loops, memory frameworks such as Mem0 or Zep, MCP tool servers, or agent evaluation frameworks. • Nice to have: exposure to fine-tuning (LoRA, PEFT, RLHF), multimodal models, or knowledge graphs. • Coming from backend or distributed systems architecture? The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale, and you've solved them before. If you've started applying that experience to LLM systems, we want to hear from you, even if you haven't used every tool listed here. Corporate Security Responsibility All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must: Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices; Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed; Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer I
jobs.description: Job Description Are you a hands-on engineer who wants to build AI agents that do real work? Not demos, but agents that provision infrastructure, investigate incidents, answer the questions engineers would otherwise file a ticket for, and take action safely on production systems? Our technology organization runs the cloud, compute, and network platforms that thousands of engineers across Thomson Reuters build on, spanning AWS, Azure, and our own data centers. We are rethinking how that platform is built and operated, with AI agents and automation taking on work that used to require tickets, runbooks, and manual toil. We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help lead that work. We are a software engineering team within Thomson Reuters’ technology organization. We design and build AI agents, agent tooling, and infrastructure automation that change how technology teams across the company work. We also own and evolve internal platform and developer tools used by engineers across the company. We place a high degree of trust in our engineers and expect them to deliver. We move quickly, ship to production, and learn from what our users actually do. In return, you will have interesting problems, the resources to solve them, and real room to shape how a large enterprise adopts AI. Key Responsibilities We build for production, so a prototype is a starting point, not a deliverable. We eliminate toil by design, asking whether software, automation, or an agent should handle repetitive work. We use AI in our own development workflow and apply engineering judgment to everything it produces. We reuse before we build, and we value aptitude and judgment over experience with any specific toolset. Design and build AI agents that reason over context, call tools, and take action on real systems, from single-purpose assistants to multi-step workflows with human approval where it matters. Build the APIs, MCP servers, and integrations that give agents safe, well-scoped access to cloud providers, source control, service management, observability, and internal platforms. Build infrastructure-as-code, pipelines, and self-service capabilities that let engineers get what they need without waiting on a person. Own production-grade concerns for agents, including evaluation and regression testing, observability, cost and latency management, guardrails, least-privilege access, defenses against prompt injection, and auditability. Lead technically by owning the design of major systems, writing clear design documents, leading design and code reviews, establishing reusable patterns and standards, and mentoring engineers across the team. Apply judgment about when AI fits, recognizing when a deterministic script, a better API, or a process change is the right answer and making that case clearly. Partner with platform, cloud, security, and SRE teams, and with the stakeholders whose work is being automated, to turn ambiguous problems into well-defined solutions. Required Qualifications 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including designing, building, and operating production systems. Strong proficiency in at least one modern programming language. Python is the primary language and experience with it is a plus, but strong engineers from Go, TypeScript, C#, Java, or similar backgrounds who are ready to work in Python are welcome. Hands-on experience building applications or agents on large language models, including tool and function calling, context management, retrieval (RAG), and structured outputs, with a practical understanding of failure modes such as hallucination, non-determinism, and prompt injection. Experience with AWS and/or Azure and with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, AWS CDK, CloudFormation, or Bicep. Experience with modern delivery practices, including Git-based workflows, CI/CD (e.g., GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines), automated testing, and containers. A secure-by-design mindset, especially when giving software the ability to act on production systems. Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to write a strong design document and explain complex trade-offs to technical and non-technical audiences. A track record of technical leadership, including mentoring engineers, leading through influence, and raising the quality of a team’s work. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Preferred Qualifications Experience with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or agent frameworks and SDKs such as LangGraph, the Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework, or Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Understanding of what these frameworks abstract is valued more than experience with any one of them. Experience designing evaluation suites for LLM systems, or with LLM observability tooling (e.g., OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, LangSmith). Experience with Kubernetes, serverless architectures, or event-driven systems. Background in platform engineering, SRE, or DevOps, including on-call and incident response. Familiarity with networking fundamentals (DNS, firewalls, cloud networking) or IT service management platforms such as ServiceNow. Experience working in large, regulated, or compliance-conscious enterprise environments. #LI-VGA1 What’s in it For You? Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected. Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance. jobs.description: : ZS is a place where passion changes lives. Bring your curiosity for learning, bold ideas, courage and passion to drive life-changing impact to ZS. : Lead – Governance, Risk & Compliance ZS is looking for a skilled and driven Lead– Governance, Risk & Compliance to join its Governance, Risk, and Compliance team. The consultant will serve as a hands-on Technology Risk Assessment subject-matter expert for applications, products, platforms, AI solutions, tools, cloud services, third-party technologies, and emerging technologies. Independently lead and deliver Application Security Governance, AI Risk Assessment, project-risk and material-change assessments for internal, client-facing, cloud-hosted, client-hosted, third-party and AI-enabled solutions. Determine assessment scope and applicable control requirements based on business criticality, data classification, external exposure, hosting model, technology stack, user population, regulatory and contractual obligations, AI usage, third-party dependencies and change magnitude. Develop a detailed understanding of product functionality, user journeys, architecture, data flows, trust boundaries, integrations, deployment models, administrative access and operational dependencies to identify credible risk scenarios. Assess solutions across ideation, architecture, design, development, testing, release, production operations, material change, migration and decommissioning. Participate in architecture reviews, design governance, stage gates, release-readiness reviews and production-readiness reviews, and provide documented risk recommendations. Evaluate inherent risk, control design and operating effectiveness, residual risk, compensating controls, remediation plans, exceptions and closure evidence using the approved risk methodology. Conduct review sessions with product owners, architects, engineers, developers, data scientists, security, privacy, legal, compliance, procurement and operations teams. Produce clear and defensible assessment reports documenting scope, assumptions, system context, evidence reviewed, risk scenarios, findings, ratings, residual risk, actions, dependencies and approval recommendations. Oversee high and critical remediation items, including accountable owners, target dates, interim safeguards, escalation, risk acceptance and closure validation. Support material incidents and risk escalations, identify root causes and recurring control weaknesses, and recommend program-level improvements. Develop management reporting covering assessment coverage, material findings, overdue actions, exceptions, recurring issues, trends and remediation performance. Contribute to policies, standards, procedures, control libraries, evidence standards, assessment playbooks, training, automation and continuous improvement. Secure SDLC and DevSecOps, including architecture review, threat modelling, SAST, DAST, API testing, software composition analysis, secrets management, penetration testing, CI/CD security, infrastructure as code and remediation validation. Modern architectures, including microservices, APIs, event-driven systems, containers, Kubernetes, serverless computing, SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, mobile, data and analytics platforms and low-code/no-code solutions. Identity and access management, encryption and key management, logging and monitoring, vulnerability management, environment segregation, third-party integrations, incident response, availability, backup, recovery, resilience and secure decommissioning. Technical evidence, including architecture and data-flow diagrams, API specifications, threat models, cloud configurations, pipelines, test reports, vulnerability reports, deployment workflows, operating records and control demonstrations. Assess AI and machine-learning solutions across data sourcing, model selection, training or fine-tuning, validation, hosting, access, integrations, third-party dependencies, deployment, monitoring, human oversight, suspension and retirement. Evaluate generative AI, foundation and open-source models, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, copilots, AI APIs, vector databases, plugins, tools and Model Context Protocol integrations. Assess risks including prompt injection, jailbreaks, insecure output handling, sensitive-data disclosure, model or data poisoning, hallucination, bias, toxicity, privacy leakage, excessive agency, weak tool permissions, supply-chain exposure, model theft and unsafe actions. Review data provenance, lawful use, consent, quality, representativeness, lineage, retention, intellectual property, training and inference-data protection, residency and cross-border requirements. Evaluate accuracy, robustness, explainability, benchmark selection, performance thresholds, validation independence, human approval, action limits, memory, identity propagation, kill switches, rollback and fail-safe behaviour. Define or review monitoring for model and data drift, anomalous behaviour, harmful outputs, performance degradation, incidents, complaints and regulatory or use-case changes. ISO/IEC 27001 and 27005, ISO 31000, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST SP 800-53/30, NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SP 800-218), SOC 2, CIS Controls and Cloud Security Alliance guidance, including the Cloud Controls Matrix. OWASP Top 10, Application Security Verification Standard, API Security Top 10, Software Assurance Maturity Model, OWASP guidance for LLM applications. NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894, AIUC‑1, responsible AI principles and applicable AI regulatory expectations, including the EU AI Act where relevant. What You'll Bring: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Information Systems or a related discipline. Demonstrated track record of leading and executing technical security audits — hands-on experience conducting walkthroughs, reviewing evidence, and making independent control assessments Strong technical foundation across SDLC governance, CI/CD pipeline security, cloud security controls, access and identity management, application security, and secrets management Demonstrated experience independently scoping, conducting, documenting and concluding complex application or technology risk assessments. Experience reviewing the work of other assessors and challenging scope, evidence, control conclusions, findings, ratings, remediation and closure decisions. Ability to distinguish control design effectiveness from operating effectiveness and determine whether evidence is complete, current, relevant, reliable and sufficient. Strong analytical, facilitation, stakeholder-management, technical-writing and executive-communication skills, with the ability to exercise independent judgement and manage concurrent priorities. Mandatory certifications — CEH, ISO 27001 Lead auditor, ISO/IEC 42001 Lead Auditor. Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform activates enterprise intelligence by unifying data, knowledge and business context to achieve tangible outcomes. Teradata delivers real business value with AI.
